requirements.body:
The SMT pipeline ([VER-001]) reaches the solver through one transport in every implementation:
each query is one `z3` process. The process is started with the argument list

```
z3 -smt2 -in -t:<timeout_ms> -T:<ceil((timeout_ms + 1000) / 1000)>
```

plus `fp.engine=spacer` for the HORN query, is fed the complete SMT-LIB2 script on stdin in a
single write, and then has its stdin closed so it sees end-of-file. Both output streams are
drained concurrently from the start, so a reply larger than a pipe buffer cannot stall the
solver, and a wall-clock watchdog at `timeout_ms + 2000` milliseconds kills a process that
ignored both timeouts. The process is killed and reaped on every exit path. No solver state
survives a query: concurrent verifications in one host process are independent, and a solver
crash is a verdict, never a crashed host. The timeout is per invocation; the HORN query, the
certificate script and its detail re-run each receive the full budget. The formula is fixed for a
`timeout_ms` of at least 1. A timeout of 0 is outside it: Java and TypeScript raise it to 1 ms, so
that `-t:0`, which `z3` reads as no limit, never reaches the solver, and Rust passes `-t:0`.

**Total budget.** Because the timeout is per invocation, one `verify()` can run for several times
it: the bound query ([VER-015]), the state-equation phase shared across its refinements
([VER-018]) and its certificate check and detail re-run, the firing-bound phase at half the
timeout ([VER-019]), the bounded witness phase at an eighth of it ([VER-025]), the HORN query and
its certificate check and detail re-run add up to about 7.6 timeouts, plus 2 s of watchdog slack per process, plus the solver-free work (the enumeration
route [VER-017], Route B [VER-012], the timed check [VER-023], the siphon and trap search
[VER-020], Farkas, the colour-slot simplex of [NU-053]), which no timeout bounds. An
implementation SHOULD therefore offer an
optional **total budget**, a wall-clock limit on the whole call. It is off by default, and with
it unset behaviour and reports are byte-identical to the above. When it is set:

- The deadline starts when `verify()` is entered, before the terminal rewrite of [EXEC-042], so
  all of the call's work counts against it.
- Every `z3` process receives `min(its normal budget, remaining)` as its `timeout_ms`, and derives
  `-t`, `-T` and the watchdog from that clamped value by the formulas above. When nothing
  remains, no process is started.
- The solver-free graph builds (the enumeration route, Route B, the timed check) and the long
  solver-free loops (siphon and trap search, Farkas, the colour-slot simplex, the trim of the
  bounded witness phase [VER-025]) poll the deadline,
  cheaply (every so many classes or iterations), and stop when it has passed. The colour-slot
  simplex runs as its own step, `colour-slot bound`, entered once every other check of the
  coloured plan has passed, and polls before every pivot.
- When the deadline passes before a verdict is reached, the verdict is `Unknown` with the reason
  `total verification budget of <N> ms exhausted during <phase>`, `<phase>` naming the step
  that was running when the budget ran out, and the report carries the same line. A poll made
  on entering a step checks the deadline **before** it records the new step, so an exhaustion
  found there blames the step that just ended, not the one about to start; every implementation
  names the same step for the same stop. A verdict reached before the deadline stands.
- A graph build the deadline stopped is not a class-budget truncation. It MUST NOT be recorded in
  a state-space cache ([VER-017]) as a truncation at the class budget: it leaves the cache entry
  as it found it, like a build that fails.
- The HORN query no longer keeps its full budget. Without a total budget, the fixpoint query gets
  the whole timeout however long the pre-fixpoint phases of [VER-018], [VER-019] and [VER-025]
  took; under a total budget it gets what they left.

The per-call timeout keeps its meaning above: the budget of one process. The total budget
applies to one `verify()` call. `SubnetDef.verify` ([MOD-051]) and open-net verification
([VER-022]) reach it only through their per-query configuration hooks, so each of their queries
gets its own budget; neither has a budget across its queries.

**Cancellation.** An implementation SHOULD let the caller stop a running `verify()` from outside
it. Cancellation is not a second mechanism: it shares the total budget's stop. The deadline
becomes "deadline passed **or** cancelled", and everything that polls the deadline (the clamp
before each `z3` process, the graph builds, the long solver-free loops) sees cancellation at the
same points, whether or not a total budget is set. Beyond that:

- A `z3` process running when cancellation arrives is killed at once and reaped, not left to its
  timeout or watchdog. A cancelled call starts no further process.
- The verdict is `Unknown` with the reason `verification cancelled during <phase>`, `<phase>` named
  as for the total budget, and the report carries the same line. There is no new verdict. A call
  cancelled before it starts returns this at once. A verdict reached before cancellation stands.
- When a total budget is also set, whichever stop comes first names the reason.
- A graph build stopped by cancellation is not a class-budget truncation and leaves a state-space
  cache as it found it, as for the total budget.
- `SubnetDef.verify` ([MOD-051]) and open-net verification ([VER-022]) honour cancellation too,
  including the solver queries open-net verification runs outside `verify()` (its termination
  ranking): a cancelled call starts no further query.

The mechanism follows each language's idiom:

- **TypeScript**: an `AbortSignal`, passed with `SmtVerifier.signal(signal)` (also reachable from
  the `configure` hook of `SubnetDef.verify` and from `OpenNetOptions`). `runZ3Text` takes the signal
  and kills the process with `SIGKILL` when it aborts.
- **Rust**: `CancelToken` (`Clone`, `Send + Sync`, a shared atomic flag; `new()`, `cancel()`,
  `is_cancelled()`), passed with `SmtVerifier::cancel_token(&CancelToken)`. The watchdog's poll
  loop in `Z3Solver::run` checks it and kills and reaps the process.
- **Python**: `libpetri.CancelToken` wraps the Rust token; `verify(..., cancel=token)` and
  `verify_subnet(..., cancel=token)`. The verification runs with the GIL released, so `cancel()`
  from another thread, or from an asyncio task while the call runs in an executor, takes effect.
- **Java**: thread interruption, Java's own cancellation idiom; there is no token. Interrupting the
  thread that runs `verify()` cancels it: the running `z3` process is destroyed, the remaining
  phases are skipped, and the result is the `Unknown` above. The graph builds and loops read the
  thread's interrupt status at their deadline polls without clearing it, and the interrupt flag is
  set again when `verify()` returns, so the caller still sees it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

   scripts in every implementation (the golden scripts under

requirements.title: Conditional Sink Places (Designed Terminals)
requirements.testDerivation: a fork whose one arm may halt while the other's token is still in flight, with the halt marker inhibiting the second arm: `deadlockFree` with the halt as a plain sink is violated (the in-flight token is stranded); with the in-flight place declared under the halt marker it is proven; with the marker alone it stays violated; `terminatesAtSink` with the same declarations is violated. A chain whose marker is consumed before quiescence (AC2), and the same net with the resting place as its own marker (AC3).

spans.text: A token in place `p` of a quiescent marking `M` is **stranded** iff `p` is not a declared sink, `p` is not a marker, and no conditional set naming `p` has its marker marked in `M`.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: Repeated declarations for one marker accumulate; declarations for different markers are independent, so a place excused by two markers is stranded only when both are unmarked.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: `TerminatesAtSink` is unaffected and reads the unconditional sinks only.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: The verifier *shall* read a token in place `p` of a marking `M` as stranded exactly when `p` is not a declared sink, `p` is not the marker of any conditional declaration, and every conditional declaration that names `p` has its marker unmarked in `M`.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *When* the verifier decides `DeadlockFree`, it *shall* report a quiescent marking as a violation exactly when some marked place of it is stranded.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: *When* the verifier decides `TerminatesAtSink`, it *shall* report a quiescent marking as a violation exactly when it would without any conditional declaration.
spans.label: s6

paragraphs.text: `DeadlockFree` ([VER-002]) reads a quiescent marking against the places where a token may rest. Besides the unconditional **sink places**, the verifier accepts **conditional sink places**: a set of places where a token may rest **while a marker place holds a token**, declared as `sinkPlacesWhen(marker, places…)`. A marked marker is a *designed terminal* — a halted or paused run, a cancelled batch — under which the work it interrupted legitimately stays where it was delivered. The marker itself is at rest whenever it is marked, so `sinkPlacesWhen(marker)` with no further places excuses exactly the marker.

Declarations union. A token in place `p` of a quiescent marking `M` is **stranded** iff `p` is not a declared sink, `p` is not a marker, and no conditional set naming `p` has its marker marked in `M`. The `DeadlockFree` error condition becomes: (all transitions disabled) ∧ (some marked place is stranded). Repeated declarations for one marker accumulate; declarations for different markers are independent, so a place excused by two markers is stranded only when both are unmarked. `TerminatesAtSink` is unaffected and reads the unconditional sinks only. An unresolved marker or place contributes nothing, as an unresolved sink does: a mistyped marker makes the property stricter, never laxer.

requirements.body:
`DeadlockFree` ([VER-002]) reads a quiescent marking against the places where a token may
rest. Besides the unconditional **sink places**, the verifier accepts **conditional sink
places**: a set of places where a token may rest **while a marker place holds a token**,
declared as `sinkPlacesWhen(marker, places…)`. A marked marker is a *designed terminal* — a
halted or paused run, a cancelled batch — under which the work it interrupted legitimately
stays where it was delivered. The marker itself is at rest whenever it is marked, so
`sinkPlacesWhen(marker)` with no further places excuses exactly the marker.

Declarations union. A token in place `p` of a quiescent marking `M` is **stranded** iff `p`
is not a declared sink, `p` is not a marker, and no conditional set naming `p` has its
marker marked in `M`. The `DeadlockFree` error condition becomes: (all transitions disabled)
∧ (some marked place is stranded). Repeated declarations for one marker accumulate;
declarations for different markers are independent, so a place excused by two markers is
stranded only when both are unmarked. `TerminatesAtSink` is unaffected and reads the
unconditional sinks only. An unresolved marker or place contributes nothing, as an
unresolved sink does: a mistyped marker makes the property stricter, never laxer.

The verifier *shall* read a token in place `p` of a marking `M` as stranded exactly when `p` is not a declared sink, `p` is not the marker of any conditional declaration, and every conditional declaration that names `p` has its marker unmarked in `M`.

*When* the verifier decides `DeadlockFree`, it *shall* report a quiescent marking as a violation exactly when some marked place of it is stranded.

*When* the verifier decides `TerminatesAtSink`, it *shall* report a quiescent marking as a violation exactly when it would without any conditional declaration.

**Encoding.** In the flat and name-coloured CHC encodings the stranded disjunction of
[VER-002] gains, for each place `p` excused by markers `k₁ < … < kₙ` (flat indices), the
disjunct `(and (>= m_p 1) (= m_k₁ 0) … (= m_kₙ 0))` in place of `(>= m_p 1)`; declared sinks
and markers contribute no disjunct. Scripts without a conditional declaration are
byte-identical to those of [VER-002]. The report renders the declarations after the property
as `(sinks: a, b; when h: c, d; when p)`, in declaration order.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A quiescent marking that marks a marker and holds tokens only in declared sinks, in the
   marker, and in that marker's conditional places is not a `DeadlockFree` violation.
2. A quiescent marking that holds a token in a conditional place whose marker is **unmarked**
   is a violation, exactly as without the declaration.
3. The marker needs no self-listing: `sinkPlacesWhen(p)` excuses a quiescent marking holding
   only `p`.
4. `TerminatesAtSink` ignores conditional declarations: a quiescent marking that marks a
   marker but no declared sink violates it.
5. Every route that decides `DeadlockFree` reads the same rest set, among them the flat
   encoder, the name-coloured encoder, the certificate check's safety condition, the abstract
   counterexample replay, the ν name-partition graph ([VER-012]), the enumeration route
   ([VER-017]), the state-equation phase ([VER-018]) and open-net verification ([VER-022]); the
   four implementations emit byte-identical scripts for the same declarations ([VER-013] AC1).

**Net-declared terminals.** A terminal place declared on the net ([EXEC-042]) is a designed
terminal that the caller does not restate. Every route verifies the net with `P` inhibiting each
transition, `P` added to the sinks, and `sinkPlacesWhen(P, all places)` added to the conditional
declarations. The open-net route ([VER-022]) merges it as a designed terminal. These additions
apply to the net's own terminals only. A net without them keeps its scripts byte-identical.

- TypeScript: `SmtVerifier.sinkPlacesWhen(marker, ...places)`; `verification/rest-set`

- Rust: `SmtVerifier::sink_places_when(marker, places)`.
- Python: `verify(..., sink_places_when={marker: [places…]})`.
- Fixtures: `sinkPlacesWhen` in `spec/verification-fixtures/fixtures.json`
  (`sink-partial-terminal-conditional-proven`, `dead-end-chain-marker-proven`,
  `dead-end-chain-unmarked-marker-violated`, `nu-mixed-terminal-route-b-conditional-proven`).

**Depends on:** [VER-002], [VER-012], [VER-013]

**Test derivation:** a fork whose one arm may halt while the other's token is still in
flight, with the halt marker inhibiting the second arm: `deadlockFree` with the halt as a
plain sink is violated (the in-flight token is stranded); with the in-flight place declared

paragraphs.text: Before the fixpoint query, a **reachability-safety** property (`PlaceBound`, `BranchPlaceBound`, `MutualExclusion`, `Unreachable`) is tried against the **state equation**: every abstract-reachable marking satisfies `M = M0 + C·σ` for some firing count vector `σ ≥ 0`, so for any weighting `y ≥ 0` with `y·C ≤ 0` on every transition, `y·M ≤ y·M0` on every reachable marking — a *decreasing* conservation law, where the P-invariants of [VER-005] are the equalities. The violation of such a property is a lower demand `d` on some places (`m_p ≥ 1` for each place of an `Unreachable` or a two-place `MutualExclusion`, `m_p ≥ k+1` for a bound `k`); if `y·d > y·M0` for some such `y`, no reachable marking meets the demand and the property is **proven structurally**, without IC3. A pairwise `MutualExclusion` over three or more places ([VER-002]) is a disjunction of demands, one per pair: it is proven when every pair's demand is separated, each pair with its own query.

The weighting for each demand is found by one `QF_LIA` query through the solver transport of [VER-013] (phase `bound`): variables `y_p ≥ 0` per flat place, `y_p = 0` on every consume-all / reset place (H1) and every injected environment place (H3'), one row `Σ_p C[p][t]·y_p ≤ 0` per flat transition, and `Σ_p d_p·y_p ≥ 1 + Σ_p M0_p·y_p`. A `sat` model is **re-checked in exact integer arithmetic** (`y ≥ 0`, the zero weights, every row, the demand) before it is believed; a model that fails the check is discarded. `unsat`, `unknown` and any transport failure hand over to the next phase of the dispatch. The phase is skipped under `Ignore` with environment places registered ([VER-006] AC4) and for the quiescence properties, whose violation is not a linear demand. A ν-net's verdict receives the [NU-050] over-approximation note like any other flat proof.

The verifier *shall* accept a weighting `y` for a demand `d` in the exact re-check only when `y_p ≥ 0` on every flat place, `y_p = 0` on every consume-all, reset and injected environment place, `Σ_p C[p][t]·y_p ≤ 0` for every flat transition `t`, and `Σ_p d_p·y_p ≥ 1 + Σ_p M0_p·y_p`, and *shall* accept every weighting that meets these conditions when every weight, and the sum of the absolute values of the terms of each of these sums, is at most `2^127 − 2`. A weighting whose sums overflow the implementation's integer arithmetic is rejected; that costs a proof and never makes one. In the re-check, `C[p][t]` is the number of tokens the flat transition `t` deposits on `p` minus the number its input on `p` requires, which for a consume-all input (`all`, `atLeast`) is its required minimum.

The verifier *shall* take as the demands of a property one demand `m_p ≥ 1` on every listed place for `Unreachable`, one demand `m ≥ 1` on the entries at positions `i` and `j` for every pair of positions `i < j` of a `MutualExclusion` of two or more entries, in lexicographic order of `(i, j)`, and one demand `m_q ≥ k + 1` on the bounded place `q` for `PlaceBound` and `BranchPlaceBound` with bound `k`. A `MutualExclusion` of fewer than two entries is never violated ([VER-002]), so its demands are left to the implementation and every choice is sound.

*When* the verifier runs the bound phase on a property, it *shall* return `Proven` exactly when, for every demand of the property, the query returned a `sat` model whose weighting the exact re-check accepts for that demand.
The verifier *shall not* return `Violated` from the bound phase; every outcome of the phase other than `Proven` hands over to the next phase of the dispatch.
*When* the bound phase proves the property, it *shall* return `Proven` with method `structural`, an empty counterexample trace and no `counterexampleConfirmed`.

A property with a demand is a `PlaceBound`, `BranchPlaceBound`, `MutualExclusion` or `Unreachable` property; the name-alignment properties of [NU-055] have no demand. The verifier *shall not* run the bound phase on a property without a demand, while the phase is disabled, or under `Ignore` with environment places registered. The verifier *shall* run the bound phase at most once in one verification call. The verifier *shall* send the `bound` query of each demand at most once in one verification call. The verifier *shall not* run Route B ([VER-012]) after the bound phase, and *shall not* run the bound phase after the colour-slot bound of the coloured encoding ([NU-053]) or after the fixpoint query. *When* the bound phase is enabled and the verifier runs the colour-slot bound or the fixpoint query on a property with a demand, not under `Ignore` with environment places registered, it *shall* have run the bound phase earlier in the same call. *When* the bound phase is enabled and the verifier runs the enumeration of [VER-017] on a property with a demand, and the enumeration route applies to a net with no drained forward, it *shall* have run the bound phase earlier in the same call, and *shall not* run the bound phase after the enumeration. *When* the bound phase runs ahead of the enumeration and does not prove the property, the next phase the verifier runs *shall* be the enumeration. On a net where the enumeration route does not apply, or that has a drained forward, the verifier *shall not* run the bound phase before the enumeration.

This closes the class of proofs IC3 does not find on pipeline-shaped nets: an *ordering* argument — "both join slots armed means every upstream stage has run, so no halt is still possible" — is a weighted count bound, which Spacer's lemma generalisation does not invent over fifty variables but a linear solver finds in milliseconds. A net that answered `unknown` after 300 s answers `proven` in under a second.

**On ν-nets the phase also runs before the name-coloured encoding ([NU-053]).** The state equation is written over the flat, name-blind net, whose firing rule ignores which name a token carries; every marking the ν semantics reaches is reachable there too, so a weighting that separates the violation on the flat net separates it on the ν-net, and a structural `Proven` is sound. A net with an exact coloured plan therefore tries the bound first, under the same conditions as the flat path (enabled, a reachability-safety property, not `Ignore` with environment places, the total budget and cancellation of [VER-013] respected), with the same phase name. `Proven` returns as on the flat path — method `structural`, the lines of AC1 — and keeps any ν-encoding notes already in the report; anything else hands over to the coloured query, whose verdict and notes are unchanged. The coloured plan is built only after the bound fails to prove; nothing before it reads the plan. Route B ([VER-012]) keeps its place in the dispatch: the bound runs after it, never before. The colour-slot bound of the coloured encoding counts coloured tokens rather than names, often two to four times the declared budget, and IC3 over that many colour slots can time out on a bound the flat state equation proves in milliseconds. On six PNID ν-nets (`research/net-metrics/validation/pnid/`), `placeBound(X, 1000)` under a budget of 2 went from `Unknown` after about 8 s to `Proven` in about 12 ms.

**On nets the enumeration route takes, the phase runs before it.** When the enumeration route of [VER-017] applies to a net with no ν-join (untimed, no environment places, a positive class budget) and the net has no drained forward ([IO-014], [VER-001] AC5), the bound runs **before** the enumeration, not after it. One query costs milliseconds; a graph that does not close costs the whole class budget before the bound is reached. Measured on a 134-transition composed agent net whose graph exceeds the budget: about 17 s per `placeBound` claim at a budget of 200 000 classes, several minutes at 5 000 000, and under 0.1 s with the bound first. A bound that proves returns as in AC1, with the report line of [VER-017] AC3 for the invariants it did not compute. Anything else falls through to the enumeration, and the fixpoint query later does not send the `bound` query again. When the solver cannot be started, the early bound sends no query and hands over with a report line, and the enumeration runs without a solver, as it did before; the `Unknown` with route `Unavailable` of [VER-013] comes only from the later phases. On every other net the phase keeps the slot above.
It is on by default and MAY be disabled (`linearBound(false)`) to force the fixpoint path — for its certificate, or to exercise the engine itself.

On a net where the enumeration route does not apply, or that has a drained forward, the verifier *shall not* run the bound phase before the enumeration.

argument — "both join slots armed means every upstream stage has run, so no halt is still
possible" — is a weighted count bound, which Spacer's lemma generalisation does not invent
over fifty variables but a linear solver finds in milliseconds. A net that answered `unknown`
after 300 s answers `proven` in under a second.

   weighting that passes the exact re-check, the property is `Proven` with method `structural`,
   without a fixpoint query, and the report names the bound and the demand:
   `  Linear state-equation bound: 2*p0 + a + b <= 2; violation needs a + b + halt >= 3`.
2. A property whose violation the state equation admits (`unsat` from the query) proceeds to
   the fixpoint query with the report line `  Linear state-equation bound: none separates the violation`.
3. The bound is re-proven in exact integer arithmetic; a model that fails it is reported
   `inconclusive (solver model failed the exact re-check)` and the fixpoint query runs.
4. The first demand's `bound` script is byte-identical across implementations ([VER-013] AC1) and is
   reported by `encodeScripts()` (`null` for a quiescence property) whenever `verify()` would
   send it, including on a net with an exact name-coloured plan.

   separates is `Proven` (structural) without the coloured query; one it does not separate

separates the violation on the flat net separates it on the ν-net, and a structural `Proven` is

conditions as the flat path (enabled, a reachability-safety property, not `Ignore` with
environment places, the total budget and cancellation of [VER-013] respected), with the same
phase name. `Proven` returns as on the flat path — method `structural`, the lines of AC1 — and

paragraphs.text: The flat CHC encoding ([VER-001]) MAY carry the **state equation** itself. With the option enabled the state is `(M, n)` — one firing counter `n_t` per flat transition after the places — the initial fact has `n = 0`, transition `t`'s rule sets `n'_t = n_t + 1` and copies every other counter, an environment-injection rule copies them all, and every transition rule's body conjoins `n' ≥ 0` and, for each place `p` whose column is exact (no consume-all / reset arc on `p`, `p` not injected), `m'_p = M0_p + Σ_t C[p][t]·n'_t` over the transitions with a non-zero effect on `p`, in transition order. A place a consume-all or reset arc clears, and that is not injected, carries the upper bound `m'_p ≤ M0_p + Σ_t C[p][t]·n'_t` in the same position instead. It is inductive because a clearing step's guard needs `m_p ≥ pre_p`, so its result `m'_p = post_p` is at most `m_p + C[p][t]`. The error rule quantifies the counters and constrains the marking only.

Every linear consequence of the marking equation — the equality laws of [VER-005] and [VER-007], the decreasing laws of [VER-015], and the mixed-sign inequalities (`y·C ≥ 0 ⇒ y·M ≥ y·M0`) that express *ordering* between the stages of a pipeline — is then a fact in every rule body rather than a lemma Spacer has to generalise to, and it comes at no enumeration cost: the cone of inequality laws of a fifty-place net has too many extreme rays to list, but its defining system has one row per place. This is what a **quiescence** proof on a workflow net needs and [VER-015] cannot give it (a `DeadlockFree` violation is not a linear demand): proper completion of a 50-place agent-dispatch net under conditional sinks ([VER-014]) went from `unknown` at 120 s to `proven` in 1.5 s with this as the only change.

The option is **off by default** so scripts and reports stay byte-identical; a genuinely violated property is still found, about 1.5× slower on the nets above. Soundness is proven in Lean (`StateEquation.lean`: `rows_hold`, `state_equation_reach_eq`): the counters are exact bookkeeping, so every row holds on every reachable augmented state and conjoining them removes none. The **certificate check** ranges over `(M, n)`: the candidate conjoins the P-invariants, `n ≥ 0` and the marking equation, and re-proves them against the raw step relation, whose only counter knowledge is the increment. The certificate check is on by default; with it disabled (`certificateCheck(false)` in Java and TypeScript, `certificate_check(false)` in Rust, `certificate_check=False` in Python) a `Proven` rests on the solver's answer alone, and the report carries `  Certificate check: not applicable (disabled)` in place of the check. The counterexample decoder reads a fact's marking from its leading `P` arguments. The option does not apply to the name-coloured encoding ([NU-050]) or to Route B ([VER-012]); the report says so on the name-coloured path only, and a run that a route or phase decides before the fixpoint query prints no state-equation line.
*While* the state-equation option is enabled, the initial fact of the flat CHC encoding *shall* set every firing counter to 0.

*While* the option is enabled, the rule of each transition *shall* fire that transition only where it is enabled, with the effect it has in the untimed abstraction of [VER-004], add one to its firing counter and copy every other counter, each environment-injection rule *shall* add one token to its place and copy every counter, and no rule but these and the initial fact *shall* derive a `Reachable` fact.

*While* the option is enabled, each transition rule *shall* require of its successor `(M', n')`, for every place that is not injected, the equality `m'_p = M0_p + Σ_t C[p][t]·n'_t` where no consume-all or reset arc clears the place, and the upper bound `m'_p ≤ M0_p + Σ_t C[p][t]·n'_t` where one does.

*While* the option is enabled, apart from the P-invariant conjuncts of [VER-005] and [VER-007] and the environment bounds of [VER-006], the rule of each transition *shall* accept its firing from every state `(M, n)` in which the transition is enabled and whose successor meets the rows above, and each environment-injection rule *shall* accept its injection from every state, so the rows remove no reachable state.

transitions with a non-zero effect on `p`, in transition order. A place a consume-all or
reset arc clears, and that is not injected, carries the upper bound

clearing step's guard needs `m_p ≥ pre_p`, so its result `m'_p = post_p` is at most

fact in every rule body rather than a lemma Spacer has to generalise to, and it comes at no

requirements.title: Bounded State-Space Enumeration Route
requirements.testDerivation: a pipeline `p0 → t0 → p1 → … → pn`, untimed: `deadlockFree` with `pn` a sink is proven by enumeration with `n+1` classes and no solver phase; without the sink it is violated with the firing sequence `t0 … t(n-1)`. The same net with a class budget at or below the graph size reports truncation and is answered by the SMT pipeline; with the budget `0` the route never runs. A `delayed` variant of the same net is skipped as timed. For AC6, the same query with and without the route returns the same verdict. For AC11, an untimed net with an unbounded producer (`gen: G → G, A`) and `placeBound(A, 2)` under a class budget of 50 is `Violated` by the route with the trace `gen, gen, gen`, where it used to fall through; `deadlockFree` on the same truncated graph falls through.

spans.text: The enumeration route *shall* apply exactly when the net it receives, after the rewrites of [VER-006], [VER-004] and [EXEC-042], declares no match transition, has no environment place registered and has only `immediate` transitions, and the class budget is positive.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: The build *shall* be stopped only when the total budget runs out or the caller cancels ([VER-013]).
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *While* the build is neither stopped by the total budget nor cancelled ([VER-013]), the state-class graph *shall* be closed exactly when it has fewer classes than the class budget.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: The state-class graph *shall* hold the initial class as its first class, and only classes reachable from it.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *When* the graph is closed, the route *shall* return `Proven` exactly when no marking reachable from the initial marking violates the property, and `Violated` otherwise.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: *While* the build is neither stopped by the total budget nor cancelled ([VER-013]), the route *shall* return `Violated` when a counted class violates the property, where a counted class is any stored class for a safety property and a class the builder expanded for a quiescence property.
spans.label: s6

spans.text: *When* the route returns `Violated`, it *shall* report a counted class that violates the property, and a firing sequence from the initial marking to the marking of that class that is a path, in the graph the route built, from the initial class to that class.
spans.label: s7

spans.text: *When* the route returns `Violated`, the firing sequence it reports *shall* be no longer than any path, in the graph the route built, from the initial class to a counted class that violates the property.
spans.label: s8

spans.text: The route *shall not* return `Proven` from a graph that is not closed, and *shall* read nothing off a graph whose build was stopped by the total budget or cancelled.
spans.label: s9

spans.text: *When* the route returns `Proven` or `Violated`, the verifier *shall* return that verdict and *shall not* run the SMT pipeline.
spans.label: s10

spans.text: *If* the route does not run, or the graph is truncated and no counted class violates the property, *then* the verifier *shall* continue with the rest of the pipeline exactly as it does without the route, except that the time the route took counts against a total budget ([VER-013]).
spans.label: s11

spans.text: *If* the build is stopped by the total budget or cancelled, *then* the verifier *shall* return the `Unknown` of [VER-013].
spans.label: s12

spans.text: *When* a state-space cache is passed, the verifier *shall* key each entry by the caller's net, the transitions the in-flight split of [VER-004] rewrote, the initial marking and whether the graph is reduced ([VER-024]), and a query *shall* read and write only the entry of its own key.
spans.label: s13

spans.text: *When* an entry holds a closed graph of `C` classes, a query at a budget greater than `C` *shall* reuse it, and a query at a budget of `C` or less *shall* read it as an explored prefix, in both cases without building.
spans.label: s14

spans.text: *When* an entry holds a truncation remembered at budget `B`, a query at a budget of `B` or less *shall* read its explored prefix without building.
spans.label: s15

spans.text: *When* an entry is empty, or holds a truncation remembered at a budget smaller than the query's, the query *shall* build at its own budget, and the entry *shall* then hold a closed graph as closed, a truncated graph with the query's budget, and, after a build stopped by the total budget or cancelled, what it held before.
spans.label: s16

spans.text: *If* a build fails, *then* the entry *shall* stay as the build found it, and the failure *shall* reach the query that ran the build.
spans.label: s17

spans.text: A query *shall* read a graph it built or reused as the route reads it without the cache, and a graph it read as an explored prefix as a graph that is not closed.
spans.label: s18

paragraphs.text: Before the SMT pipeline ([VER-001]), an implementation SHOULD try to decide the property by **enumerating the state-class graph** ([VER-010]) up to a class budget. When the graph closes with fewer classes than the class budget, the verdict is read off it directly and no solver runs for the enumeration; when it does not, the route declines and the SMT pipeline runs unchanged. A reachability-safety property first tries the linear bound of [VER-015], which runs ahead of this route.

The motivation is a shape the fixpoint engine handles badly and enumeration handles trivially. IC3/PDR is built for state spaces that are wide and shallow; a workflow net is the opposite, narrow and deep. A forty-node pipeline has fewer than two thousand reachable classes, but its *diameter* is the length of the pipeline, so the search needs a frame per stage and its cost climbs with roughly the cube of the length. Enumeration is linear in the reachable state space. Measured on a compiled forty-node linear workflow (370 places, 163 transitions, 1 967 classes): **410 s on the fixpoint path, 0.11 s here**; at 160 nodes (1 450 places) enumeration takes 5.5 s while the fixpoint path is far beyond any practical budget.
**When the route applies.** All four conditions, so that its verdict is interchangeable with the one it replaces:

1. The net declares **no match (ν-join) transitions** — a ν-net has its own exact route ([VER-012], Route B), which subsumes this one.
2. **No environment places** are registered on the net the route receives. The graph does not model injection ([VER-006]), so a verdict about an open net would not mean what the encoders' does. A net closed under `Arrivals` ([VER-006]) has none left, and the route applies to it.
3. The net is **untimed** — every transition `immediate`. - The cache holds its graphs until the caller drops it or clears it. It never shares memory the caller did not ask for.

The enumeration route *shall* apply exactly when the net it receives, after the rewrites of [VER-006], [VER-004] and [EXEC-042], declares no match transition, has no environment place registered and has only `immediate` transitions, and the class budget is positive.

notes.text:
- TypeScript: `verification/scg-verifier` (`verifyViaStateClassGraph`, `isUntimed`); `SmtVerifier.enumerationMaxClasses(max)`, default 50 000. The shared predicate is `verification/graph-decision` (`decideOverClasses`), used by [VER-012]'s route as well. The state-space cache is `StateSpaceCache` (`verification/state-space-cache`; its only public method is `clear()`), passed with `SmtVerifier.stateSpaceCache(cache)`. The key is the net instance (held weakly), the list of transitions the in-flight split rewrote, the initial marking in the order it lists its places, and the `Place` objects it names, so an equal marking listed in another order misses. `decideOverStateSpace` (exported from `libpetri/verification`) returns an `ScgOutcome`, `truncated` for an incomplete graph. The build is synchronous, so concurrent `verify()` calls on one event loop build an entry once, and a build that throws leaves the previous entry in place.
- Java: `org.libpetri.smt.ScgVerifier`; `SmtVerifier.enumerationMaxClasses(int)`. A transition with the deprecated `Timing.Unconstrained` counts as timed there, so a net using it skips the route in Java only; the rest of the pipeline gives the same verdict. The state-space cache is `org.libpetri.smt.StateSpaceCache` (`clear()`; `size()` counts entries, builds in flight included), passed with `SmtVerifier.stateSpaceCache(StateSpaceCache)`. The key is the net by identity, the list of transitions the in-flight split rewrote, the initial marking by equality, and the order `placesWithTokens()` lists its places in, so the whole witness matches an uncached query. It is thread-safe: concurrent queries wait on one build per entry, and waiting is not interruptible.
- Rust: `libpetri-verification` `scg_verifier`; `SmtVerifier::enumeration_max_classes(usize)`. The cache is `state_space_cache::StateSpaceCache` (`new`, `clear`, `len`, `is_empty`, `build_count`; `len` counts closed and truncated entries, including one whose larger rebuild is in flight, but not a first build; `Clone` shares it, `Send + Sync`), passed as `SmtVerifier::state_space_cache(&cache)`. A `PetriNet` has no identity, so the key is a structural fingerprint of the net every route reads (closed under arrivals, with its inert places, split in flight unless `assume_atomic_firing`): the `Debug` rendering of its place names, sorted, its terminals and, per transition, name, input specs, output spec, inhibitor, read and reset arcs, timing, priority and match presence. Actions and transition ids are left out, so clones and rebuilt copies hit. The full string is the key, not a hash. The marking is keyed by its counts in place-name order. A witness from a cached graph starts at the caller's own listing of the initial marking. Parallel queries wait on a per-entry condition variable. A build that panics restores the slot to what it held (empty, or the truncation), wakes the waiters to retry, and propagates.
- Python: `verify(..., enumeration_max_classes=50_000)`. The cache is `libpetri.StateSpaceCache()` (`len(cache)`, `cache.build_count`, `cache.clear()`), passed as `verify(..., state_space_cache=cache)`. It wraps the Rust cache, so it keys on the same structural fingerprint, which is why it hits although the binding clones the net on every call. An empty cache is falsy, since it defines `__len__`. The `initial_marking` dict is read in insertion order, so a witness starts in the caller's order.
- Under `Arrivals` ([VER-006]) the implementations differ. Java and TypeScript do not use the cache for a query whose `Arrivals` closure closes the net, and the report says so, with the same line in both (`SmtVerifier.java` and `smt-verifier.ts`, the enumeration step). Rust and Python key the fingerprint of the closed net, so the closure is in the key and a repeated query hits.

paragraphs.text: The enumeration of [VER-017] explores every interleaving. A net that forks one token into `k` independent subnets therefore has a state space close to the **product** of the subnets' spaces, although each subnet closes alone in a few hundred classes. Measured on a 134-transition composed agent net that forks into six independent subnets (3 to 404 classes each): about 3 000 000 classes explored in 600 s without closing. A quiescence property only asks about the classes where nothing is enabled, and the order in which independent transitions fire does not change which dead markings are reachable. On such a property the route SHOULD therefore expand, at each class, only the enabled transitions of a **stubborn set** (Valmari's deadlock-preserving reduction), which brings the graph close to the **sum** of the subnets' spaces.
**When the reduction applies.** All of:

1. The enumeration route of [VER-017] runs (no ν-join, no environment places, untimed, positive class budget).
2. The property is a **quiescence property**: `deadlockFree`, `terminatesAtSink`, `joinedOrDeadLettered` or `quiescentCount`. Each reads only the classes without successors. Safety properties keep the full graph; their violations need not be dead.
3. The net has no drained forward ([IO-014]); its marking-dependent deposits are outside the model the reduction is proven on.
4. The reduction is enabled. It is on by default; `partialOrderReduction(false)` turns it off.

**Footprints.** The reduction reads the net the graph is built on (after the inert-place, in-flight split of [VER-004] and terminal rewrites of [EXEC-042]). For a transition `t`, taking every outcome of every branch ([VER-021]) together:

- `tests(t)`: its input, read and inhibitor places.
- `writes(t)`: its input and reset places and every place an outcome deposits into.
- `overwrites(t)`: its reset places and its consume-all inputs (`all`, `atLeast`), whose new count does not depend on the old one.

Two transitions `t ≠ u` are **dependent** when `writes(t) ∩ tests(u)`, `writes(u) ∩ tests(t)`, `overwrites(t) ∩ writes(u)` or `overwrites(u) ∩ writes(t)` is non-empty. Independent transitions enabled together stay enabled after either fires, and firing them in either order reaches the same marking. A transition that can **increase** `p` is one with an outcome depositing into `p`; one that can **decrease** `p` has `p` among its inputs or resets.
**The stubborn set at a class with marking `M`.** For a seed transition `s` enabled at `M`, the closure `S(s)` is the least set containing `s` such that, for every `t ∈ S(s)`:

- (D1) if `t` is enabled at `M`, every transition dependent with `t` is in `S(s)`;
- (D2) if `t` is disabled at `M`, take its **first unsatisfied condition**, over its input and read places in code-point order of place name, then over its inhibitor places in code-point order: an input or read place `p` with too few tokens puts every transition that can increase `p` into `S(s)`; a marked inhibitor place `p` puts every transition that can decrease `p` into `S(s)`.

The route computes `S(s)` for every enabled seed and keeps the one with the **fewest enabled transitions**, the code-point-smallest seed name breaking ties, and expands only that set's enabled transitions, each with all of its outcomes. The choice is a function of the marking and the net, so every implementation builds the same reduced graph, with the same class count.

**What the verdict means.** Unchanged: exact for the quiescence property. Every class of the reduced graph is reachable, and every dead marking reachable in the full graph is reachable in the reduced one: a run to a dead marking must fire a transition of the set (an enabled member that no transition outside it can disable would otherwise still be enabled at the end), and the first such firing commutes to the front. A class has no reduced successor exactly when nothing is enabled at it, so the classes the reduced graph reports quiescent are exactly the reachable dead markings. A `violated` is a real firing sequence and stays confirmed ([VER-017] AC2), but it is the shortest path **in the reduced graph**, which may be longer than the shortest run of the net. A truncated reduced graph is read as in [VER-017]: a violation in its expanded prefix stands, and no truncated graph yields `Proven`.

**State-space cache.** A reduced graph answers only quiescence properties, so the cache of [VER-017] keys it apart from the full graph of the same net and marking: a safety query never reads a reduced entry, and a quiescence query with the reduction off never reads one either.

*While* the enumeration route of [VER-017] runs on a quiescence property (`deadlockFree`, `terminatesAtSink`, `joinedOrDeadLettered` or `quiescentCount`), on a net without a drained forward ([IO-014]), with the reduction enabled, the route *shall* build the reduced graph.
*If* the property is not a quiescence property, the net has a drained forward or the reduction is disabled, *then* the route *shall* build the full graph of [VER-017].
Every implementation *shall* turn the reduction on by default.

*While* the reduction applies, *when* the route expands a class whose marking `M` enables a transition, it *shall* expand exactly the enabled transitions of `S(s)` for the enabled seed `s` whose closure has the fewest enabled transitions, the code-point-smallest seed name breaking ties.

*When* a transition `t` of `S(s)` is disabled at `M`, the closure *shall* read its first unsatisfied condition over its input and read places in code-point order of place name, then over its inhibitor places in code-point order.
*While* the reduction applies, the route *shall* expand the transitions it selects at a class in ascending code-point order of transition name.
*When* the route expands a class, it *shall* expand only enabled transitions, each with all of its outcomes.
*While* the reduction applies, every dead marking reachable from the initial marking *shall* be reachable by a run that fires, at each class, one of the transitions the route expands there.
*While* the reduction applies, a class *shall* have no reduced successor exactly when no transition is enabled at its marking.

The cache of [VER-017] *shall* key a reduced graph apart from the full graph of the same net and initial marking, so that a safety query, and a quiescence query with the reduction off, never read a reduced entry.

requirements.title: State-Equation Phase with Refinement
requirements.testDerivation: with the enumeration budget of [VER-017] at 0 and `assumeAtomicFiring`, since [VER-017] would otherwise decide these small untimed nets first and the in-flight split of [VER-004] would verify the arms of the join and `produce` of the queue in two steps: the join of a compiled workflow net, `route: start → AND(aData, bEmpty) | AND(aEmpty, bData)`, a data arm writing `hasdata` with its `ready`, an empty arm its `ready` alone, `mergeStart: ready0 + ready1 + all(hasdata) → done`, `mergeSkip: ready0 + ready1, inhibitor(hasdata) → skipped`, under `deadlockFree` with `done` and `skipped` as sinks: the first candidate skips after the data arrived, one inductive inequality excludes it, and the proof passes the certificate check. The queue-and-bundle net (`produce: budget → q` inhibited by `s` and by `out`, `signal: src → s`, `bundle: all(q) + s → out`, `bundleEmpty: s, inhibitor(q) → out`, `M0 = {budget: 3, src: 1}`) with `out` and `budget` as sinks: proven with `3*out + q <= 3`, relative to the equation. With a `cancel: src → cancelled` alternative and `cancelled` a sink: violated, with the run `produce, produce, produce, cancel`.

spans.text: *When* the state-equation query answers `unsat`, the phase *shall* end with a proof over the refinements it has added so far.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *If* the state-equation query fails in the transport, answers `unknown`, gives a model that cannot be decoded, or the timeout runs out before its answer, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *When* the state-equation query answers `sat`, the phase *shall* first run the witness search on the candidate, and *shall* return `Violated` with the run the search reports before it tries any refinement.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: The witness search *shall* fire each flat transition at most as often as the candidate's counts allow, under the exact abstract semantics of [VER-004] and with no injection step, and *shall* report a run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.
spans.label: s4

paragraphs.text: Before the fixpoint query, the verifier asks one `QF_LIA` query (phase `state-equation`, through the transport of [VER-013]): can a marking that satisfies the marking equation of [VER-016] violate the property? The equation is `m = M0 + C·n` over firing counts `n ≥ 0`, with an upper bound on a place a consume-all or reset arc clears and no row for an injected place; the violation is encoded exactly as the error rule of [VER-001] encodes it. Every reachable marking satisfies the equation for the counts of its run, so `unsat` proves the property. Unlike [VER-015] the query asks for the violation directly, so it covers every property, quiescence included.
*When* the state-equation query answers `unsat`, the phase *shall* end with a proof over the refinements it has added so far.

*If* the state-equation query fails in the transport, answers `unknown`, gives a model that cannot be decoded, or the timeout runs out before its answer, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.

A `sat` model is a **candidate**: the equation ignores firing order and the guards that impose it, so the net need not reach the candidate. On a compiled workflow net the typical spurious candidate is a join's skip transition, inhibited by the data place, firing after the data arrived. Each candidate is settled, in this order, by:

1. **Witness.** A breadth-first search from `M0` under the exact abstract semantics ([VER-004]: consume-all and reset clearing, inhibitor and read guards) that fires each flat transition at most as often as the candidate's counts allow and stops at the first violating marking. A run found is reported `violated`, confirmed ([VER-003]).

Injections are not searched. On a net with injected environment places a run found is still real: it injects nothing, and quiescence is judged with the relax-env enablement of [VER-006], so its marking is stuck whatever the environment does. A completed search there proves nothing, since an injected token could enable a run it never tried. The search is the phase's only source of witnesses there. A run that needs an injection is left to the bounded witness phase ([VER-025]), which unrolls injection steps and runs before the fixpoint query.

2. **Trap.** An initially marked trap the candidate leaves empty (Esparza, Ledesma-Garza, Majumdar, Meyer and Niksic, CAV 2014). A transition with a consume-all input or a reset arc on a trap place removes tokens from the trap, so it too must put one back. Adds `Σ_{q∈Q} m_q ≥ 1`.
3. **Inductive inequality.** A linear inequality `a·M ≤ b` that holds at `M0`, is kept by every step of the exact step relation, and excludes the candidate. One `QF_LIA` query (phase `invariant`) encodes Farkas consecution with the invariant's multiplier restricted to `{0, 1}` per transition (Colón, Sankaranarayanan and Sipma, CAV 2003): each step either keeps the bound or re-establishes it from its guard alone. The weights are integers of least total magnitude, re-checked in exact integer arithmetic before use. When none exists, the query is repeated with the marking equation as a premise of every step (one Farkas weighting of the equation per transition). Such a *relative* inequality is inductive only together with the equation, so the exact re-check cannot apply and only the certificate check re-proves it. On the join above the result is `hasdata ≤ ready_0 + ready_1`; on a queue bundled once a signal arrives, `N·out + q ≤ N`, relative to the equation's `q + budget ≤ N`.

*When* the state-equation query answers `sat`, the phase *shall* first run the witness search on the candidate, and *shall* return `Violated` with the run the search reports before it tries any refinement.

The witness search *shall* fire each flat transition at most as often as the candidate's counts allow, under the exact abstract semantics of [VER-004] and with no injection step, and *shall* report a run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.
A run the witness search reports *shall* be no longer than any other run within the counts that ends in a violating marking.
The witness search *shall* report that no violating run exists only when it has completed, no run within the counts ends in a violating marking, and no environment place is declared for injection.
*While* environment places are declared for injection, the phase *shall* still run the witness search, and the search *shall* report the same run it reports on the same net without injection.
*If* a run within the candidate's counts ends in a violating marking, *then* the witness search *shall* report a run whenever its node budget is large enough.

The trap search *shall* return a set `Q` of places of the flat net only when every flat transition that can take a token from `Q`, through an input arc, a consume-all input or a reset arc, also puts a token into `Q`, some place of `Q` is marked in `M0`, and the candidate leaves every place of `Q` empty.
The trap search *shall* return a trap whenever some initially marked trap among the places of the flat net is empty in the candidate.
The exact re-check *shall* accept an inequality `a·M ≤ b` only when it holds at `M0` and every firing and every injection step of the exact step relation keeps it.

The exact re-check *shall* accept an inequality `a·M ≤ b` that holds at `M0`, gives no injected place a positive weight, and for which every flat transition that can fire, taken from the least marking its guard allows, passes the keep test or the restore test: the keep test, that the firing does not raise `a·M` and every place the firing clears without inhibiting has a weight of at least 0; the restore test, that the marking after the firing meets the bound and every place the firing neither clears nor inhibits has a weight of at most 0.

*When* the witness search reports no run and the phase has added fewer refinements than the refinement limit, the phase *shall* settle the candidate in this order: with `Σ_{q∈Q} m_q ≥ 1` when the trap search returns a trap `Q`; otherwise with the inequality the `invariant` query returns, marked inductive, when the exact re-check accepts it and the candidate violates it; otherwise, when that query answers `unsat`, with the inequality the same query returns with the marking equation as a premise of every step, marked relative, when the candidate violates it.
*When* the phase adds a refinement, it *shall* ask the state-equation query again with every refinement added so far.

*If* no trap and no inequality settles the candidate, an inequality fails the exact re-check or holds at the candidate, or an `invariant` query fails in the transport, answers `unknown`, gives a model that cannot be decoded, or the timeout runs out before its answer, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.

Every trap and inductive refinement holds in every reachable marking, and a relative one does too when the solver's answer is right, since it is inductive together with the equation; so the query is asked again and a later `unsat` is still a proof. The phase steps aside, leaving the pipeline unchanged, when nothing settles a candidate, after 32 refinements, on a transport failure, or when the timeout runs out.

*If* the witness search reports no run on a candidate after the phase has added as many refinements as the refinement limit, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.
The refinement limit *shall* be 32 in every implementation.
The node budget of one witness search *shall* be 100 000 in every implementation.
Each weight of an inductive or relative inequality *shall* have a magnitude of at most the larger of 8 and the number of tokens in `M0`.

**Certificate.** A proof is the inductive invariant `SE(M, n) ∧ ⋀ refinements(M)` over the places and one counter per flat transition. It goes as the `Reachable` interpretation to the certificate check of [VER-016], which re-proves initiation, consecution and safety against the raw step relation before `Proven` is reported with method `state-equation`. The report prints each refinement and the result lists them as its discovered invariants. A failed or inconclusive check withholds the `Proven`, says so in the report, and the pipeline continues. The Farkas dual of the final `unsat` is not used as the certificate: for a quiescence property the violation is a disjunction, and one inequality per disjunct is exponential in the net.

*While* the certificate check is enabled, the verifier *shall* return the phase's proof as `Proven` with method `state-equation` and neither a counterexample nor `counterexampleConfirmed` when the certificate check of [VER-016] passes on the invariant `SE(M, n) ∧ ⋀ refinements(M)`, and a failed or inconclusive check *shall* withhold the `Proven` and let the pipeline continue.

*While* the certificate check is disabled, the verifier *shall* return the phase's proof as `Proven` with method `state-equation` and neither a counterexample nor `counterexampleConfirmed`, and the report *shall* carry `  Certificate check: not applicable (disabled)` in place of the check.
*When* the phase returns `Violated`, the verifier *shall* return the markings and transitions of the run, in firing order, as the counterexample, with `counterexampleConfirmed` `true`.

**Where it runs.** On the flat path, after [VER-015] and before the fixpoint query. Not on a net with match transitions (the flat encoding is name-blind there; [VER-012] and [NU-053] are its exact routes), not on the name-coloured encoding, and not under `Ignore` with environment places registered ([VER-006]). On by default; MAY be disabled to force the fixpoint path.
The pipeline *shall* place the state-equation phase at one point, after the linear bound of [VER-015] and before the fixpoint query.

*While* the phase is enabled, the pipeline *shall* run it on exactly the queries whose verified net has no match transition and that are not verified under `Ignore` with environment places registered ([VER-006]), unless an earlier step has decided the query or the run has stopped.
*If* the phase is disabled, *then* the verifier *shall not* run it, and the verdicts and reports *shall* be those of the pipeline without the phase.
Every implementation *shall* turn the phase on by default.

Measured on 23 compiled workflow nets of 28–370 places under `DeadlockFree` with conditional sinks ([VER-014]): 21 proven in 10–220 ms, four after one refinement, among them a 41-node chain and a twenty-way switch that took 410 s and 277 s on the fixpoint path; one violated in 0.3 s; one left to the next phase.

paragraphs.text: After [VER-018] and before the fixpoint query, the verifier tries to bound the length of every run. A **ranking** is a weighting `r ≥ 0` of the places with `r·C_t ≤ −1` for every flat transition `t` that can fire (one that inhibits a place it needs cannot). A consume-all or reset arc removes at least `pre`, so with `r ≥ 0` the column `C_t = post − pre` bounds such a firing's effect on `r·M` from above. Every firing therefore lowers `r·M` by at least one, `r·M` never goes below zero, and no run from `M0` has more than `K = r·M0` firings. The ranking with the least `K` is found by one `QF_LIA` optimisation query (phase `ranking`) and re-checked in exact integer arithmetic.

*When* the ranking query answers with a weighting `r`, the phase *shall* re-check in exact integer arithmetic that every weight is at least 0 and that `r·C_t ≤ −1` for every flat transition `t` that can fire, and *shall* take the bound `K = r·M0` only when the re-check passes.
*If* the re-check fails or `K` is larger than `2^53 − 1`, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive without a bounded model check, and the pipeline *shall* continue.
`2^53 − 1` is the largest integer that every implementation counts depths in exactly, so all of them refuse the same bounds.

With the bound, a **bounded model check** decides the property. One `QF_LIA` script (phase `bmc`) unrolls `d` steps of the exact step relation from `M0`: a selector per step names the transition fired or an idle step, an idle step is followed only by idle steps, and the violation is asked of the last marking. The encoder also emits the environment post-caps of [VER-006] for the bounded witness phase ([VER-025]); here there are none, since this phase sends no query on a net with injected environment places.

*When* the phase has the bound `K`, it *shall* ask the bounded model check first at depth `min(K, 8, L)`, where `L` is the depth limit, and after an `unsat` answer at a depth `d` below both `K` and `L` it *shall* ask next at depth `min(2d, K, L)`.
The depth limit `L` *shall* be 512 in every implementation.
With the default limit, a bound of 5 is asked at depth 5 alone, and a bound of 25 at the depths 8, 16 and 25.
*If* the bounded model check answers `unsat` at a depth of at least `K`, *then* the phase *shall* return `Proven` with method `bounded-model-check` and the bound `K`.
That is a claim about every run, since none is longer than `K`.
*If* the bounded model check answers `unsat` at the depth limit while `K` is larger, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.

*When* the bounded model check answers `sat` at a depth, the phase *shall* read the run from the model's selectors as the bounded witness phase ([VER-025]) reads it with no injection step, replay it under the exact abstract semantics, and return `Violated` with that run, untrimmed and confirmed, when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.

*If* the depth is positive and the model defines none of the step selectors, or the run does not replay to a violating marking, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.
A depth of 0 has no selectors: its run is empty, and it is reported when `M0` violates the property. That depth is asked only when `K` is 0.

When no ranking exists, Farkas gives firing counts `y ≥ 0, y ≠ 0` with `C·y ≥ 0`, which the marking equation lets repeat forever. The report names their transitions (a second query) and the pipeline continues. This does not show that the net has an infinite run (a loop that only an inhibitor stops has no ranking), only that the phase makes no claim about runs it cannot bound.
*If* the ranking query answers `unsat`, *then* the phase *shall* report that the net has no firing bound, whatever the second query answers, and the pipeline *shall* continue to the fixpoint query.

*If* the ranking query or a bounded model check fails in the transport or answers `unknown`, or the phase budget is spent before its answer, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.

A proof from this phase has no inductive invariant, so the certificate check does not apply; it rests on the exactly re-checked ranking and the solver's `unsat`. The phase gets half the timeout, rounded down to whole milliseconds and at least 1 ms: short counterexamples take seconds, while a proof to a deep bound on a wide net can outlast any budget. It runs on the queries [VER-018] runs on, whether [VER-018] is enabled or not. Its bounded run has transition steps only. The bounded witness phase ([VER-025]) shares its encoder, adds injection steps to it and asks one fixed depth without a bound, so it finds runs but proves nothing; on a net without injection its script is this phase's script. A name-alignment property ([NU-055]) gets no query from the phase: it ends inconclusive with the reason of [NU-055] before any other check.
*If* environment places are declared for injection, *then* the phase *shall* send no query and *shall* end inconclusive, also when no arc touches such a place.
No weighting bounds an injection.
Every implementation *shall* turn this phase on by default, as it turns on the phase of [VER-018].
A pre-fixpoint verdict carries its own `method` and report, so differing defaults break the verdict-parity fixtures without any property differing.
*If* the phase is disabled, *then* the verifier *shall not* run it, and the verdicts and reports *shall* be those of the pipeline without the phase.
Disabling the phase leaves the query to the later steps, up to the fixpoint query.
The pipeline *shall* place the firing-bound phase at one point, after the state-equation phase of [VER-018] and before the bounded witness phase of [VER-025] and the fixpoint query.
So no run enters the state-equation phase after this phase, this phase after the witness phase or the fixpoint query, or this phase twice.

*While* the phase is enabled, the pipeline *shall* run it on exactly the queries that the state-equation phase of [VER-018] runs on when that phase is enabled, whether [VER-018] is enabled or not, unless an earlier step has decided the query or the run has stopped.
*When* the phase ends inconclusive or reports that the net has no firing bound, the pipeline *shall* go on to its next step.

*When* the phase returns `Proven` or `Violated`, the verifier *shall* return that result: `Proven` with the method `bounded-model-check` and neither a counterexample nor `counterexampleConfirmed`; `Violated` with the transitions of the replayed run, in firing order, as the counterexample and `counterexampleConfirmed` `true`.

Measured on the same 23 workflow nets: the violated net [VER-018] leaves open has `K = 25` and a 22-step counterexample at depth 25 in about 11 s; proofs to `K ≤ 22` take 0.1–70 s; `K = 86` on the twenty-way switch does not finish depth 16 within 120 s; two loop nets have no ranking. Four agent nets whose round only an inhibitor stops have none either, although every run terminates; with the re-entry routed through a place of its own they have one, and where their graphs close `K` equals the longest run (38, 41, 50 and 70 firings).

1. The ranking is re-checked in exact integer arithmetic before its bound is used; the report

   confirmed.

requirements.title: Bounded Witness Phase
requirements.testDerivation: the `envBoundedPair` fixtures at the default depth and at depth 10. One test per gate and per outcome, each failing when only that gate or outcome is removed: the stub replies of AC7 and AC8, and for AC5 the ν-net of [VER-006] AC7 under `Bounded(1)` with `Unreachable(merged)` and with `DeadlockFree`. A test elsewhere that pins the fixpoint query's own result (its replay and the replay's outcomes, the replay opt-out, its report lines, a dump listing) sets the witness depth to 0, since the phase now answers first.

spans.text: *If* the pipeline reaches the flat fixpoint query, the witness depth `D` is positive, and the net has no match transitions or the property is a reachability-safety property with a budget place declared, *then* the verifier *shall* run the phase directly before the fixpoint script is encoded.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *While* the fixpoint query takes the name-coloured encoding ([NU-053]), the verifier *shall not* run the phase.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *If* the net has match transitions and either the property is not a reachability-safety property or no budget place is declared, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the phase.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: *If* the witness depth is 0, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the phase, and its verdict, route, report and scripts *shall* be those of the pipeline without the phase.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *When* the verifier does not run the phase, it *shall* send no query for it and print no report line for it.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: *While* environment places are registered under `Ignore`, the phase *shall* run where it runs on any other flat net, with no injection step.
spans.label: s6

spans.text: *While* the counterexample replay of [VER-003] is disabled, the phase *shall* run where it runs with the replay enabled, and a run it reports *shall* still be confirmed.
spans.label: s7

spans.text: *If* the property is a name-alignment property ([NU-055]), *then* the phase *shall* send no query and *shall* end inconclusive with the reason of [NU-055] that the property is decided only by the name-partition state-class graph.
spans.label: s8

spans.text: *When* the phase runs, the verifier *shall* send this script, and every implementation *shall* emit it byte for byte the same for the same net, initial marking, property and options.
spans.label: s9

spans.text: *If* `J` is 0, *then* the script *shall* be byte-identical to the bounded run of [VER-019] at the same depth.
spans.label: s10

spans.text: *When* the solver answers `sat`, the phase *shall* read the run from the model's selectors in step order up to the first idle step, taking a value in `[0, T)` as a transition step, a value in `[T, T + J)` as an injection step, and any other value, or a selector the model leaves undefined, as idle, and *shall* read no run from a model that defines no selector.
spans.label: s11

spans.text: *When* the phase replays a run, it *shall* fire each transition step under the exact abstract semantics with the environment post-caps, take each injection step only while its guard holds, and accept the run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.
spans.label: s12

spans.text: *When* a run replays, the phase *shall* trim it: it *shall* first cut the run to its violating prefix, then try the steps from the last to the first, replace the run by the violating prefix of the run without that step whenever one exists, and repeat such passes until one changes nothing.
spans.label: s13

spans.text: *When* the phase reports a run, it *shall* report the trimmed run, replayed, with each transition step labelled by its transition's name and each injection step by `inject(<place>)`.
spans.label: s14

spans.text: *When* the phase starts, it *shall* start a wall-clock budget of `max(1, floor(timeout_ms / 8))` milliseconds before it encodes the script, and the query *shall* receive what is left of it.
spans.label: s15

spans.text: *When* the phase runs, the report *shall* carry the line `  Bounded witness phase (VER-025):` followed by exactly one of the status lines below.
spans.label: s16

spans.text: *When* a run replays, the phase *shall* return `Violated` with the trimmed run as the counterexample, `counterexampleConfirmed` `true` and the route of the SMT pipeline ([VER-003]), and the result *shall* continue as the witness result of [VER-018] and [VER-019] does.
spans.label: s17

spans.text: *When* the phase returns `Violated` on a net with match transitions, the result *shall* pass the ν guard of [NU-050] as a name-blind verdict and carry the guard's note that the counterexample may be spurious.
spans.label: s18
