paragraphs.text: Directly before the flat fixpoint query, the verifier asks one `QF_LIA` query (phase `witness`, through the transport of [VER-013]): does a run of at most `D` steps lead from `M0` to a violating marking? A step is the firing of a flat transition or an **injection step** of [VER-006]. A `sat` answer is decoded into a run, replayed under the exact abstract semantics ([VER-004]), trimmed and reported `Violated`, confirmed. Every other answer leaves the pipeline as it was, and the fixpoint query runs. The phase finds the short counterexamples the earlier phases cannot: [VER-018] does not search injections, [VER-019] refuses a net with injected environment places, and neither runs on a net with match transitions.

The phase proves nothing. `unsat` at depth `D` says nothing about a run of `D + 1` steps, and a net with injections or loops has no firing bound ([VER-019]) that would turn it into a proof. The phase therefore adds `Violated` verdicts and never removes one: a replayed run is a run of the step relation the fixpoint query over-approximates, so a sound fixpoint query could not have proven the property.
**Where it runs.**

*If* the pipeline reaches the flat fixpoint query, the witness depth `D` is positive, and the net has no match transitions or the property is a reachability-safety property with a budget place declared, *then* the verifier *shall* run the phase directly before the fixpoint script is encoded.
*While* the fixpoint query takes the name-coloured encoding ([NU-053]), the verifier *shall not* run the phase.
*If* the net has match transitions and either the property is not a reachability-safety property or no budget place is declared, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the phase.
The ν guard ([NU-050]) turns every verdict there into `Unknown`, so the query would be pure cost.
*If* the witness depth is 0, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the phase, and its verdict, route, report and scripts *shall* be those of the pipeline without the phase.
*When* the verifier does not run the phase, it *shall* send no query for it and print no report line for it.
*While* environment places are registered under `Ignore`, the phase *shall* run where it runs on any other flat net, with no injection step.

A run that injects nothing is a run of the net, as the fixpoint query's `Violated` is there ([VER-006]). Under `Arrivals` the net is rewritten before any route runs and has no environment places ([VER-006]), so the arrivals are ordinary transitions of the run.
*While* the counterexample replay of [VER-003] is disabled, the phase *shall* run where it runs with the replay enabled, and a run it reports *shall* still be confirmed.
That option governs the replay after the fixpoint query only; the phase replays its own run.

*If* the property is a name-alignment property ([NU-055]), *then* the phase *shall* send no query and *shall* end inconclusive with the reason of [NU-055] that the property is decided only by the name-partition state-class graph.
Route B decides such a property before the pipeline reaches the phase; the refusal keeps the phase from reading a run of counts as a claim about names.
**The step relation.** The phase unrolls the flat net's steps:

- a **transition step** fires one flat transition under the exact abstract semantics of [VER-004] (consume-all and reset clearing, inhibitor and read guards) and keeps the environment post-caps of [VER-006];
- an **injection step** adds one token to one injected environment place that resolves in the flat net. Under `Bounded(k)` it is enabled only while the place holds fewer than `k` tokens, under `AlwaysAvailable` always. It has no post-cap: its guard already keeps the place at or below `k`.

These are the steps of the HORN encoding's transition and injection rules and of the counterexample replay of [VER-003]. The phase's script and replay carry no P-invariant or semiflow conjunct ([VER-005], [VER-007]), which the HORN rules add: a `Violated` from the phase rests on the replay alone and does not depend on the invariants the pipeline computed.

The script caps every marking after `M0` and the replay caps each transition step's successor, so the two accept the same runs only while `M0` is within the post-caps. The premises of [VER-006] AC3, checked before any route runs, keep it there.

**The script.** `T` is the number of flat transitions and `J` the number of injected environment places that resolve in the flat net, taken in place-index order, each with its bound under `Bounded(k)` or none. Selector value `t < T` is transition `t` in net order, `T + j` is injection `j`, and `T + J` is the idle step. Each step `i` of the `D` steps emits, in this order:
The violation at the last marking and the trailer are those of [VER-019], and so is the first line, `; Bounded run (VER-019): <D> steps of the exact step relation from M0, idle`.
*When* the phase runs, the verifier *shall* send this script, and every implementation *shall* emit it byte for byte the same for the same net, initial marking, property and options.
*If* `J` is 0, *then* the script *shall* be byte-identical to the bounded run of [VER-019] at the same depth.
**Decode, replay and trim.**

*When* the solver answers `sat`, the phase *shall* read the run from the model's selectors in step order up to the first idle step, taking a value in `[0, T)` as a transition step, a value in `[T, T + J)` as an injection step, and any other value, or a selector the model leaves undefined, as idle, and *shall* read no run from a model that defines no selector.

*When* the phase replays a run, it *shall* fire each transition step under the exact abstract semantics with the environment post-caps, take each injection step only while its guard holds, and accept the run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.

*When* a run replays, the phase *shall* trim it: it *shall* first cut the run to its violating prefix, then try the steps from the last to the first, replace the run by the violating prefix of the run without that step whenever one exists, and repeat such passes until one changes nothing.

The violating prefix of a run is its shortest prefix that replays to a violating marking, the empty prefix (`M0` itself) included; a run has none when no prefix replays to a violating marking. A step after the violation need not be enabled for a prefix to count.
*When* the phase reports a run, it *shall* report the trimmed run, replayed, with each transition step labelled by its transition's name and each injection step by `inject(<place>)`.

The solver pads a run to the full depth with steps that lead nowhere, and a padded run can pass a violating marking and go on; the trim removes such steps. The trimmed run ends at the first violating marking it reaches, and it is irredundant: no single step of it can be dropped so that some prefix of the rest still replays to a violating marking. When `M0` violates, the trimmed run is the empty one, whatever model the solver returned. It is not claimed to be a shortest run. Which run is reported depends on the model the solver returns; for one model the trim fixes it, so every implementation reports the same run for the same stub model.
**Budget.**
*When* the phase starts, it *shall* start a wall-clock budget of `max(1, floor(timeout_ms / 8))` milliseconds before it encodes the script, and the query *shall* receive what is left of it.

The query passes the total-budget clamp of [VER-013] like every other process. The phase is the step `witness phase` of that requirement's reason `total verification budget of <N> ms exhausted during <phase>`. The trim polls the [VER-013] deadline (the total budget and cancellation) before each candidate it replays; a stop found there ends the verification as a stop anywhere else in the step `witness phase` does. Outside a `verify()` call the poll does nothing.
**Report.**
*When* the phase runs, the report *shall* carry the line `  Bounded witness phase (VER-025):` followed by exactly one of the status lines below.

- `    Status: a run of <n> steps reaches a violation (replayed; depth <D>)`, with `<n>` the number of steps of the trimmed run, written the same way for every `n` (`a run of 1 steps` included, and `0` exactly when `M0` violates)
- `    Status: no run of at most <D> steps reaches a violation (not a proof)`
- `    Status: inconclusive (<reason>)`

The inconclusive reasons are the transport's failure message ([VER-013]); `z3 reported an error: <line>`, when the reply carries an `(error ...)` line other than `model is not available`, with a verdict line or without; `time budget of <ms> ms exhausted`, with `<ms>` the phase budget `max(1, floor(timeout_ms / 8))`, when that budget is spent before the query starts; `the bounded run at depth <D> answered unknown`; `the bounded run did not replay under the exact semantics`, when the model yields no run or its run does not replay; and the reason of [NU-055] for a name-alignment property. A reply with such an error line counts as a query that fails in the transport: an errored assertion drops out of the query, so its verdict line would answer a different question. The phases of [VER-018] and [VER-019] read their replies the same way. When the total budget or a cancellation of [VER-013] stops the verification during the phase, the trim included, the status line is `    Status: inconclusive (<reason>)` with the stop reason of [VER-013], and the `Unknown` result of that requirement follows it.
**Outcomes.**

*When* a run replays, the phase *shall* return `Violated` with the trimmed run as the counterexample, `counterexampleConfirmed` `true` and the route of the SMT pipeline ([VER-003]), and the result *shall* continue as the witness result of [VER-018] and [VER-019] does.

That result is `=== RESULT ===`, `VIOLATED: <property>`, `  Counterexample trace (replay order, <k> states):` with one line per marking, `  Firing sequence: <a> -> <b>` unless the run is empty, and the untimed warning of [VER-003] AC7. A run of 0 steps is the empty firing sequence of [VER-003] AC8: one marking, no transition and no `Firing sequence` line.

*When* the phase returns `Violated` on a net with match transitions, the result *shall* pass the ν guard of [NU-050] as a name-blind verdict and carry the guard's note that the counterexample may be spurious.
*When* the phase returns `Violated`, the counterexample-timing step of [VER-023] *shall* apply to the result as to every result of the pipeline.
*If* the solver answers `unsat`, *then* the phase *shall* report that no run of at most `D` steps reaches a violation, and the pipeline *shall* continue to the fixpoint query.

*If* the query fails in the transport, the solver answers `unknown`, the phase budget is spent or the run does not replay, *then* the phase *shall* report itself inconclusive with its reason, and the pipeline *shall* continue to the fixpoint query.
The phase *shall not* report `Proven`, and *shall not* read an `unsat` answer as a proof.

*If* the phase ends without a run, *then* the pipeline *shall* continue as it does without the phase, and the phase *shall* change no verdict except through the time it spends against the total budget of [VER-013].
**Option.**
The witness depth *shall* default to 8 in every implementation.
*When* the caller sets the witness depth to a positive `n`, the phase *shall* ask one query at depth `n`.
*If* the caller sets a negative witness depth, *then* setting it *shall* fail with the argument error `witnessDepth must be non-negative, got <n>`.

A language whose depth type has no negative value has no such error. Only depth 8 is cheap: a larger depth costs up to the phase budget on every query that has no short run, each `Proven` one included.
**Scripts and dump.**
*When* `LIBPETRI_SMT_DUMP` is set, the verifier *shall* keep the phase's script and reply under the phase name `witness` ([VER-013]).

*When* the scripts are encoded without a solver ([VER-013] AC1), the result *shall* carry as its `witness` member the script `verify()` sends when it reaches the phase, present exactly when the encoding is flat, the witness depth is positive, and the net has no match transitions or the property is a reachability-safety property with a budget place declared, and absent otherwise.
The member follows these gates alone: it is present whether or not an earlier phase, an earlier route or a refusal (an unresolved property place among them) would end `verify()` before the phase.

Measured on a 169-place net with 18 bounded injected places (z3 4.16.0): three violations need runs of 7 steps with one or two injections. Depth 8 finds each in 0.15 to 0.25 s, where the fixpoint query took 57 to 272 s, and every model is 8 steps long before the trim. A depth-8 query with no run costs 0.15 to 0.32 s. Where no run exists, depth 12 costs up to 3.7 s and depth 16 up to 120 s, so a depth above 8 is opt-in.

notes.text:
- Java: `org.libpetri.smt.z3.BoundedRun` (`encodeBoundedRun`, `decodeBoundedRun`, `replayRun` and the phase driver); `SmtVerifier.witnessDepth(int)`; `encodeScripts().witness()`.
- TypeScript: `verification/z3/bounded-run`; `SmtVerifier.witnessDepth(n)`; `encodeScripts().witness` (`string | null`). A non-integer depth fails with `witnessDepth must be an integer, got <n>`; the other languages' depth types hold integers only.
- Rust: behind the `z3` feature, `bounded_run`; `SmtVerifier::witness_depth(usize)`; `encode_scripts().witness` (`Option<String>`).
- Python: `verify(..., witness_depth=8)`; `encode_smt_scripts(..., witness_depth=8)["witness"]`. The negative-depth error names the option as Python spells it: `witness_depth must be non-negative, got <n>`.
- The goldens `spec/verification-fixtures/scripts/<id>/witness.smt2` are written by the Rust verifier (`scripts/smt-script-parity.py --update`), never by hand.

A class holds a state when the class's marking is the state's marking and its firing domain holds every combination of firing times the state allows the class's clocks. A class is well formed when its clocks are the transitions enabled in its marking and its firing domain has the form letting time pass leaves: the closure of a matrix with a finite reference bound in which every clock's lower bound is zero. For a well-formed class that holds a state, the class's clocks are the state's enabled transitions.
*When* a timed run of the net reaches a state, the state class graph *shall* hold a class, reachable from its initial class, that holds the state.

Every class the state class graph reaches from its initial class *shall* be well formed and *shall* list its clocks once each, in ascending order of transition name compared by Unicode code point ([VER-013]).

*When* a transition can fire with one of its outcomes ([VER-001]) from a state in which no enabled transition is past its latest firing time, and a well-formed class holds that state, the state class graph *shall* give that class a successor, labelled with the transition's name and the outcome's index, that holds the state the firing leaves.

Every successor of a class *shall* be labelled with the name of a transition among the class's clocks and the index of one of that transition's outcomes, and *shall* have the marking that firing the transition with that outcome leaves: each input place less the `consumptionCount(available)` of [IO-007], so an `All` or `AtLeast` input empties its place, each reset place emptied, and the outcome's tokens added.

*When* a transition `t` fires from marking `M` into marking `M'`, the successor step of the state class graph *shall* keep the clock of a transition `t'` enabled in `M` exactly when `t'` is not `t` and is enabled both in `M'` and in the intermediate marking `M - Pre(t)`, which has the inputs of `t` consumed, its reset places drained and none of its outputs deposited.

The canonical order of the state class graph *shall* either keep a list of transitions or return a permutation of its positions, and *shall* leave every list it is given in ascending order of transition name, compared by Unicode code point ([VER-013]).

*If* the transition names of the net are unique, *then* the class key of the state class graph *shall* give two classes, each with the transitions enabled in its marking as clocks, once each in that order, and a canonical firing domain (closed, zero on the diagonal, every clock with a finite lower bound), the same key exactly when they have the same marking and their firing domains hold the same firing times.

A net may give two transitions one name ([CORE-021]); the key sentence does not reach such a net, since an order by name cannot tell two enabling orders of one name apart. These sentences speak of the successor's soundness: a class holds every state the firing rule allows. That a class holds no state a timed run cannot reach is the exact half of the successor, not stated here, and so is the exact half of the fresh interval a newly enabled clock gets.

requirements.body:
The engine may support state class graph construction using the Berthomieu-Diaz (1991) algorithm. State classes combine a marking with a Difference Bound Matrix (DBM) representing timing constraints on enabled transitions.

An implementation that offers the graph is bound by the sentences below. In them a timed run of the net starts at an initial marking with every clock at zero, on a net in which no transition's earliest firing time is below zero or above its latest, and follows the Time Petri net semantics: time may pass only as far as no enabled transition goes past its latest firing time, a transition fires no earlier than its earliest firing time and deposits its outputs at the instant it fires, and a clock is kept or restarted by the persistence rule below. A class holds a state when the class's marking is the state's marking and its firing domain holds every combination of firing times the state allows the class's clocks. A class is well formed when its clocks are the transitions enabled in its marking and its firing domain has the form letting time pass leaves: the closure of a matrix with a finite reference bound in which every clock's lower bound is zero. For a well-formed class that holds a state, the class's clocks are the state's enabled transitions.

*When* a timed run of the net reaches a state, the state class graph *shall* hold a class, reachable from its initial class, that holds the state.

Every class the state class graph reaches from its initial class *shall* be well formed and *shall* list its clocks once each, in ascending order of transition name compared by Unicode code point ([VER-013]).

*When* a transition can fire with one of its outcomes ([VER-001]) from a state in which no enabled transition is past its latest firing time, and a well-formed class holds that state, the state class graph *shall* give that class a successor, labelled with the transition's name and the outcome's index, that holds the state the firing leaves.

Every successor of a class *shall* be labelled with the name of a transition among the class's clocks and the index of one of that transition's outcomes, and *shall* have the marking that firing the transition with that outcome leaves: each input place less the `consumptionCount(available)` of [IO-007], so an `All` or `AtLeast` input empties its place, each reset place emptied, and the outcome's tokens added.

*When* a transition `t` fires from marking `M` into marking `M'`, the successor step of the state class graph *shall* keep the clock of a transition `t'` enabled in `M` exactly when `t'` is not `t` and is enabled both in `M'` and in the intermediate marking `M - Pre(t)`, which has the inputs of `t` consumed, its reset places drained and none of its outputs deposited.

The canonical order of the state class graph *shall* either keep a list of transitions or return a permutation of its positions, and *shall* leave every list it is given in ascending order of transition name, compared by Unicode code point ([VER-013]).

*If* the transition names of the net are unique, *then* the class key of the state class graph *shall* give two classes, each with the transitions enabled in its marking as clocks, once each in that order, and a canonical firing domain (closed, zero on the diagonal, every clock with a finite lower bound), the same key exactly when they have the same marking and their firing domains hold the same firing times.

When every bound of the net is a whole number of milliseconds, the successor step of [VER-011] leaves every firing domain canonical, so two classes that step builds on a net with unique names are one exactly when they have the same marking and the same firing domain, whatever interleavings reached them. A net may give two transitions one name ([CORE-021]); the key sentence does not reach such a net, since an order by name cannot tell two enabling orders of one name apart. These sentences speak of the successor's soundness: a class holds every state the firing rule allows. That a class holds no state a timed run cannot reach is the exact half of the successor, not stated here, and so is the exact half of the fresh interval a newly enabled clock gets.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. State class graph enumerates reachable (marking, timing zone) pairs. A class's identity is
   its marking and its **full** firing domain, independent of the order in which its
   transitions became enabled: the successor step lays clocks out persistent-then-newly-
   enabled, which is path-dependent, so implementations MUST put every class's clocks in one
   canonical order (ascending transition name, in the code-point order of [VER-013]) and key
   on the complete difference-bound matrix ([VER-011]), not on the per-clock projections
   alone. Two arrivals at the same marking and zone by different interleavings are one class;
   two zones that agree on every projection but differ in a difference constraint are two. On
   an untimed workflow net the order-sensitive key inflated the class count 1.5× (one marking
   held by fourteen classes); the projection-only key merges classes whose successors differ,
   which can lose a reachable marking.
2. Successor computation correctly handles transition firing and clock updates. The
   number of tokens a firing removes from each input place MUST be the canonical
   `consumptionCount(available)` of [IO-007] — the same function the executor uses —
   and not the enablement threshold `requiredCount()`. In particular `All` and
   `AtLeast(m)` drain the place.
3. Every outcome of a transition, each XOR branch and a timeout outcome that deposits
   differently from every branch, is expanded into a virtual transition of its own
   ([VER-001]), and a successor is labelled with the fired transition's name and the
   outcome's index, counting the outcomes in the order in which [VER-001] numbers the
   `_b<i>` virtual transitions: the branches in enumeration order, then the timeout outcome.
4. Clock persistence uses the intermediate marking of Berthomieu and Diaz. After `t` fires
   from marking `M`, a transition `t' ≠ t` keeps its clock only if it is enabled in `M`, in
   the successor marking `M'`, and in the intermediate marking `M - Pre(t)`: inputs
   consumed, reset places drained, outputs not yet deposited. Every other transition
   enabled in `M'` gets a fresh firing interval. This is the executor's rule ([TIME-012])
   for an on-time executor with atomic firings, one that reaps no transition, fires none
   after its latest bound, and gives an action no duration, the assumptions [VER-023] lists;
   the enablement recheck of a firing pass ([EXEC-003] AC3) is part of atomic firings.
   A successor that keeps a clock the executor restarts under-approximates the executor's
   behaviors. A transition outside the in-flight split of [VER-004] fires atomically and
   takes no time (a split one completes through its immediate completion step at any later
   time). Under `alwaysAvailable` an environment input never disables a transition, and under
   `bounded(k)` only one that demands more than `k` tokens does, permanently ([VER-006] AC3).
5. The graph builder (`StateClassGraph.build` in every language) builds the graph of the net it
   is given and does not apply the in-flight split itself. A caller that builds the graph
   directly, outside `SmtVerifier`, MUST apply the split first (`splitInFlight` in TypeScript,
   `in_flight::split_in_flight` in Rust, `InFlight.split` in Java) to get the executor's
   two-step firing ([VER-004]); when the split is refused, no graph of this kind is faithful to
   the executor. The builder's documentation MUST say so.

**Depends on:** [IO-007], [EXEC-010], [TIME-012], [TIME-013], [VER-001], [VER-004], [VER-011],
[VER-013]

- TypeScript: Full implementation
- Rust: Full implementation (`libpetri-verification` `state_class_graph`)

requirements.title: DBM Zone Representation
requirements.testDerivation: Create DBM for 3 timed transitions; fire one; verify successor zone constraints.

spans.text: *When* the zone library creates a zone from one lower and one upper bound per clock, the zone *shall* hold exactly the firing times that lie between the bounds of each clock.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: Canonicalising a zone *shall not* change the firing times it holds.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *When* a zone holds some firing times, its canonical matrix *shall* be closed: no bound exceeds the sum of the two bounds of a detour through any clock of the matrix, the reference clock included.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: The zone library *shall* report a zone empty only when it holds no firing times.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *If* every finite bound of a zone is a whole number of milliseconds and every clock, the reference clock included, has a finite lower bound, *then* the zone library *shall* report the zone empty exactly when it holds no firing times.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: *When* a transition fires from a zone, the successor zone, with the persistent clocks first in the order given and the newly enabled clocks after them, *shall* hold every firing time the firing rule allows: the fired clock is not later than any other clock, each persistent clock keeps the time it had left after the fired clock, and each newly enabled clock lies between its static bounds.
spans.label: s6

spans.text: *When* the clocks of a zone that holds some firing times are permuted, the zone library *shall* keep the reference clock first, move every other bound of the matrix with its two clocks, and write zero as the bound of the reference clock against itself.
spans.label: s7

requirements.body:
Timing constraints within a state class are represented as a Difference Bound Matrix (DBM), encoding constraints of the form `θᵢ - θⱼ ≤ cᵢⱼ` where θᵢ is the firing time of transition i: the time from entering the class until it fires.

*When* the zone library creates a zone from one lower and one upper bound per clock, the zone *shall* hold exactly the firing times that lie between the bounds of each clock.

Canonicalising a zone *shall not* change the firing times it holds.

*When* a zone holds some firing times, its canonical matrix *shall* be closed: no bound exceeds the sum of the two bounds of a detour through any clock of the matrix, the reference clock included.

The zone library *shall* report a zone empty only when it holds no firing times.

*If* every finite bound of a zone is a whole number of milliseconds and every clock, the reference clock included, has a finite lower bound, *then* the zone library *shall* report the zone empty exactly when it holds no firing times.

*When* a transition fires from a zone, the successor zone, with the persistent clocks first in the order given and the newly enabled clocks after them, *shall* hold every firing time the firing rule allows: the fired clock is not later than any other clock, each persistent clock keeps the time it had left after the fired clock, and each newly enabled clock lies between its static bounds.

*When* the clocks of a zone that holds some firing times are permuted, the zone library *shall* keep the reference clock first, move every other bound of the matrix with its two clocks, and write zero as the bound of the reference clock against itself.

*If* two zones each hold some firing times and every finite bound of both is a whole number of milliseconds, *then* their dedup keys *shall* be equal exactly when their matrices are equal entry by entry, the bounds between two clocks included.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. DBM encodes lower and upper bounds for each transition clock.
2. Zone emptiness is detectable (unsatisfiable constraints).
3. Successor DBM is computed correctly after transition firing.
4. The zone exposes a dedup key over its full canonical matrix (every `θᵢ - θⱼ` bound, not
   only the diagonal projections), and a permutation of its clocks that reorders the matrix
   with them; equality is positional over the canonical order ([VER-010] AC1). The key renders
   each finite bound to the millisecond, so on zones that hold some firing times it is exact
   when every finite bound is a whole number of milliseconds.

**Depends on:** [VER-010]

- Java: Full implementation
- TypeScript: Full implementation
- Rust: Full implementation (`libpetri-verification` `dbm`)

paragraphs.text: The state class graph ([VER-010]) MAY be made **ν-aware** to decide [NU-020] join correlation *exactly* — the [NU-050] **Route B** carve-out. Each correlation token carries an abstract, interchangeable name-symbol; a matched (ν-join) transition is enabled only when one symbol is shared by every correlated input (not merely when the token counts allow); a minting fork introduces a globally-fresh symbol; and the graph is quotiented under name-permutation symmetry (its dedup key abstracts the symbol identities). The timed firing domain ([VER-011]) is carried beside the name partition, with a matched join's clock gated by name-enablement ([NU-050]) and, unless `assumeNoReaping` is set, without latest bounds ([TIME-013]); the Route B class key pairs the base class (for a timed net its marking, zone and earliest-ready times) with the canonical key of the name layer. Quiescence ([NU-050]) is decided over the name-aware terminal classes.

*When* the Route B graph fires a ν-join on a name-symbol, every correlated input *shall* hold at least the required count of that symbol, and the firing *shall* remove the required count of that symbol from each correlated input and add one token of it to each relay target of the fired branch ([NU-054]). *If* every correlated input of a ν-join holds at least the required count of a name-symbol, *then* the name successors of a firing of that join *shall* include one with the canonical key of the join fired on that symbol. *When* the Route B graph fires a coloured consumer ([NU-051]), it *shall* fire it on a name-symbol its coloured input holds, removing one token of that symbol from the input and adding one token of it to each coloured output of the fired branch. *If* the coloured input of a coloured consumer holds a name-symbol, *then* the name successors of a firing of that consumer *shall* include one with the canonical key of the consumer fired on that symbol. *When* the Route B graph fires a minting transition, its one name successor *shall* add one token of a name-symbol that no coloured place of the class holds to each coloured output of the fired branch. *When* the Route B graph fires a transition that neither mints, joins nor consumes a name-symbol, its one name successor *shall* be the name layer of the class unchanged. Two name layers *shall* have the same canonical key exactly when one is the other with its name-symbols renamed by a permutation. The Route B graph *shall* identify two classes exactly when they have the same base class and their name layers have the same canonical key. *When* the Route B graph fires a transition, the successor *shall* hold on each place the transition does not reset the tokens the place held, less the tokens the transition's input on that place consumes by [IO-007] (all of them for an `All` or `AtLeast` input), plus the tokens the fired branch deposits there.

The executor fires a ν-join on one of the names that enable it ([NU-020]); the graph fires it on each of them, up to renaming, and a coloured consumer ([NU-051]) on each resident name. Route B's successor step gives any two classes with the same key the same transition labels and successor keys, up to order, so the premise of the completeness sentence below holds for it.

Every class the Route B build stores *shall* be reachable in the graph from the initial class, whether the build closed, was truncated, was stopped or stopped early. *If* the Route B build closes, *then* it *shall* have expanded every class it stored. *While* the graph's successor step gives any two classes with the same key the same transition labels and successor keys, up to order, *if* the Route B build closes, *then* it *shall* have stored a class with the key of every class the graph reaches from the initial class. *If* the Route B build stops early at a violating class of a reachability-safety property, *then* its verdict for that property *shall* be the verdict of the same build without the early stop, unless that build is stopped by the total budget or a cancellation. *If* the Route B build stops early, *then* it *shall not* report the graph as closed.

**Exactness precondition (consumption model).** The soundness and completeness of criterion 3 are not unconditional: they hold only while the graph's successor relation removes as many tokens from each place as the executor would. The successor step MUST derive each input's token count from the canonical `consumptionCount(available)` of [IO-007] (so `All` and `AtLeast(m)` consume **all** available tokens, not merely `requiredCount()`). Which names the removed tokens carry is the graph's free choice, where the executor takes the oldest ([EXEC-010], [NU-020]), so criterion 3 claims completeness only for the graph's own name semantics. A successor relation that consumes a *minimum* instead leaves phantom residue in the source place; that residue keeps inhibitor arcs on the place unsatisfied and suppresses successor classes, so a genuinely reachable marking is reported unreachable — an **unsound** `Proven`, not a conservative one. Implementations therefore MUST delegate to the same cardinality contract the executor uses rather than restating it.

notes.text:
- Rust: Full implementation (`libpetri-verification` `name_state_class_graph` / `nu_scg_verifier`); the canonical name-partition key format is shared verbatim.
- Java: Full implementation (`org.libpetri.analysis.NameStateClassGraph` / `org.libpetri.smt.NuScgVerifier`).
- TypeScript: Full implementation (`verification/analysis/name-state-class-graph` / `verification/nu-scg-verifier`).
- Python: inherits the Rust analysis through `verify`.
- Memory: an implementation MAY intern (hash-cons) the base class and the name layer between state classes. The base intern key MUST include the class-relative earliest-ready times alongside the marking and zone, because the [NU-052] prune reads them while class equality does not. Class identity MUST carry them too: the graph's dedup key is the pair of intern ids (base, name layer), not the class object, so two arrivals that agree on marking, zone and name layer but disagree on the earliest-ready times stay two classes and each keeps its own prune input. Interning is semantics-free by key-equivariance of the successor step (Lean `Interning.lean`, `interned_keys_eq`): the reachable quotient and the verdict are unchanged; class indices and the reported counterexample trace may differ from a non-interned build.
- Successor emission (orbit dedup): a join yields one successor per **distinct signature** among its enabling symbols, not one per symbol; a symbol's signature is its count vector over the coloured places in `colouredOrder`, and the consume role ([NU-051]) is deduplicated the same way. Two symbols with equal signatures are exchanged by a transposition that fixes the name marking, so their successors have equal canonical keys: the class set and the set of (label, key) successor pairs are unchanged, and only parallel identical edges disappear. The per-symbol emission copied and keyed every successor only to collapse them into one class, which made join-heavy graphs roughly quadratic in their class count. Measured in TypeScript on PNID Fig. 11(b): 8 000 classes in 0.49 s instead of 14.5 s; 100 000 classes in about 19 s instead of an estimated 35 min. Class counts and verdicts are unchanged, and so is the discovery order when each signature is represented by its first enabling symbol; a count of edges is not a stable quantity to test. The renaming-equivariance that Lean `Interning.lean` assumes per role still holds, because the number of distinct signatures is itself invariant under renaming.
- Early stop (AC5) is Route B only: the [VER-017] enumeration and the [VER-023] timed check still build their graphs in full, since those feed the state-space cache and other properties. An early-stopped build is a BFS prefix, so every class in it is reachable, by the argument of Lean `build_reach` for the enumeration route.
- The counterexample path is read from per-class labelled successor lists, not by scanning every edge for each dequeued class.
- Solver-free (no Z3); the verifier prefers Route A's bounded name-colouring for budget-declared untimed reachability-safety and uses this route for quiescence, budget-less, and timed ν-nets.

**Conditional on an executor-faithful consumption model** (see below): when the graph closes within the class bound the verdict for reachability-safety and quiescence is sound for every executor run ([NU-050]) and complete for the free-choice name semantics the graph explores: every class the graph reaches is stored and expanded, so a property that a class the graph reaches violates is `Violated`, and a `Violated` names a class the graph reaches. When that graph keeps a latest bound (under `assumeNoReaping`, or a direct call on a timed net) it reads each firing as one instant step, so the verdict is exact only for an on-time executor whose actions take no time, and the report says so ([VER-004] AC3). A graph that does not close within the class bound truncates (NU-050 #2 — undecidability surfaces as truncation) and the shared predicate runs over the explored prefix by the rule of [VER-017] ("Verdicts from a truncated graph"): a safety property violated by any stored class, or a quiescence property violated by an **expanded** class with no successor, is `Violated` with the shortest witness in the explored graph and a report line naming the truncation; otherwise the verdict is `Unknown`. A truncated graph never yields `Proven`, and a reachability-safety `Unknown` from Route B is still final (the dispatcher has no fallback for it), so the prefix check is what turns a shallow violation into a verdict. PNID Fig. 11(b) (`research/net-metrics/validation/pnid/`), `placeBound(order_clerk, 2)` at a class bound of 50: `Violated` with the depth-3 trace `create_order ×3`.

`All` and `AtLeast(m)` inputs drain their place in the graph exactly as they do at run time: after a successor step the source place holds no residue, so an inhibitor arc on that place is satisfied in the successor class.

**Early stop for safety properties.** For a reachability-safety property (`PlaceBound`, `BranchPlaceBound`, `Unreachable` and `MutualExclusion`, the safety set of [VER-017]'s "Verdicts from a truncated graph", and `NameAligned` of [NU-055]) the build checks each class with the same shared predicate as it is discovered and stops at the first violating class. BFS discovers classes in index order, so that class is the lowest-index violating class — the one the check over a full or truncated graph selects — and its path is the shortest; verdict and route are identical to a build without the early stop and the witness ends at the same class; only the class count, the time and, among equally short paths to that class, the path the witness takes may differ. When the stop comes before the class bound, the report note `Note: Route B stopped at the first violating class after N classes (VER-012). Every explored class is reachable and classes are discovered breadth-first, so the counterexample is a real firing sequence and a shortest one to any violation.` replaces both the truncation note and the exact-graph note, and the parent whose expansion discovered the violating class does not count as expanded; when the bound is hit first, criterion 3 applies unchanged. Quiescence properties do not stop early (they need expanded classes). An early-stopped graph is not complete and MUST NOT be treated as closed. PNID Fig. 11(b), `placeBound(order_clerk, 2)` at the default class bound: `Violated` with `create_order ×3` after a handful of classes, where it took 1.8 s to fill the cap first.

paragraphs.text: The flat encoders decide the untimed abstraction ([VER-004]), so a `Violated` on a timed net can rest on a run the timing forbids. A call that answers within `window(0, 2)`, raced by a watchdog that fires after `delayed(5)`, never times out; `unreachable(TIMEOUT)` is nevertheless `Violated` by the SMT pipeline, with `counterexampleConfirmed` true, because the trace `start, watchdog` replays in the untimed abstraction. Until [VER-003]'s `counterexampleTiming`, the only signal was a warning line in the report. An implementation SHOULD offer an opt-in **timed check** that asks the timed state-class graph about such a counterexample. It is off by default.
**When it runs.** The option is on, the verdict is `Violated`, and:
Otherwise `counterexampleTiming` keeps the value [VER-003] gives it without the check: `UNTIMED_NET`, `TIMED_EXACT` or `UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION`.

**What it does.** Build the **timed** state-class graph of [VER-010] (firing domains kept) from the same net, initial marking and terminal rewrite ([EXEC-042]) the other routes use, under the class budget of [VER-017] and the total budget of [VER-013] when one is set, and decide the same property over its classes with the same shared predicate the enumeration route and Route B use ([VER-017]), with the same sinks and conditional sinks ([VER-014]). The check does not read or write a state-space cache ([VER-017]): the cache holds untimed graphs. It runs once, as a wrapper at the end of `verify()`, after every route has spoken.

The graph is **priority-blind**: like every state-class graph of [VER-010], it expands each enabled transition whatever its priority. What the check decides is therefore the timed semantics without priority: a violating class shows a timing-feasible run, not one the executor's priority-ordered scheduling ([EXEC-003]) must allow, while a closed graph without one also excludes every prioritized run, since priority only removes runs.

For the quiescence properties the predicate reads "this class has no successor" as "no transition can ever fire again", and, on a net with a reapable transition, also treats a class whose enabled transitions are all reapable as resting ([VER-002]). The graph itself fires every transition on time: it does not hold the runs a late executor takes after a reap, so `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING` there means that no on-time run reaches a violating rest. On a timed graph that MUST still hold: a class with an enabled transition has a successor whatever its interval, so a `delayed(5)` transition, whose interval `[5, ∞)` has no upper bound, still fires out of its class. A graph that dropped such a class's successors would report a timed deadlock that the net does not have. On the [VER-002] AC11 witness the check is `TIMED_CONFIRMED` with the empty trace.
**Outcomes.**

- The graph reaches a violating class: `TIMED_CONFIRMED`. The counterexample trace and its transitions are **replaced** by the shortest path from the initial class to a violating class (the first one the breadth-first build stored, [VER-017]), a run of the timed semantics **ignoring priority** (the graph of [VER-010] does not order transitions by priority), and the report says the trace came from the timed graph. The run is timing-feasible, not necessarily one the executor takes: when priority is what keeps the executor off the trace (a higher-priority transition always wins the conflict, e.g. `hi: A → OK` at priority 10 and `lo: A → BAD` at priority 0, both `delayed(1)`, under `unreachable(BAD)`), the result is still `TIMED_CONFIRMED` with the trace `lo`. The path is an ordered firing sequence, so `counterexampleConfirmed` reports it confirmed, as for [VER-017] AC2.
- The graph closes and no class violates: `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING`. The property holds under timing. The untimed trace is kept, and the report says plainly that the counterexample is spurious under timing, with the class count. The report MUST also say what that timed claim assumes: an on-time executor with atomic firings, one that reaps no transition, fires none after its latest bound, and gives an action no duration. A late executor can still reach the counterexample (Lean `TimedScg/Retrodict.reaping_escapes_timed_graph`: `t1: p → a` at `window(3, 5)`, `t2: p → b` at `delayed(10)`, `unreachable(b)` is `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING` while an executor blocked past 5 ms reaps `t1` and marks `b`), and so can an action long enough for other firings to interleave with it.
- The graph is truncated at the class budget and its explored prefix violates the property, by the rule of [VER-017] ("Verdicts from a truncated graph": any stored class for a safety property, only expanded classes that rest for a quiescence property, a class resting when it has no successor or every transition it enables is reapable, [VER-002]): `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, the trace replaced by the shortest path in the explored graph, and the report says the timed graph was truncated at `N` classes and the violation found in its prefix.
- The graph is truncated at the class budget with no violation in its prefix, or stopped by the total budget or by cancellation ([VER-013]): `TIMED_UNDECIDED`, and the report says which. `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING` needs a **closed** graph and never comes from a prefix.

**Why it never changes a verdict.** [VER-004] makes the untimed claim the contract: `Proven` means the property holds for every run of the untimed abstraction, which implies it for every timed run. A closed timed graph with no violation establishes only the weaker, timed claim, and [VER-017] condition 3 forbids a route to return a weaker claim than the route it replaces, which is why the enumeration route skips timed nets altogether. Turning the `Violated` into `Proven` would be exactly that substitution; turning it into `Unknown` would withdraw a verdict that is correct under the contract. The timed claim also rests on the on-time, atomic executor above, which the executor does not guarantee. So the timed check annotates. `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING` with verdict `Violated` is not a contradiction: the untimed abstraction violates the property, and the timed net does not. The verdict, the route and the invariants are unchanged; under `TIMED_CONFIRMED` the trace, its transitions and `counterexampleConfirmed` are replaced, and under the other two outcomes they are kept. With the option off, the result and the report are byte-identical to those of a verifier that does not offer the check.
**The check, as EARS sentences.**

The verifier *shall* run the timed check exactly when the option is on, the verdict is `Violated`, some transition of the verified net is not `immediate`, no environment place is still registered on the verified net (the `Arrivals` rewrite of [VER-006] removes them), the net declares no match transition, and the route that decided is not Route B ([VER-012]).
*If* the build of the timed graph is stopped by the total budget or cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* the timed check *shall* answer `TIMED_UNDECIDED`.

*While* the build is neither stopped by the total budget nor cancelled, the timed check *shall* answer `TIMED_CONFIRMED` when a counted class of the timed graph violates the property, a counted class being any stored class for a safety property and a class the builder expanded for a quiescence property.
*When* the timed graph is closed and no class of it violates the property, the timed check *shall* answer `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING`.
*When* the timed graph is truncated at the class budget and no counted class of it violates the property, the timed check *shall* answer `TIMED_UNDECIDED`.

*When* the timed check answers `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, the path it reports *shall* lead, in the timed graph it built, from the initial class to the first class, in the order the builder stored the classes, that is counted and violates the property, and *shall* be no longer than any other path of that graph from the initial class to that class.
*If* the timed check does not run, *then* the verifier *shall* leave the result unchanged, its `counterexampleTiming` at the value [VER-003] gives it.
*When* the timed check runs, the verifier *shall* leave the verdict, the route and the reported P-invariants unchanged.

*When* the timed check answers `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, the verifier *shall* report `counterexampleTiming` `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, replace the counterexample's transitions by those of the path the check reports, and report `counterexampleConfirmed` as `true`.
*When* the timed check answers `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING`, the verifier *shall* report it as `counterexampleTiming` and keep the counterexample's transitions and `counterexampleConfirmed`.
*When* the timed check answers `TIMED_UNDECIDED`, the verifier *shall* report it as `counterexampleTiming` and keep the counterexample's transitions and `counterexampleConfirmed`.
**The timed graph, as EARS sentences.**
*While* every finite bound of the net is a whole number of milliseconds, a class of the timed graph *shall* have no successor exactly when its marking enables no transition.
*When* the timed graph is closed and no class of it violates a safety property, the property *shall* hold on every marking that an on-time run with atomic firings reaches from the initial marking.

*When* the timed graph is closed and no class of it violates a quiescence property, the property *shall* hold on every resting marking that an on-time run with atomic firings reaches from the initial marking, a marking resting when every transition it enables is reapable ([VER-002], [TIME-013]), which under `assumeNoReaping` means when it enables none.

notes.text:
- Java: `SmtVerifier.timedCounterexampleCheck(boolean)`; the graph is `StateClassGraph.build(..., Options.TIMED)`, the predicate `GraphDecision.decideOverClasses`.
- TypeScript: `SmtVerifier.timedCounterexampleCheck(on: boolean)`; the graph is built with `{ untimed: false }`, the predicate `decideOverClasses` (`verification/graph-decision`).
- Rust: `SmtVerifier::timed_counterexample_check(bool)`; the graph is built with `StateClassGraph::build_with_options`, the predicate `graph_decision::decide_over_classes`.
- Python: `verify(..., timed_counterexample_check=False)`.

The flat encoders decide the untimed abstraction ([VER-004]), so a `Violated` on a timed net can
rest on a run the timing forbids. A call that answers within `window(0, 2)`, raced by a watchdog
that fires after `delayed(5)`, never times out; `unreachable(TIMEOUT)` is nevertheless
`Violated` by the SMT pipeline, with `counterexampleConfirmed` true, because the trace

the only signal was a warning line in the report. An implementation SHOULD offer an opt-in
**timed check** that asks the timed state-class graph about such a counterexample. It is off by
default.

**When it runs.** The option is on, the verdict is `Violated`, and:

1. the net is timed (some transition is not `immediate`, [VER-017] condition 3);
2. no environment places are registered, since the graph does not model injection ([VER-006],
   [VER-017] condition 2); under the `Arrivals` mode of [VER-006] the net is closed before any
   route and has none, so the check runs on the closed net;
3. the net declares no match (ν-join) transitions. The state-class graph is name-blind: it fires a
   join on tokens whose names differ and misses the quiescent markings of a join that never
   matches ([VER-017] condition 1, [VER-022]), so neither its violation nor its closure would
   mean anything about the net. A timed ν-net is normally decided by Route B, which is already
   `TIMED_EXACT`;
4. the deciding route is not already `TIMED_EXACT`.

Otherwise `counterexampleTiming` keeps the value [VER-003] gives it without the check:
`UNTIMED_NET`, `TIMED_EXACT` or `UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION`.

out of its class. A graph that dropped such a class's successors would report a timed deadlock
that the net does not have. On the [VER-002] AC11 witness the check is `TIMED_CONFIRMED` with the empty trace.

**Outcomes.**
- The graph reaches a violating class: `TIMED_CONFIRMED`. The counterexample trace and its
  transitions are **replaced** by the shortest path from the initial class to a violating class
  (the first one the breadth-first build stored, [VER-017]), a run of the timed semantics
  **ignoring priority** (the graph of [VER-010] does not order transitions by priority), and the
  report says the trace came from the timed graph. The run is
  timing-feasible, not necessarily one the executor takes: when priority is what keeps the
  executor off the trace (a higher-priority transition always wins the conflict, e.g.
  `hi: A → OK` at priority 10 and `lo: A → BAD` at priority 0, both `delayed(1)`, under
  `unreachable(BAD)`), the result is still `TIMED_CONFIRMED` with the trace `lo`. The path is an
  ordered firing sequence, so `counterexampleConfirmed` reports it confirmed, as for [VER-017]

- The graph closes and no class violates: `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING`. The property holds under
  timing. The untimed trace is kept, and the report says plainly that the counterexample is
  spurious under timing, with the class count. The report MUST also say what that timed claim
  assumes: an on-time executor with atomic firings, one that reaps no transition, fires none
  after its latest bound, and gives an action no duration. A late executor can still reach the

  property, only expanded classes that rest for a quiescence property, a class resting when it
  has no successor or every transition it enables is reapable, [VER-002]):
  `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, the trace replaced by the shortest path in the explored graph, and the
  report says the timed graph was truncated at `N` classes and the violation found in its prefix.

*When* the timed graph is truncated at the class budget and no counted class of it violates the property, the timed check *shall* answer `TIMED_UNDECIDED`.

*When* the timed check answers `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, the path it reports *shall* lead, in the timed graph it built, from the initial class to the first class, in the order the builder stored the classes, that is counted and violates the property, and *shall* be no longer than any other path of that graph from the initial class to that class.

*If* the timed check does not run, *then* the verifier *shall* leave the result unchanged, its `counterexampleTiming` at the value [VER-003] gives it.

*When* the timed check runs, the verifier *shall* leave the verdict, the route and the reported P-invariants unchanged.

*When* the timed check answers `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, the verifier *shall* report `counterexampleTiming` `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, replace the counterexample's transitions by those of the path the check reports, and report `counterexampleConfirmed` as `true`.

*When* the timed check answers `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING`, the verifier *shall* report it as `counterexampleTiming` and keep the counterexample's transitions and `counterexampleConfirmed`.

*When* the timed check answers `TIMED_UNDECIDED`, the verifier *shall* report it as `counterexampleTiming` and keep the counterexample's transitions and `counterexampleConfirmed`.

**The timed graph, as EARS sentences.**

*While* every finite bound of the net is a whole number of milliseconds, a class of the timed graph *shall* have no successor exactly when its marking enables no transition.

*When* the timed graph is closed and no class of it violates a safety property, the property *shall* hold on every marking that an on-time run with atomic firings reaches from the initial marking.

*When* the timed graph is closed and no class of it violates a quiescence property, the property *shall* hold on every resting marking that an on-time run with atomic firings reaches from the initial marking, a marking resting when every transition it enables is reapable ([VER-002], [TIME-013]), which under `assumeNoReaping` means when it enables none.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. The watchdog net (`start: REQ → CALLING`; `answer: CALLING → RESP`, `window(0, 2)`;
   `watchdog: CALLING → TIMEOUT`, `delayed(5)`; one token on `REQ`) under
   `unreachable(TIMEOUT)`: with the check off the result is `Violated`, `UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION`;
   with it on it is `Violated`, `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING`, and the report names the class count.
2. The same net with the watchdog at `delayed(1)`: `Violated`, `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, and the trace
   is the timed graph's shortest path `start, watchdog`.
3. Quiescence on the timed graph. `S → d → X` with `d` at `delayed(5)` and one token on `S`,
   under `deadlockFree` with no sinks: `Violated`, `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, and the replaced trace is
   `d`, not the empty run; the class holding `S` is not a deadlock, because `d` still fires out
   of it. `S → start → A`, `fast: A → DONE` at `window(0, 2)`, `slow: A → STUCK` at
   `delayed(5)`, `DONE` a sink: `Violated` untimed, `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING` with the check on.
4. A class budget below the timed graph's size gives `TIMED_UNDECIDED` when the explored prefix
   holds no violating class; so does a total budget that runs out during the check. When the
   prefix does hold one, the result is `TIMED_CONFIRMED` with the report naming the truncation:
   an unbounded timed producer `gen: G → G, A` at `delayed(1)`, one token on `G`, under
   `placeBound(A, 2)` with a class budget of 50 never closes, and its prefix holds `A = 3` after
   `gen, gen, gen`.
5. With environment places registered under a mode other than `Arrivals` ([VER-006]), or with
   match transitions, the check does not run and the value is `UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION`; a Route B

paragraphs.text: The engine may support structural analysis of siphons (sets of places that, once empty, stay empty) and traps (sets of places that, once marked, stay marked).

**Commoner's theorem governs ORDINARY nets only.** The siphon and trap fixpoints are computed from the pre/post vectors, so they model a net in which the sole reason a transition is disabled is an input place holding too few tokens. A read arc, an inhibitor arc, a reset arc, a consume-all input or an input arc weight above one is a disablement the fixpoints do not see, and dropping it yields a strictly **more permissive** net, the wrong direction for a deadlock proof. An implementation that converts a siphon/trap result into a `Proven` verdict MUST therefore refuse to do so for any net carrying one of them, exactly as it already refuses when sinks are declared or environment places are registered on the net it decides. Three witnesses, each a net that is dead at its initial marking and was reported deadlock-free before the restriction: `t1: one(a) read(g) → g` with `t2: one(g) → a` from `{a:1}`; `t: exactly(2, a) → a` from `{a:1}`; `t: one(a) inhibitor(b) → a` from `{a:1, b:1}`.

**Commoner's theorem needs at least one transition.** On a net with no transition every marking is dead, yet each marked place is a siphon whose maximal trap, the place itself, is marked, so the condition holds vacuously. An implementation MUST NOT convert the structural result into a `Proven` for such a net. Witness: one place `a`, no transition, from `{a:1}`; it is quiescent at once with a token stranded, a `DeadlockFree` violation.

**A structural proof needs every minimal siphon, each with an initially marked trap.** Commoner's condition quantifies over all siphons; checking the minimal ones suffices, because a trap inside a minimal siphon lies inside every siphon that contains it. An implementation MUST therefore find **every** minimal siphon before it concludes "no potential deadlock", and MUST require each one's maximal trap to hold a token in the **initial** marking; an empty or unmarked trap is a potential deadlock. Growing a siphon by committing to one input of each producer (the first, or all of them) is incomplete: it can miss exactly the empty siphon that makes the net dead. Deciding the condition is co-NP-complete, so the search MAY run under a budget; past it the result is inconclusive, never a proof. Two witnesses, each dead at its initial marking with a token stranded: `t1: one(g) one(x) → y, g` with `t2: one(h) one(y) → x, h` from `{g:1, h:1}` (minimal siphon `{x, y}`); `t1: one(a) one(c) → b, c` with `t2: one(b) → a` from `{c:1}` (minimal siphon `{a, b}`).
*When* the siphon search returns, every set it returns *shall* be a nonempty siphon that contains no other nonempty siphon.
*When* the siphon search returns, every nonempty siphon *shall* contain a set it returns.
The maximal trap the check computes inside a set of places *shall* be a trap inside that set that contains every trap inside it.
*If* the net has more than 50 places or no transition, *then* the structural check *shall* answer inconclusive.
The structural check *shall* pass the siphon search a budget of 10 000 search nodes.
*If* the siphon search does not return, *then* the structural check *shall* answer inconclusive.

*When* the siphon search returns on a net with at most 50 places and at least one transition, the structural check *shall* answer no potential deadlock exactly when the maximal trap inside each returned siphon holds a token in the initial marking, and potential deadlock otherwise.
*While* the total budget of [VER-013] is not spent, the siphon search *shall* return at a budget of 10 000 search nodes on the two witnesses above with minimal siphons `{x, y}` and `{a, b}`.
*If* the total budget of [VER-013] is spent before the siphon search starts on a net with at least one place, *then* the siphon search *shall not* return.

**A match transition hides a dead marking from the flat net.** A match transition ([NU-020]) joins tokens by identity, which the flat net does not see: the flat net enables the join whenever the counts are there, so it can have no dead marking while the net it stands for has one. The structural route therefore does not decide a net with match transitions, as it does not decide one with a reapable transition ([VER-002]) unless `assumeNoReaping` is set.

The verifier *shall* convert a no-potential-deadlock answer into a `Proven` only when it decides `DeadlockFree` on a net with no match transition ([NU-020]), no reapable transition ([VER-002]) unless `assumeNoReaping` is set, no read, inhibitor or reset arc, no consume-all input, no input arc weight above one, no declared sink or conditional sink and no environment place registered on the net it decides (the `Arrivals` rewrite of [VER-006] leaves none).

requirements.title: XOR Branch Analysis
requirements.testDerivation: Net with a XOR transition enabled after one step and a second XOR transition whose input place is never marked; on the closed graph the first XOR transition reports every outcome taken and the second every outcome untaken. A graph truncated before the first XOR transition fires is not complete and reports that transition's outcomes untaken. A transition split in flight is read off `complete:<t>`, a start edge alone takes none of its outcomes, and a class that marks `inflight:<t>` splits it before any completion fires. A XOR transition beside an unrelated drained forward is still reported.

spans.text: The XOR branch analysis *shall* report every transition of the net with two or more outcomes, and no other, once each with its number of outcomes.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *While* the graph it reads does not split a transition in flight, the XOR branch analysis *shall* report an index of that transition as taken exactly when an edge of the graph fires the transition with that index.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *While* the graph it reads splits a transition in flight ([VER-004]), that is, while an edge fires its completion `complete:<t>` or a class marks its place `inflight:<t>`, the XOR branch analysis *shall* report an index of that transition as taken exactly when an edge of the graph fires `complete:<t>` with that index.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: The XOR branch analysis *shall* report as untaken exactly the outcomes of a reported transition, numbered from 0 below its number of outcomes, that it does not report as taken.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *When* the graph is closed, the XOR branch analysis *shall* report an outcome of a reported transition as untaken exactly when no run of the net from its initial marking fires the transition with that outcome, or fires `complete:<t>` with it when the graph splits the transition.
spans.label: s5

paragraphs.text: The verifier supports analysis of the outcomes of transitions with XOR output branches over a built state class graph ([VER-010]), reporting which outcomes the graph takes. Each outcome of a transition, each XOR branch and a timeout outcome that deposits differently from every branch, is a virtual transition of its own ([VER-001]), and the outcomes are numbered from 0 in that order: the XOR branches in enumeration order, then the timeout outcome.
The XOR branch analysis *shall* report every transition of the net with two or more outcomes, and no other, once each with its number of outcomes.

*While* the graph it reads does not split a transition in flight, the XOR branch analysis *shall* report an index of that transition as taken exactly when an edge of the graph fires the transition with that index.

*While* the graph it reads splits a transition in flight ([VER-004]), that is, while an edge fires its completion `complete:<t>` or a class marks its place `inflight:<t>`, the XOR branch analysis *shall* report an index of that transition as taken exactly when an edge of the graph fires `complete:<t>` with that index.
The XOR branch analysis *shall* report as untaken exactly the outcomes of a reported transition, numbered from 0 below its number of outcomes, that it does not report as taken.

*When* the graph is closed, the XOR branch analysis *shall* report an outcome of a reported transition as untaken exactly when no run of the net from its initial marking fires the transition with that outcome, or fires `complete:<t>` with it when the graph splits the transition.

An index is taken as the edge carries it, with no bound: a graph builder that fires a transition only with its own outcomes gives no index at or above the number of outcomes. A transition whose `Timeout` forwards an `All` or `AtLeast` input ([IO-014]) has no virtual transitions of [VER-001], so the first sentence does not cover it: the analysis may report it with the number of outcomes its graph builder fires, as the runtimes do, and still reports every other transition of the net.

The analysis reads only the graph it is given and does not report whether that graph is closed. On a graph truncated at its class budget ([VER-017]) an untaken outcome may still fire beyond the budget, so a caller reads the graph's completeness (`isComplete`, `is_complete` in Rust) before calling an outcome unreachable.

requirements.title: Open-Net Verification Against a Contract

spans.text: *Count clauses*, each named: at every quiescent marking the tokens across the clause's places, each place counted once, number between `min` and `max`, or at least `min` for a clause with no `max`.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: A cycle of reapable transitions ([TIME-013]) counts too, since a run need not reap them.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: A quiescent marking **meets** the contract when every clause holds, lower bounds only while no terminal marker is marked, and every token lies on a clause place, a rest place, an environment place, a terminal marker, or an excused place of a marked terminal.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: The second condition is the rest set of [VER-014] with the clause, rest and environment places as sinks and each terminal as a conditional sink, and implementations MUST decide it through that same predicate.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: The verifier *shall* judge a quiescent marking to meet the contract exactly when, counting each place of a clause once, the tokens across each clause's places number at most the clause's `max` if it has one, at least its `min` unless some terminal marker is marked, and no marked place is stranded under the rest set of [VER-014] whose sinks are the clause, rest and environment places and whose conditional sinks are the terminals.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: Arrival group `i` contributes a source place holding `min` tokens and a source place holding `max − min`, each left out with its transitions when its count is 0, one transition per source and target place moving a token from that source onto the place, and a transition with no output that declines a token of the second source.
spans.label: s6

spans.text: A run is therefore quiescent only once every required arrival has happened and every optional one has been delivered or declined.
spans.label: s7

spans.text: The contract's environment transitions join the closed net unchanged.
spans.label: s8

spans.text: Contract places no arc touches join as places of their own and are listed in the report, so a clause over a place nothing writes counts zero there: a finding, never a refusal.
spans.label: s9

spans.text: *If* a name the closure adds, or the name of an environment transition, is already a place or transition name of the subnet, *then* the verifier *shall* refuse the closure, and it *shall* not refuse a closure whose added and environment-transition names are distinct from each other, from the subnet's names and from the environment places.
spans.label: s10

spans.text: The verifier *shall* build the closed net from the subnet's transitions, then the environment transitions unchanged, then, for each arrival group `i` in order, numbered from 0, one immediate transition `env:arrive[i]:<place>` per target place, in the group's order, taking one token from the source `env:arrivals[i]` when `min > 0`, and one immediate transition `env:arrive?[i]:<place>` per target place, in the group's order, taking one token from the source `env:optional[i]`, followed by an immediate `env:decline[i]` discarding one, when `max > min`; the transitions the closure adds have no other arc.
spans.label: s11

spans.text: The verifier *shall* start the closed net from the contract's initial marking with `min` tokens on `env:arrivals[i]` and `max − min` tokens on `env:optional[i]` for each source it builds.
spans.label: s12

spans.text: The verifier *shall* treat as an environment place exactly a place that an environment transition touches and the subnet does not, and *shall* make every place of the subnet and every place the contract names a place of the closed net.
spans.label: s13

spans.text: The verifier *shall* mark as environment steps exactly the environment transitions and the transitions the closure adds.
spans.label: s14

spans.text: The graph route MUST NOT run on a closed net that declares **match (ν-join) transitions**, the exclusion of [VER-017] condition 1.
spans.label: s15

spans.text: Both routes read quiescence as [VER-002] does: a class or marking whose enabled transitions are all reapable ([TIME-013]) rests too.
spans.label: s16
