The export *shall* give the end category to an ordinary place that some transition's output spec names and on which no transition has an input arc or a read arc.
The export *shall not* give the end category to an ordinary place on which some transition has an input arc.
The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start, the end or the regular place category.

An ordinary place that some transition's output spec names, and on which some transition has a read arc and none has an input arc, may have the end or the regular place category in this version; the regular place category is the intended one.

The export *shall* give the same category to all ordinary places, in one net or in different nets, that some transition's output spec names, on which some transition has a read arc and on which no transition has an input arc.

requirements.title: Compile-Time Diagram Generation
requirements.testDerivation: Annotated net structure; build project; verify diagram generated.

paragraphs.text: The engine MAY support generating diagrams from net structure annotations at compile time, embedding them in documentation or source comments.

notes.text:
- Java: `@NetStructure` annotation processed by `@petrinet` Javadoc taglet to embed DOT in `data-dot` attributes
- TypeScript: `@petrinet` TypeDoc plugin resolves net definitions and embeds DOT in `data-dot` attributes
- Rust: `libpetri-docgen` build-dependency crate emits DOT-in-HTML via `SvgGenerator` / `generate_svg()`

All three generators emit self-contained HTML pages that inline the canonical `LibpetriViewer` IIFE bundle (with `@viz-js/viz` Graphviz WASM baked in). DOT → SVG conversion happens client-side at view time. No external tooling (`dot`, `node`, etc.) is required on the doc-generation host.
notes.label: Implementation notes

requirements.body:

- Java: `@NetStructure` annotation processed by `@petrinet` Javadoc taglet to embed DOT in `data-dot` attributes

- Rust: `libpetri-docgen` build-dependency crate emits DOT-in-HTML via `SvgGenerator` / `generate_svg()`

All three generators emit self-contained HTML pages that inline the canonical `LibpetriViewer` IIFE bundle (with `@viz-js/viz` Graphviz WASM baked in). DOT → SVG conversion happens client-side at view time. No external tooling (`dot`, `node`, etc.) is required on the doc-generation host.

requirements.testDerivation: For each language, build a net with `XOR(A, B)`, `AND(C, D)`, `AND(A)`, and a nested case; export; assert junction node count, shape, and edge wiring.

spans.text: For every `Out.Xor` or `Out.And` group with **two or more children**, the mapper MUST insert a synthetic *junction node* between the transition and the children.
spans.label: s1

paragraphs.text: For every `Out.Xor` or `Out.And` group with **two or more children**, the mapper MUST insert a synthetic *junction node* between the transition and the children. A group with fewer than two children MUST NOT produce a junction (it is a pass-through).

- **XOR junction**: shape `diamond`, fill `#FFFFFF`, stroke `#333333`, penwidth `1.0`, width `0.3`, height `0.3`, label `"✕"` (U+2715 Multiplication X), fontsize `14`, fixedsize `true`. Style category `xor-junction`.

The two kinds share a shape and color family; the inline heavy glyph (`✕` for exclusive choice, `✚` for parallel split) is the discriminator. Heavy dingbat variants are used (instead of the lightweight `×` U+00D7 / `+` U+002B) so the symbol stays legible at the small junction size where the diamonds read as scaffolding rather than first-class entities.
The mapper *shall* draw one junction node for each `And` or `Xor` group of an output spec that has two or more children, of the group's kind, and no other junction node.
*Where* an `And` or `Xor` group has fewer than two children, the mapper *shall* draw its child, if it has one, from the group's parent and with the label the edge into the group would carry.

The mapper *shall* draw exactly one solid output edge into each junction node, into the place of each `Place` leaf and into the target place of each `ForwardInput` leaf, from the nearest junction node above it, or from the transition when there is none, and no other edge for the output spec.
The edge into a child of an `Xor` junction *shall* carry the child's branch label: the place name of a `Place` child, `⏱<n>ms` for a `Timeout` child of n ms, and no label for an `And` or `Xor` child.
The edge into a child of an `And` junction, and the edge from the transition into the output spec, *shall* carry no label of their own.
*Where* a `Timeout` node of n ms is in an output spec, the edge drawn into its child *shall* carry `⏱<n>ms` in place of the label the edge into the `Timeout` would carry.

*Where* a leaf is a `ForwardInput` from place F to place P, the mapper *shall* draw its edge as the edge of a `Place` leaf for P at the same position, dashed instead of solid, and with `⟵F` after its label and a space, or as its only label when it has none.
*Where* [EXP-013] combines a leaf edge into a reset place, that edge *shall* take the arc type, label and style [EXP-013] gives it in place of the ones above.

notes.text:
- Edge `transition → junction`: output style, no label (or the timeout label `⏱<n>ms` if the group is wrapped in `Out.Timeout`).
- Edge `junction → child` for an XOR junction: output style, label = the inferred branch label (place name for `Place`, `⏱<n>ms` for `Timeout`, or none if the child is itself a group).

requirements.body:
For every `Out.Xor` or `Out.And` group with **two or more children**, the mapper MUST insert a synthetic *junction node* between the transition and the children. A group with fewer than two children MUST NOT produce a junction (it is a pass-through).

**Junction node attributes** (gateway convention — diamond + single heavy glyph):
- **XOR junction**: shape `diamond`, fill `#FFFFFF`, stroke `#333333`, penwidth `1.0`, width `0.3`, height `0.3`, label `"✕"` (U+2715 Multiplication X), fontsize `14`, fixedsize `true`. Style category `xor-junction`.
- **AND junction**: shape `diamond`, fill `#FFFFFF`, stroke `#333333`, penwidth `1.0`, width `0.3`, height `0.3`, label `"✚"` (U+271A Heavy Greek Cross), fontsize `14`, fixedsize `true`. Style category `and-junction`.

The two kinds share a shape and color family; the inline heavy glyph (`✕` for exclusive choice, `✚` for parallel split) is the discriminator. Heavy dingbat variants are used (instead of the lightweight `×` U+00D7 / `+` U+002B) so the symbol stays legible at the small junction size where the diamonds read as scaffolding rather than first-class entities.

**Edge routing:**
- Edge `transition → junction`: output style, no label (or the timeout label `⏱<n>ms` if the group is wrapped in `Out.Timeout`).
- Edge `junction → child` for an XOR junction: output style, label = the inferred branch label (place name for `Place`, `⏱<n>ms` for `Timeout`, or none if the child is itself a group).
- Edge `junction → child` for an AND junction: output style, no label of its own.
- A `Timeout` node puts its label `⏱<n>ms` on the edge that enters its child, wherever the `Timeout` sits.
- A `ForwardInput` leaf edge is dashed and labelled `⟵<from>`, after the label the edge would otherwise carry and a space when it has one.
- Where [EXP-013] combines a leaf edge into a reset place, its arc type, label and style are those of [EXP-013].

The mapper *shall* draw one junction node for each `And` or `Xor` group of an output spec that has two or more children, of the group's kind, and no other junction node.

*Where* an `And` or `Xor` group has fewer than two children, the mapper *shall* draw its child, if it has one, from the group's parent and with the label the edge into the group would carry.

The mapper *shall* draw exactly one solid output edge into each junction node, into the place of each `Place` leaf and into the target place of each `ForwardInput` leaf, from the nearest junction node above it, or from the transition when there is none, and no other edge for the output spec.

The edge into a child of an `Xor` junction *shall* carry the child's branch label: the place name of a `Place` child, `⏱<n>ms` for a `Timeout` child of n ms, and no label for an `And` or `Xor` child.

The edge into a child of an `And` junction, and the edge from the transition into the output spec, *shall* carry no label of their own.

*Where* a `Timeout` node of n ms is in an output spec, the edge drawn into its child *shall* carry `⏱<n>ms` in place of the label the edge into the `Timeout` would carry.

*Where* a leaf is a `ForwardInput` from place F to place P, the mapper *shall* draw its edge as the edge of a `Place` leaf for P at the same position, dashed instead of solid, and with `⟵F` after its label and a space, or as its only label when it has none.

*Where* [EXP-013] combines a leaf edge into a reset place, that edge *shall* take the arc type, label and style [EXP-013] gives it in place of the ones above.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Net with `XOR(P_a, P_b)` exports one diamond junction labelled `"✕"` and two edges junction→{P_a, P_b}.
2. Net with `AND(P_c, P_d)` exports one diamond junction labelled `"✚"` and two edges junction→{P_c, P_d}.
3. Net with `AND(P_a)` (single child) exports a direct edge transition→P_a, no junction.
4. Nested groups (e.g. `XOR(AND(P_a, P_b), P_c)`) produce nested junctions.
5. Java, TypeScript, and Rust mappers produce byte-identical junction nodes and edges for the same input net (modulo deterministic ordering already in place).

requirements.body:
Synthetic junction nodes MUST use IDs of the form `j_<transitionSanitized>__<kind>_<idx>`, where:
- `transitionSanitized` is the transition's name with non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters replaced by `_` (the same `sanitize` function used for place and transition IDs).
- `<kind>` is `xor` or `and`.
- `<idx>` is a non-negative integer. Junctions in a single transition's `Out` tree are numbered in depth-first pre-order, with the counter starting at `0` and incrementing once per emitted junction. Single-child XOR/AND groups collapse (per EXP-012) and consume no counter slot. Example: `t_Nested` with output `AND(XOR(a,b), XOR(c,d))` produces three junctions in the order `j_Nested__and_0`, `j_Nested__xor_1`, `j_Nested__xor_2`.

The flat counter (rather than a hierarchical path-encoded index) keeps junction IDs short and human-scannable while still being uniquely determined by the depth-first traversal of the `Out` tree, which is what cross-language byte-equality requires.

This guarantees:
1. Junction IDs do not collide with place IDs (`p_…`) or transition IDs (`t_…`).
2. Repeated exports of the same net produce byte-identical DOT (required for stable Graphviz `dot` layouts across reloads in debug-ui and reproducible doc-generated SVGs).
3. Cross-language byte-equality of DOT output for the same input net.

*Where* a node's name (the place's, the transition's, or for a junction its transition's) holds only ASCII characters, the mapper *shall* give the node the ID `p_<s>`, `t_<s>` or `j_<s>__<kind>_<idx>` according to what it stands for, with `<s>` that name with each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` replaced by `_`, `<kind>` the kind of the junction and `<idx>` its index written in decimal without leading zeros.

The ID of a node whose name holds a character outside ASCII is implementation-defined, within the rule of the next sentence.

The mapper *shall* give no junction node the ID of a place node or a transition node, whatever the names.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* draw for each transition one junction node for each group with two or more children in its output spec, of the kind of that group, and no other junction node for the transition.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* give the junction node of a group with two or more children the index of that group in the depth-first pre-order of such groups in the transition's output spec, counting from 0, with one counter for both kinds.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* draw as the output edges of a transition, compared by their ends, exactly the edges [EXP-012] draws for its output spec, each as often as [EXP-012] draws it, with each junction numbered by the index of its group.

The mapper *shall* draw no edge that starts or ends at a junction node it does not draw.

The mapper *shall* draw no junction node for a transition the net does not have.

The mapper *shall* give a junction node of kind `xor` the `xor-junction` category of the node table and a junction node of kind `and` the `and-junction` category.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, its place and transition names hold only ASCII characters, and no two different place names, nor two different transition names, become equal when each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` is replaced by `_`, the mapper *shall* give no two nodes of the graph the same ID.

AC1 covers the junctions of transitions whose name is not empty and holds only ASCII characters.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. All junction IDs match the regex `j_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__(xor|and)_[0-9]+`.
2. Two consecutive exports of the same net produce byte-equal DOT.
3. Java, TypeScript, and Rust exports of the same net produce byte-equal DOT.

**Test derivation:** Export same net twice in same language; diff. Export same net across all three languages; diff.
acceptance: All junction IDs match the regex `j_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__(xor|and)_[0-9]+`.
Two consecutive exports of the same net produce byte-equal DOT.
Java, TypeScript, and Rust exports of the same net produce byte-equal DOT.

- **Subnet-membership metadata** ([MOD-026]) carried by a directly-composed net — a node mapped to subnet `S` clusters under `cluster_<sanitize(S)>`; a shared (multi-subnet) place has no entry and is not grouped by metadata.

When the net carries membership metadata the exporter SHOULD prefer it and fall back to instance-prefix detection for any node without an entry, so direct and instance composition coexist. The cluster source MAY be caller-selectable (metadata-only, prefix-only, or no clustering); the default SHOULD be metadata-when-present.

The sanitization function applied to the key MUST match the existing DOT ID sanitization per [EXP-014] (non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters, including `/`, replaced by `_`). The cluster `label` attribute SHOULD carry the original (un-sanitized) key string for human readability.

This requirement does NOT alter the styling, junction, or arc rendering rules of EXP-002..EXP-015; it adds grouping structure only. A net with neither composed instances nor membership metadata (no `/` in any node name) MUST produce no cluster subgraphs.

The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter draws cluster subgraphs at all. For an exporter that draws them, every MAY, SHOULD and MUST sentence of this requirement reads as *shall*: it lets the caller select each cluster source named above, takes the default source when the caller selects none, and follows the sentences below.

Under the default cluster source the cluster key of a place or a transition is its membership entry when it has one and otherwise its instance prefix; under the metadata-only source it is the membership entry alone, under the prefix-only source the instance prefix alone, and under no clustering there is none. The instance prefix of a name is the part before its last `/`; a name without `/`, or whose only `/` is its first character, has none. A junction node has the cluster key of its transition. A node without a cluster key is a top-level node. A `/`-prefix of a key is the non-empty beginning of the key up to, and not including, one of its `/` characters.

These sentences cover nets whose place names and transition names are ASCII, in which no two place names and no two transition names become equal under the sanitization of [EXP-014], and in which every cluster key of a place or transition name is ASCII, non-empty and has no empty `/`-segment: it neither starts nor ends with `/` and holds no `//`. On other nets the clustering, and whether it changes the nodes and edges drawn, is implementation-defined.

The mapper *shall* make each node that has a cluster key a direct member of the cluster of that key and of no other cluster, and a top-level node a member of no cluster.

The mapper *shall* list as a member of a cluster only a node it draws, and, on a net whose transition names are pairwise distinct, list each such node at most once.

The mapper *shall* draw exactly one cluster for each cluster key of a drawn node and for each `/`-prefix of such a key, and no other cluster.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

requirements.section: Visualization Rules — junctions and combined edges

paragraphs.text: DOT export SHOULD set `compound=true` at the digraph level unconditionally so Graphviz honours `lhead` and `ltail` attributes on edges that cross cluster boundaries. This is a no-op for flat (uncomposed) nets but keeps the digraph header uniform across all exports.

In this requirement the cluster key of a node is its key under [EXP-016], so a node with a key lies in the deepest cluster of that key, and an orphan is a node with no key, which is drawn at the top level. An edge is an edge of the exported graph other than a ghost edge, of any arc type, in the direction it is drawn, and either end of it may be a junction node ([EXP-012]). A bridge for an ordered pair of distinct keys (X, Y) is an orphan `o` together with an edge `a → o` from a node `a` with key X and an edge `o → b` to a node `b` with key Y, so one orphan with several such pairs of edges gives several bridges. A cluster and a cluster nested in it, such as `outer` and `outer/inner`, have two distinct keys, so an orphan between them bridges them.
For every ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y) that at least one bridge connects, the exporter MUST emit exactly one invisible ghost edge with:

- `style = invis` (no visible artifact; pure layout constraint)
- `arrowhead = none`
- `ltail = "cluster_" + sanitize(X)` (matches the cluster id defined by [EXP-016])
- `lhead = "cluster_" + sanitize(Y)`

The ghost edge's source and target node ids MUST be the `a` and the `b` of the first bridge for (X, Y) in this scan order: the nodes in the order they are drawn, for each orphan the edges into it in the order they are drawn, and for each of those the edges out of it in the order they are drawn. Graphviz then has a real cluster-to-cluster connection to constrain layout, while the visible flow still passes through the orphan via the original real edges.

Because every drawn edge counts, a reset edge into an orphan place and a read edge out of it bridge two clusters although no token moves between them. An orphan transition whose output spec has a junction bridges nothing through that junction, since the junction is itself an orphan.

Multiple orphans bridging the same ordered cluster pair `(X, Y)` collapse to one ghost edge (dedup by ordered pair). The reverse direction `(Y, X)` is a separate ghost edge when its own 1-hop path exists. Orphan paths that fall entirely inside a single cluster (`X == Y`) or that only touch one clustered neighbour MUST NOT produce a ghost edge.
This requirement does NOT change [EXP-016] cluster membership, the visible edge set, or styling rules. It only adds the `compound=true` graph attribute and the synthesized ghost edges.

Apart from the `compound` attribute, these sentences cover the nets that the sentences of [EXP-016] cover; on other nets the ghost edges, and whether clustering changes the other edges drawn, are implementation-defined.
The exporter *shall* set the graph attribute `compound` to true in every export.

*Where* a bridge connects an ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y), an exporter that clusters *shall* draw a ghost edge from the `a` to the `b` of the first bridge for (X, Y), with `ltail` the cluster ID of X and `lhead` the cluster ID of Y.

Each ghost edge that an exporter that clusters draws *shall* run from the `a` to the `b` of the first bridge for some ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y), with `ltail` the cluster ID of X and `lhead` the cluster ID of Y.
An exporter that clusters *shall* draw at most one ghost edge for each ordered pair of cluster keys.
The exporter *shall* draw the same edges other than ghost edges as it draws for the same net with no clustering.

requirements.body:
DOT export SHOULD set `compound=true` at the digraph level unconditionally so Graphviz honours `lhead` and `ltail` attributes on edges that cross cluster boundaries. This is a no-op for flat (uncomposed) nets but keeps the digraph header uniform across all exports.

In this requirement the cluster key of a node is its key under [EXP-016], so a node with a key lies in the deepest cluster of that key, and an orphan is a node with no key, which is drawn at the top level. An edge is an edge of the exported graph other than a ghost edge, of any arc type, in the direction it is drawn, and either end of it may be a junction node ([EXP-012]). A bridge for an ordered pair of distinct keys (X, Y) is an orphan `o` together with an edge `a → o` from a node `a` with key X and an edge `o → b` to a node `b` with key Y, so one orphan with several such pairs of edges gives several bridges. A cluster and a cluster nested in it, such as `outer` and `outer/inner`, have two distinct keys, so an orphan between them bridges them.

For every ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y) that at least one bridge connects, the exporter MUST emit exactly one invisible ghost edge with:

- `style = invis` (no visible artifact; pure layout constraint)
- `arrowhead = none`
- `ltail = "cluster_" + sanitize(X)` (matches the cluster id defined by [EXP-016])
- `lhead = "cluster_" + sanitize(Y)`

The ghost edge's source and target node ids MUST be the `a` and the `b` of the first bridge for (X, Y) in this scan order: the nodes in the order they are drawn, for each orphan the edges into it in the order they are drawn, and for each of those the edges out of it in the order they are drawn. Graphviz then has a real cluster-to-cluster connection to constrain layout, while the visible flow still passes through the orphan via the original real edges.

Because every drawn edge counts, a reset edge into an orphan place and a read edge out of it bridge two clusters although no token moves between them. An orphan transition whose output spec has a junction bridges nothing through that junction, since the junction is itself an orphan.

Multiple orphans bridging the same ordered cluster pair `(X, Y)` collapse to one ghost edge (dedup by ordered pair). The reverse direction `(Y, X)` is a separate ghost edge when its own 1-hop path exists. Orphan paths that fall entirely inside a single cluster (`X == Y`) or that only touch one clustered neighbour MUST NOT produce a ghost edge.

This requirement does NOT change [EXP-016] cluster membership, the visible edge set, or styling rules. It only adds the `compound=true` graph attribute and the synthesized ghost edges.

Apart from the `compound` attribute, these sentences cover the nets that the sentences of [EXP-016] cover; on other nets the ghost edges, and whether clustering changes the other edges drawn, are implementation-defined.

The exporter *shall* set the graph attribute `compound` to true in every export.

*Where* a bridge connects an ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y), an exporter that clusters *shall* draw a ghost edge from the `a` to the `b` of the first bridge for (X, Y), with `ltail` the cluster ID of X and `lhead` the cluster ID of Y.

Each ghost edge that an exporter that clusters draws *shall* run from the `a` to the `b` of the first bridge for some ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y), with `ltail` the cluster ID of X and `lhead` the cluster ID of Y.

An exporter that clusters *shall* draw at most one ghost edge for each ordered pair of cluster keys.

The exporter *shall* draw the same edges other than ghost edges as it draws for the same net with no clustering.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Every DOT export contains `compound="true"` as a top-level graph attribute.
2. A net where `cluster_left` and `cluster_right` are bridged by a single orphan transition produces exactly one ghost edge with `style=invis`, `arrowhead=none`, `ltail="cluster_left"`, `lhead="cluster_right"`.
3. Three orphans bridging the same `(left, right)` pair still produce exactly one ghost edge (dedup by ordered pair).
4. Bidirectional bridging (`left → o1 → right` and `right → o2 → left`) produces two ghost edges, one per direction.
5. An orphan with `X → o → X` (same cluster on both sides) produces no ghost edge.
6. An orphan with only one clustered neighbour produces no ghost edge.
7. A flat net (no instance prefixes) produces no ghost edges but still emits `compound="true"`.
8. Anchor node selection is deterministic and matches across Java, TypeScript, and Rust exporters byte-for-byte for the same composed input.

**Depends on:** [EXP-012], [EXP-014], [EXP-016]
**Test derivation:** Build a composed net with two instances and an orphan transition between them; export DOT in each language; assert one `style="invis"` edge with matching `ltail`/`lhead`. Add bidirectional and multi-orphan variants. Verify `compound="true"` on a flat net.

requirements.section: Visualization Rules — junctions and combined edges

paragraphs.text: When a transition declares a ν-net join correlation ([NU-020]), each **input edge** to a correlated place is decorated to mark it as a name-matched input:

- **Color** `#0d9488` (teal, the `match-input` edge style in `spec/petri-net-styles.json`), distinguishing it from a plain input edge.
- **Label** prefixed with the bound-name variable `⟨n⟩` (U+27E8 `n` U+27E9). When the input also carries a cardinality label ([EXP-006]), the two are joined with a single space: `⟨n⟩ ×2`, `⟨n⟩ *`, `⟨n⟩ ≥3`. A correlated `One` input shows `⟨n⟩` alone.

Non-correlated inputs of the same transition are unaffected. The decoration is a mapper concern: it is emitted into the DOT by every exporter, so the canonical viewer and all three doc generators render it identically with no viewer change.
The export *shall* draw each input arc of a transition as an edge of arc type input from the arc's place to the transition, whether or not the transition correlates the place.

*Where* the match specification of a transition ([NU-020]) correlates the place of one of its input arcs, the export *shall* draw the edge of that arc with the `match-input` style row and label it `⟨n⟩` if the arc's cardinality is `One`, and otherwise `⟨n⟩`, one space and the arc's cardinality label ([EXP-006]).

*Where* a transition does not correlate the place of one of its input arcs, the export *shall* draw the edge of that arc with the `input` style row and give it the arc's cardinality label alone, or no label if the cardinality is `One`.
Apart from ghost edges ([EXP-017]), the export *shall* draw only the input edges of correlated places with the `match-input` style row.

When a transition declares a ν-net join correlation ([NU-020]), each **input
edge** to a correlated place is decorated to mark it as a name-matched input:

- **Color** `#0d9488` (teal, the `match-input` edge style in
  `spec/petri-net-styles.json`), distinguishing it from a plain input edge.
- **Label** prefixed with the bound-name variable `⟨n⟩` (U+27E8 `n` U+27E9). When
  the input also carries a cardinality label ([EXP-006]), the two are joined with
  a single space: `⟨n⟩ ×2`, `⟨n⟩ *`, `⟨n⟩ ≥3`. A correlated `One` input shows
  `⟨n⟩` alone.

Non-correlated inputs of the same transition are unaffected. The decoration is a
mapper concern: it is emitted into the DOT by every exporter, so the canonical
viewer and all three doc generators render it identically with no viewer change.

The export *shall* draw each input arc of a transition as an edge of arc type input from the arc's place to the transition, whether or not the transition correlates the place.

*Where* the match specification of a transition ([NU-020]) correlates the place of one of its input arcs, the export *shall* draw the edge of that arc with the `match-input` style row and label it `⟨n⟩` if the arc's cardinality is `One`, and otherwise `⟨n⟩`, one space and the arc's cardinality label ([EXP-006]).

*Where* a transition does not correlate the place of one of its input arcs, the export *shall* draw the edge of that arc with the `input` style row and give it the arc's cardinality label alone, or no label if the cardinality is `One`.

Apart from ghost edges ([EXP-017]), the export *shall* draw only the input edges of correlated places with the `match-input` style row.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. An input edge to a correlated place has color `#0d9488` and a label beginning
   with `⟨n⟩`.
2. A non-correlated input edge on the same transition keeps the default color and
   no `⟨n⟩` prefix.
3. The label combines with cardinality as `⟨n⟩ ×n` / `⟨n⟩ *` / `⟨n⟩ ≥m`.
4. The emitted DOT for a ν-net is byte-identical across the Java, TypeScript, and
   Rust exporters.

**Depends on:** [EXP-006], [EXP-017], [NU-020]
**Test derivation:** Build a join with `match` correlating two `one` inputs;
export; verify both correlated edges are teal and labeled `⟨n⟩`, and a third

requirements.title: Linear Scaling
requirements.testDerivation: Benchmark chain nets of 5, 50, and 500 transitions; verify near-linear scaling of orchestrator overhead.

paragraphs.text: Execution time scales linearly with the number of transitions in the net. There MUST be no quadratic or worse blowup in the orchestrator loop.

requirements.body:
Execution time scales linearly with the number of transitions in the net. There MUST be no quadratic or worse blowup in the orchestrator loop.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A net with 2N transitions takes approximately 2× the orchestrator time of a net with N transitions (for equivalent workloads).
2. No O(n²) iteration over all transitions on each cycle (dirty set ensures only affected transitions are re-evaluated).

**Depends on:** [CONC-005]
**Test derivation:** Benchmark chain nets of 5, 50, and 500 transitions; verify near-linear scaling of orchestrator overhead.
acceptance: A net with 2N transitions takes approximately 2× the orchestrator time of a net with N transitions (for equivalent workloads).
No O(n²) iteration over all transitions on each cycle (dirty set ensures only affected transitions are re-evaluated).

requirements.title: Enablement Check O(W)
requirements.testDerivation: Benchmark enablement check on nets of varying sizes; verify constant-time for small nets.

paragraphs.text: Individual transition enablement checks are O(W) where W = ceil(numPlaces / word_size). Word size is implementation-defined (32-bit or 64-bit). For nets with fewer than 64 places, this is O(1).

requirements.body:
Individual transition enablement checks are O(W) where W = ceil(numPlaces / word_size). Word size is implementation-defined (32-bit or 64-bit). For nets with fewer than 64 places, this is O(1).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Enablement check for a single transition does not iterate over arcs.
2. Check is constant-time for nets with < 64 places.
3. Check scales with word count for larger nets.

**Depends on:** [CONC-004]
**Test derivation:** Benchmark enablement check on nets of varying sizes; verify constant-time for small nets.
acceptance: Enablement check for a single transition does not iterate over arcs.
Check is constant-time for nets with < 64 places.
Check scales with word count for larger nets.

requirements.title: Dirty Set O(affected)
requirements.testDerivation: Net with 50 transitions; token change affects 3; verify only 3 re-evaluated (via instrumentation or timing).

paragraphs.text: Each orchestrator cycle re-evaluates only the transitions affected by token changes since the last cycle. The cost is O(D) where D is the number of dirty transitions, not O(T) where T is the total transition count.

requirements.body:
Each orchestrator cycle re-evaluates only the transitions affected by token changes since the last cycle. The cost is O(D) where D is the number of dirty transitions, not O(T) where T is the total transition count.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Adding a token to a place with 3 connected transitions causes exactly 3 re-evaluations.
2. Transitions connected to unchanged places are not re-evaluated.

**Depends on:** [CONC-005]
**Test derivation:** Net with 50 transitions; token change affects 3; verify only 3 re-evaluated (via instrumentation or timing).
acceptance: Adding a token to a place with 3 connected transitions causes exactly 3 re-evaluations.
Transitions connected to unchanged places are not re-evaluated.

requirements.title: Lock-Free Hot Path
requirements.testDerivation: 100 concurrent action completions; verify no lock contention in profiler.

paragraphs.text: The completion signaling path (action completing → orchestrator notified) uses lock-free data structures. No mutex/lock acquisition on the hot path.

requirements.body:
The completion signaling path (action completing → orchestrator notified) uses lock-free data structures. No mutex/lock acquisition on the hot path.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Completion queue is lock-free (CAS-based, channel-based, or similar).
2. Wake-up signal does not require acquiring a contended lock.

**Depends on:** [CONC-006]
**Test derivation:** 100 concurrent action completions; verify no lock contention in profiler.
acceptance: Completion queue is lock-free (CAS-based, channel-based, or similar).
Wake-up signal does not require acquiring a contended lock.

requirements.title: Noop Event Store Zero-Cost
requirements.testDerivation: Benchmark same net with noop vs in-memory store; verify noop is faster (no allocation overhead).

paragraphs.text: When the noop event store is used (isEnabled() returns false), the executor MUST skip event object creation entirely. No allocation occurs for events that will be discarded.

requirements.body:

**Acceptance Criteria:**

3. Measurable performance difference between noop and in-memory stores under load.

**Test derivation:** Benchmark same net with noop vs in-memory store; verify noop is faster (no allocation overhead).
acceptance: Executor checks isEnabled() before creating event objects.

requirements.title: Inline Action Optimization
requirements.testDerivation: Chain of 100 transitions bound to trivial synchronous actions; measure total time; verify sub-millisecond per transition.

paragraphs.text: Synchronous actions (passthrough, simple transforms) that complete immediately SHOULD be executed inline on the orchestrator thread, avoiding task dispatch overhead.

requirements.body:
Synchronous actions (passthrough, simple transforms) that complete immediately SHOULD be executed inline on the orchestrator thread, avoiding task dispatch overhead.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Passthrough action executes without spawning a task.
2. Chain of N transitions bound to trivial synchronous actions completes with overhead proportional to N, not N × task_spawn_cost.

**Depends on:** [CONC-011]
**Test derivation:** Chain of 100 transitions bound to trivial synchronous actions; measure total time; verify sub-millisecond per transition.
acceptance: Passthrough action executes without spawning a task.

requirements.title: Benchmark Suite
requirements.testDerivation: Run benchmark suite; verify all scenarios execute without errors.

paragraphs.text: Each implementation MUST include a benchmark suite covering the following scenarios:

1. **Single passthrough**: One transition with passthrough action.
2. **Linear chain**: Sequence of N transitions (for N = 5, 10, 50, 100, 500).
3. **Parallel branches**: Multiple independent branches firing concurrently.
4. **Sync-only chain**: Chain of synchronous actions (inline execution path).
5. **Async chain**: Chain of actions with async work (task dispatch path).
6. **Mixed net**: Combination of sync and async actions.

paragraphs.text: The bitmap executor uses compact representations:

- Place presence: 1 bit per place per bitmap word
- Transition masks: k full-width masks per transition, each ceil(P / word_size) words

In the current implementations k is 2 in Rust and TypeScript (the needs-mask and the inhibitor-mask of [CONC-007]) and 5 in Java (a reset-mask besides the two, and a word-array copy of each of the two).

- Per-transition masks: k × ceil(P / word_size) words for each transition

The bitmap executor *shall* keep at most k full-width masks per transition, for one number k that the implementation fixes and that does not depend on the net, and no full-width mask words beside those masks.

requirements.testDerivation: Profile execution of a 100-transition net; verify no hash map operations on the hot path.

paragraphs.text: The precompiled executor SHOULD use a flat-array memory layout with no hash map lookups on the hot path. Per-transition data is stored in parallel arrays of length T (transition count) indexed by transition ID. Token storage uses ring buffers indexed by place ID. In-flight transition tracking uses arrays indexed by transition ID.

requirements.body:
The precompiled executor SHOULD use a flat-array memory layout with no hash map lookups on the hot path. Per-transition data is stored in parallel arrays of length T (transition count) indexed by transition ID. Token storage uses ring buffers indexed by place ID. In-flight transition tracking uses arrays indexed by transition ID.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. No hash map lookups occur during the execution loop (consume, fire, complete, enable).
2. Per-transition timing, priority, masks, and opcodes are in parallel arrays.
3. Token access is by integer place ID, not by place object lookup.
4. In-flight tracking is by integer transition ID, not by transition object lookup.

**Depends on:** [CONC-020]
**Test derivation:** Profile execution of a 100-transition net; verify no hash map operations on the hot path.

requirements.title: Sparse Enablement Masks
requirements.testDerivation: Net with 200 places where each transition touches 2–3 places; verify sparse check matches full bitmap check and is faster.

spans.text: *Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, it *shall* compile a needs-mask or an inhibitor-mask to the empty sentinel exactly when all its words are zero and a mask with exactly one non-zero word to the single-word form holding that word's index and value, and it *shall* put only non-zero words of the mask, each with its index, into a multi-word form.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, its presence check on the sparse forms compiled from a transition's needs-mask and inhibitor-mask *shall* return, for every presence bitmap, the result of the presence check of [CONC-004] computed over every word of both masks.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: These two sentences hold for masks and presence bitmaps of the same number of words, each word within the executor's word size.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: Enablement results are identical to full-width bitmap checks.
spans.label: s4

paragraphs.text: Enablement masks SHOULD use a sparse representation to avoid scanning zero words in large nets. Three cases:

- **Empty** (sentinel value): skip the check entirely (e.g., transition with no input places or no inhibitors)
- **Single-word** (fast path): store word index + mask value; one AND + one compare operation
- **Multi-word sparse**: store only non-zero word indices and their mask values; iterate only non-zero entries
This avoids scanning W words when most are zero (common in large, sparse nets).

*Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, it *shall* compile a needs-mask or an inhibitor-mask to the empty sentinel exactly when all its words are zero and a mask with exactly one non-zero word to the single-word form holding that word's index and value, and it *shall* put only non-zero words of the mask, each with its index, into a multi-word form.

*Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, its presence check on the sparse forms compiled from a transition's needs-mask and inhibitor-mask *shall* return, for every presence bitmap, the result of the presence check of [CONC-004] computed over every word of both masks.

These two sentences hold for masks and presence bitmaps of the same number of words, each word within the executor's word size. The SHOULD above is about whether an executor uses a sparse representation at all; an executor that does is bound by the two sentences above.

- **Multi-word sparse**: store only non-zero word indices and their mask values; iterate only non-zero entries

This avoids scanning W words when most are zero (common in large, sparse nets).

*Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, it *shall* compile a needs-mask or an inhibitor-mask to the empty sentinel exactly when all its words are zero and a mask with exactly one non-zero word to the single-word form holding that word's index and value, and it *shall* put only non-zero words of the mask, each with its index, into a multi-word form.

*Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, its presence check on the sparse forms compiled from a transition's needs-mask and inhibitor-mask *shall* return, for every presence bitmap, the result of the presence check of [CONC-004] computed over every word of both masks.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Empty masks are detected and skipped with no computation.
2. Single-word masks use one AND + one compare (no loop).
3. Multi-word sparse masks iterate only non-zero words.
4. Enablement results are identical to full-width bitmap checks.

**Depends on:** [CONC-004], [CONC-020]
**Test derivation:** Net with 200 places where each transition touches 2–3 places; verify sparse check matches full bitmap check and is faster.
acceptance: Empty masks are detected and skipped with no computation.
Single-word masks use one AND + one compare (no loop).
Multi-word sparse masks iterate only non-zero words.
Enablement results are identical to full-width bitmap checks.

requirements.title: SubnetDef Definition (open net + interface)
requirements.testDerivation: Build a subnet definition with two places and one transition, exposing one place as a port; verify body, interface, port set, and channel set are accessible and unmodifiable.

spans.text: *When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared ports, each with the name, direction and place it was declared with.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared channels, each with the name and transition it was declared with.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its body *shall* hold the places and terminal places of the net that the net builder builds from the declaration, and the declared transitions in the order they were added, none of them renamed.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: *When* building the subnet definition succeeds, the subnet definition *shall* keep the name it was declared with.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *When* the net builder builds the body and the interface declares no port and no channel, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed.
spans.label: s5

paragraphs.text: A **subnet definition** is an open Petri net fragment paired with a declared **interface**. The fragment is a structurally complete net definition (places, transitions, arcs, timing, priority, optional actions) per [CORE-040]; the interface enumerates which of its places are exposed as **ports** and which of its transitions are exposed as **synchronous channels**.
A subnet definition MAY be parameterised by a typed `Params` value supplied at instantiation time (see [MOD-010]). When unparameterised, the parameter type is the implementation's unit/void type.

Building a subnet definition fails in the cases of [MOD-006]; this requirement says what a successful build returns. The body is the net that the net builder builds from the declared places, transitions and terminal places ([CORE-040]), so its places include every place an arc of a body transition names. The order in which the interface lists its ports and channels is not specified. As in [TIME-010], the transitions of one body are assumed to have pairwise distinct names.
*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared ports, each with the name, direction and place it was declared with.
*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared channels, each with the name and transition it was declared with.

*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its body *shall* hold the places and terminal places of the net that the net builder builds from the declaration, and the declared transitions in the order they were added, none of them renamed.
*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, the subnet definition *shall* keep the name it was declared with.
*When* the net builder builds the body and the interface declares no port and no channel, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed.

The body is the net that the net builder builds from the declared places, transitions and terminal places ([CORE-040]), so its places include every place an arc of a body transition names. The order in which the interface lists its ports and channels is not specified. As in [TIME-010], the transitions of one body are assumed to have pairwise distinct names.

*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared ports, each with the name, direction and place it was declared with.

*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared channels, each with the name and transition it was declared with.

*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its body *shall* hold the places and terminal places of the net that the net builder builds from the declaration, and the declared transitions in the order they were added, none of them renamed.

*When* the net builder builds the body and the interface declares no port and no channel, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A subnet definition can be constructed with a body net and an interface.
2. The body net follows all CORE construction rules and is itself immutable per [CORE-041].
3. The interface enumerates a (possibly empty) set of ports and a (possibly empty) set of channels.
4. The subnet definition exposes both `body()` (the unrenamed body) and `iface()` (the interface) for inspection.

**Test derivation:** Build a subnet definition with two places and one transition, exposing one place as a port; verify body, interface, port set, and channel set are accessible and unmodifiable.

requirements.title: Subnet Identity (sealed/sum-type distinction from PetriNet)
requirements.testDerivation: Attempt to construct an executor from an open subnet; verify the call site does not compile (Java/Rust) or fails fast at construction (TypeScript). Attempt to compose a closed net into a builder; verify symmetric rejection.

paragraphs.text: The engine distinguishes between **closed** nets (a `PetriNet` per [CORE-040], runnable by an executor) and **open** nets (a subnet definition, not directly runnable). The two share a common type abstraction (sealed sum, sealed interface, or enum, depending on language) so APIs can accept "any net" or restrict to one variant.

APIs that require a runnable net MUST reject an open subnet at the type level where the language permits, and at construction-time otherwise. APIs that require an open fragment MUST symmetrically reject a closed net.

requirements.body:
The engine distinguishes between **closed** nets (a `PetriNet` per [CORE-040], runnable by an executor) and **open** nets (a subnet definition, not directly runnable). The two share a common type abstraction (sealed sum, sealed interface, or enum, depending on language) so APIs can accept "any net" or restrict to one variant.

APIs that require a runnable net MUST reject an open subnet at the type level where the language permits, and at construction-time otherwise. APIs that require an open fragment MUST symmetrically reject a closed net.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A common abstraction (`Subnet`) classifies nets as closed or open.
2. The two variants are distinguishable by type (sealed/sum-type), not merely by a runtime tag.
3. Passing an open subnet to an executor-construction API is a compile-time error in languages with sealed types, or a clearly reported construction-time error otherwise.
4. Passing a closed net to a composition API that expects an open fragment is similarly rejected.

**Test derivation:** Attempt to construct an executor from an open subnet; verify the call site does not compile (Java/Rust) or fails fast at construction (TypeScript). Attempt to compose a closed net into a builder; verify symmetric rejection.
acceptance: A common abstraction (`Subnet`) classifies nets as closed or open.
The two variants are distinguishable by type (sealed/sum-type), not merely by a runtime tag.
Passing an open subnet to an executor-construction API is a compile-time error in languages with sealed types, or a clearly reported construction-time error otherwise.
Passing a closed net to a composition API that expects an open fragment is similarly rejected.

requirements.title: Port Declaration (name + direction + place)
requirements.testDerivation: Build an interface with ports `in: Input<String>` and `out: Output<String>`; verify both names and directions retrievable. Attempt to declare two ports with the same name; verify rejection. Attempt to declare a port over a place not in the body; verify rejection. Declare a second port with another name over the place of `in`, once as `Input` and once as `Output`; verify that both subnets build.

spans.text: *If* two ports of one interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *If* the net builder builds the body and a port exposes a place that is not a place of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *When* building a subnet definition succeeds, building it with one more port, whose name no port of the interface has and which exposes the place of one of its ports, *shall* also succeed, whatever the directions of the two ports.
spans.label: s3

paragraphs.text: An **interface place** (port) declares:

1. A **name** unique within the interface.
2. A **direction**: `Input`, `Output`, or `InOut`.
3. The underlying `Place<T>` from the body net it exposes.

The exposed place MUST be a place of the subnet's body. Two distinct ports MAY expose the same body place, whatever their directions. When two ports expose one body place, a caller binds both to one caller place; which binding a composition keeps when they are bound to two different caller places is not defined ([MOD-020]).
*If* two ports of one interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
*If* the net builder builds the body and a port exposes a place that is not a place of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*When* building a subnet definition succeeds, building it with one more port, whose name no port of the interface has and which exposes the place of one of its ports, *shall* also succeed, whatever the directions of the two ports.

requirements.body:
An **interface place** (port) declares:
1. A **name** unique within the interface.
2. A **direction**: `Input`, `Output`, or `InOut`.
3. The underlying `Place<T>` from the body net it exposes.

The exposed place MUST be a place of the subnet's body. Two distinct ports MAY expose the same body place, whatever their directions. When two ports expose one body place, a caller binds both to one caller place; which binding a composition keeps when they are bound to two different caller places is not defined ([MOD-020]).

*If* two ports of one interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*If* the net builder builds the body and a port exposes a place that is not a place of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*When* building a subnet definition succeeds, building it with one more port, whose name no port of the interface has and which exposes the place of one of its ports, *shall* also succeed, whatever the directions of the two ports.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A port can be declared with name, direction, and a body place.
2. The port name is unique within an interface (duplicate names rejected at build).
3. The exposed place's token type is preserved in the port's typed handle (see [MOD-011]).
4. A port whose underlying place is not present in the body net is rejected at build (see [MOD-006]).
5. Two ports with different names over one body place build, whatever their directions.

**Test derivation:** Build an interface with ports `in: Input<String>` and `out: Output<String>`; verify both names and directions retrievable. The port name is unique within an interface (duplicate names rejected at build).
The exposed place's token type is preserved in the port's typed handle (see [MOD-011]).
A port whose underlying place is not present in the body net is rejected at build (see [MOD-006]).
Two ports with different names over one body place build, whatever their directions.

requirements.title: Port Direction Semantics (advisory; arcs govern flow)
requirements.testDerivation: Build a subnet whose `Output` port place has both an internal output arc (producer) and an internal input arc (consumer); verify build succeeds.

spans.text: *When* two subnet declarations differ only in the directions of their ports, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed for both or fail for both.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *When* two subnet definitions differ only in the directions of their ports, `instantiate` with one prefix *shall* succeed for both or fail for both, and two successes *shall* give the same places, the same transitions, the same port and channel handles, and the same ports apart from their directions.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *When* building a subnet definition succeeds, the definition *shall* have a port with the name of each declared port, and each such port *shall* carry the declared direction.
spans.label: s3

paragraphs.text: Port direction is **advisory metadata**: the subnet builder, `instantiate` and composition do not read it. Documentation, visualization and the verification harness of [MOD-051] read it. It does NOT constrain arc flow at runtime: an `Output` port's place MAY have input arcs from internal transitions; an `Input` port's place MAY be read by internal transitions. Actual token flow at run time is governed exclusively by arcs declared per CORE-030..CORE-035.

Implementations MAY emit a build-time warning when declared direction conflicts with the arc structure (e.g., an `Input` port whose place has no internal consumer transition), but MUST NOT reject the subnet on direction-versus-arc mismatch.
*When* two subnet declarations differ only in the directions of their ports, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed for both or fail for both.

*When* two subnet definitions differ only in the directions of their ports, `instantiate` with one prefix *shall* succeed for both or fail for both, and two successes *shall* give the same places, the same transitions, the same port and channel handles, and the same ports apart from their directions.
*When* building a subnet definition succeeds, the definition *shall* have a port with the name of each declared port, and each such port *shall* carry the declared direction.

It does NOT constrain arc flow at runtime: an `Output` port's place MAY have input arcs from internal transitions; an `Input` port's place MAY be read by internal transitions. Actual token flow at run time is governed exclusively by arcs declared per CORE-030..CORE-035.

Implementations MAY emit a build-time warning when declared direction conflicts with the arc structure (e.g., an `Input` port whose place has no internal consumer transition), but MUST NOT reject the subnet on direction-versus-arc mismatch.

*When* two subnet declarations differ only in the directions of their ports, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed for both or fail for both.

*When* two subnet definitions differ only in the directions of their ports, `instantiate` with one prefix *shall* succeed for both or fail for both, and two successes *shall* give the same places, the same transitions, the same port and channel handles, and the same ports apart from their directions.

*When* building a subnet definition succeeds, the definition *shall* have a port with the name of each declared port, and each such port *shall* carry the declared direction.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Direction metadata is preserved and queryable via the port handle.
2. A subnet whose `Output` port place is also written internally by transitions is accepted at build.
3. A subnet whose `Input` port place is also read internally by transitions is accepted at build.
4. Where a warning channel exists, an obvious mismatch (declared `Input` with no internal consumer; declared `Output` with no internal producer) MAY emit a warning but MUST NOT raise an error.

**Depends on:** [CORE-030], [CORE-031], [CORE-032], [CORE-033], [CORE-034], [CORE-035]
**Test derivation:** Build a subnet whose `Output` port place has both an internal output arc (producer) and an internal input arc (consumer); verify build succeeds.
acceptance: Direction metadata is preserved and queryable via the port handle.
A subnet whose `Output` port place is also written internally by transitions is accepted at build.
A subnet whose `Input` port place is also read internally by transitions is accepted at build.
Where a warning channel exists, an obvious mismatch (declared `Input` with no internal consumer; declared `Output` with no internal producer) MAY emit a warning but MUST NOT raise an error.

requirements.title: Channel Declaration (interface transitions for synchronous fusion)
requirements.testDerivation: Build an interface with one channel exposing a transition `attempt`; verify the channel handle resolves to the same transition identity in the renamed body. Attempt to declare two channels with the same name; verify rejection.

spans.text: *If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *If* a channel of the interface exposes a transition whose name is not the name of a transition of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *When* the net builder builds the body, the subnet definition builds without its channels, every channel exposes a transition of the built body, no two channels have the same name, and no channel has the name of a port, building the subnet definition with its channels *shall* succeed.
spans.label: s3

paragraphs.text: An **interface transition** (synchronous channel) declares:

1. A **name** unique within the interface (sharing namespace with port names is implementation-defined; collisions MUST be rejected if they share a namespace).
2. The underlying `Transition` from the body net it exposes.

A channel MAY be bound at composition time to a caller-side transition, producing a single merged transition in the composed net (see [MOD-021]). Channels are the synchronization primitive for cross-instance and host-instance coupling at the transition level; ports synchronize at the place level.

As in [MOD-006], a channel whose transition has the name of no body transition is rejected, a channel over a transition of the body is accepted, and a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a body transition is implementation-defined. For subnet definitions [MOD-006] settles the namespace choice of item 1: port names and channel names are two namespaces.
*If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
*If* a channel of the interface exposes a transition whose name is not the name of a transition of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*When* the net builder builds the body, the subnet definition builds without its channels, every channel exposes a transition of the built body, no two channels have the same name, and no channel has the name of a port, building the subnet definition with its channels *shall* succeed.

1. A **name** unique within the interface (sharing namespace with port names is implementation-defined; collisions MUST be rejected if they share a namespace).
2. The underlying `Transition` from the body net it exposes.

A channel MAY be bound at composition time to a caller-side transition, producing a single merged transition in the composed net (see [MOD-021]). Channels are the synchronization primitive for cross-instance and host-instance coupling at the transition level; ports synchronize at the place level.

As in [MOD-006], a channel whose transition has the name of no body transition is rejected, a channel over a transition of the body is accepted, and a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a body transition is implementation-defined. For subnet definitions [MOD-006] settles the namespace choice of item 1: port names and channel names are two namespaces.

*If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*If* a channel of the interface exposes a transition whose name is not the name of a transition of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*When* the net builder builds the body, the subnet definition builds without its channels, every channel exposes a transition of the built body, no two channels have the same name, and no channel has the name of a port, building the subnet definition with its channels *shall* succeed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A channel can be declared with a name and a body transition.
2. The channel name is unique within its namespace.
3. The exposed transition's identity is preserved through the channel handle (see [MOD-011]).
4. A channel whose underlying transition is not present in the body net is rejected at build (see [MOD-006]).

**Test derivation:** Build an interface with one channel exposing a transition `attempt`; verify the channel handle resolves to the same transition identity in the renamed body. Attempt to declare two channels with the same name; verify rejection.

The channel name is unique within its namespace.
The exposed transition's identity is preserved through the channel handle (see [MOD-011]).
A channel whose underlying transition is not present in the body net is rejected at build (see [MOD-006]).

requirements.title: Subnet Validation at Build
requirements.testDerivation: Construct invalid subnets covering rejection cases 1 to 4; verify each fails at build with a message naming the offending element. Case 5 has no test: the subnet-definition builder takes only places, transitions, ports and channels, the net builder rejects none of these on its own, and `fromNet` ([MOD-014]) takes a net that is already built.

spans.text: *If* a port of the interface exposes a place that is not a place of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: *If* a channel of the interface exposes a transition whose name is not the name of a transition of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: *If* two ports of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: *If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *If* the net builder rejects the body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: *When* the net builder builds the body, every port exposes a place of the built body, every channel exposes a transition of the built body, and no two ports and no two channels have the same name, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed.
spans.label: s6

spans.text: *When* building the subnet definition fails, the error message *shall* contain the message with which the net builder rejected the body, or the name of a port or channel that meets one of the rejection cases 1 to 4.
spans.label: s7

paragraphs.text: Construction of a subnet definition MUST validate the interface against the body before producing an immutable result. The body is the net that the net builder builds, and the places and transitions of the body are those of that net ([CORE-040]). Validation MUST reject:

1. A port whose underlying place is not present in the body.
2. A channel whose underlying transition is not present in the body.
3. Duplicate port names within the interface.
4. Duplicate channel names within the interface.
5. A body that the net builder rejects ([CORE-040], [EXEC-042]).
Each failure MUST produce an error identifying the offending element by name.

Duplicate names (cases 3 and 4) do not depend on the body and may be checked before the body is built. Port names and channel names are two namespaces: a port and a channel may have the same name. This settles for subnet definitions the choice that [MOD-005] leaves to the implementation.

A channel whose transition has the name of no body transition is rejected in every implementation (case 2), and a channel over a transition of the body is accepted in every implementation. Whether a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a body transition is accepted is implementation-defined: Java and TypeScript compare transition objects and reject it, Rust and Python compare names and accept it. As in [TIME-010], the transitions of one body are assumed to have pairwise distinct names; no builder checks this.

Construction of a subnet definition MUST validate the interface against the body before producing an immutable result. The body is the net that the net builder builds, and the places and transitions of the body are those of that net ([CORE-040]). Validation MUST reject:
1. A port whose underlying place is not present in the body.
2. A channel whose underlying transition is not present in the body.
3. Duplicate port names within the interface.
4. Duplicate channel names within the interface.
5. A body that the net builder rejects ([CORE-040], [EXEC-042]).

Each failure MUST produce an error identifying the offending element by name.

Duplicate names (cases 3 and 4) do not depend on the body and may be checked before the body is built. Port names and channel names are two namespaces: a port and a channel may have the same name. This settles for subnet definitions the choice that [MOD-005] leaves to the implementation.

Whether a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a body transition is accepted is implementation-defined: Java and TypeScript compare transition objects and reject it, Rust and Python compare names and accept it. As in [TIME-010], the transitions of one body are assumed to have pairwise distinct names; no builder checks this.

A terminal place that the body declares ([EXEC-042]) and that no body transition consumes from or reads is not by itself a reason to reject at subnet build; `instantiate` and composition refuse such a body ([EXEC-042], [MOD-010]).

*If* a channel of the interface exposes a transition whose name is not the name of a transition of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*If* two ports of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*If* the net builder rejects the body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.

*When* the net builder builds the body, every port exposes a place of the built body, every channel exposes a transition of the built body, and no two ports and no two channels have the same name, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed.

*When* building the subnet definition fails, the error message *shall* contain the message with which the net builder rejected the body, or the name of a port or channel that meets one of the rejection cases 1 to 4.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Each rejection case above produces an error at subnet build, not later at instantiation or composition.
2. Error messages name the offending port, channel, place, or transition.
3. A valid subnet definition is immutable after build.

**Depends on:** [CORE-040], [CORE-041]
**Test derivation:** Construct invalid subnets covering rejection cases 1 to 4; verify each fails at build with a message naming the offending element. paragraphs.text: Implementations MUST provide a utility `fromNet(net, iface)` that constructs a subnet definition from an existing closed `PetriNet` plus an interface declaration whose ports and channels expose places and transitions of that net. This allows pre-existing nets to be wrapped as reusable subnet fragments without rebuilding them. It is also how a subnet definition whose body holds a composed instance is built, which nested instantiation needs ([MOD-013]).

The retrofit utility MUST validate the interface against the supplied net per [MOD-006] (port places exist, channel transitions exist, names unique). The net is already built, so the body rejection of [MOD-006] (case 5) does not arise. A net that declares terminal places ([EXEC-042]) is accepted by `fromNet` and refused when the definition is instantiated ([MOD-010]).

As in [MOD-006], a channel over a transition of the net is accepted and a channel whose transition has the name of no transition of the net is rejected. Whether a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a net transition is accepted is implementation-defined: Java and TypeScript compare transition objects and reject it, Rust and Python compare names and accept it. After a composition the net holds rewritten transitions, so a channel exposes the transition taken from the net.

An interface holds at most one port and at most one channel of each name in every implementation, because the interface builder rejects a second declaration of a name; `fromNet` checks the names again. Port names and channel names are two namespaces, as in [MOD-006].

*If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* `fromNet` *shall* fail.

*When* `fromNet` succeeds, the subnet definition *shall* have the net's name, the net's places, transitions and terminal places as its body, with the transitions in the net's order, and the given ports and channels as its interface.

requirements.title: Composition Operation (port mapping by structural rewrite)
requirements.testDerivation: Build subnet with port `out`; compose with `out -> P`; export the resulting net and a hand-written equivalent; assert structural equivalence.
