requirements.title: Name Identity
requirements.testDerivation: Construct `NameId("a")` twice; verify equal. Verify `NameId("a") < NameId("b")`. Verify a net with no match spec emits identical token events with and without the ν-net APIs linked. Run a two-branch join on a marking where two names can join and their earliest tokens differ, then the same join with its keys composed with a swap of the two names; verify that the renamed join fires with the renamed name, consumes the same tokens and leaves the same marking.

paragraphs.text: A **name** (`NameId`) is an opaque correlation identity, constructed from an underlying string value. Whether a matched transition is enabled, and which tokens its firing consumes, *shall* depend on the names its keys project only through name **equality** and, for the tie-break of [NU-020], the name order. The name order exists solely for that tie-break and carries no domain meaning.

*When* a matched transition fires with a chosen name, and a one-to-one renaming of names makes the renamed chosen name the chosen name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) of the same transition with every name its keys and relay targets project renamed, at the same marking, that renamed transition *shall* fire from that marking with the renamed chosen name, for the same emission, delivering the same tokens and leaving the same marking.

The name constructor *shall* return equal names for equal underlying values and different names for different underlying values. Each implementation *shall* order names by one fixed strict total order, the name order: if one name precedes another, the other does not precede it; if a first name precedes a second and the second precedes a third, the first precedes the third; and of two different names, one precedes the other. Of two names whose underlying values hold only Basic Multilingual Plane characters, one *shall* precede the other exactly when its value precedes the other's in the lexicographic order of code points. On other names the name order need not agree across implementations: Rust and Python order by code point, Java and TypeScript by UTF-16 code unit, and the two orders disagree on some names that hold supplementary-plane characters ([NU-020]).

Identity is a **projection of the token payload**, not a field on the token: a [NU-020] match (or the analyzer) declares a `value → NameId` key. The token model ([CORE-010]) is unchanged: no name field is added, so event ([EVT-011], [EVT-012]) and archive formats are unaffected.

transition with every name its keys and relay targets project renamed, at the same
marking, that renamed transition *shall* fire from that marking with the renamed
chosen name, for the same emission, delivering the same tokens and leaving the same
marking.

The name constructor *shall* return equal names for equal underlying values and
different names for different underlying values. Each implementation *shall* order
names by one fixed strict total order, the name order: if one name precedes another,
the other does not precede it; if a first name precedes a second and the second
precedes a third, the first precedes the third; and of two different names, one

[EVT-012]) and archive formats are unaffected.

1. Two names constructed from the same underlying value are equal; from

2. Names admit a stable total order consistent across a single implementation.
3. Adding ν-matching to a net does not change the token type or the on-the-wire
   shape of token-bearing events.
4. A one-to-one renaming of the names a join's keys project, which makes the
   renamed chosen name the chosen name of the renamed join, does not change which
   tokens the join consumes or the marking it leaves.

requirements.title: Fresh-Name Minting
requirements.testDerivation: A `fork` transition mints a name per firing and stamps both output branches; with three source tokens, verify three distinct names reach the downstream join and each pair merges (see `nu_fork_mints_unique_ids_then_join_merges`).

spans.text: *When* an action calls `freshName()`, the executor *shall* return a name that differs from every name it returned earlier in the same execution, whether the earlier call came in the same firing or in an earlier one.
spans.label: s1

spans.text: For a fixed scope and a fixed sequence of calling transitions, the executor *shall* return the same sequence of names to the `freshName()` calls, whichever firings the calls fall in.
spans.label: s2

spans.text: A declared mint that is not a transition of the net MUST be refused, by a failure or an `Unknown`, with the same reason naming it at every entry point (verification, script encoding ([VER-013]) and open-net verification ([VER-022])): `declared mint transition 'x' not in the net (NU-010)`, or `declared mint transitions 'a', 'b' not in the net (NU-010)` when several are not, each named once in code-point order.
spans.label: s3

spans.text: A refusal that does not depend on the declaration, such as a stop before the call starts ([VER-013]) or an unresolved property place ([VER-003]), may come first, and that refusal is then the answer.
spans.label: s4

spans.text: *When* a declared mint that has no input arc on a coloured place fires, every name it writes into a coloured place *shall* be a name it minted with `freshName()` in that firing.
spans.label: s5

spans.text: *When* a declared mint that has no input arc on a coloured place fires, every name it writes into coloured places *shall* be one and the same name, whether in one place or in several.
spans.label: s6

spans.text: The fragment classifier ([NU-051]) *shall* give the mint role only to a declared mint.
spans.label: s7

spans.text: *If* a transition without a match specification has no input arc on a coloured place, writes a coloured place and is not a declared mint, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role.
spans.label: s8

spans.text: *If* the timeout outcome of a transition writes a coloured place, *then* the fragment classifier *shall not* give it the mint role.
spans.label: s9

spans.text: *If* a transition without a match specification has no input arc on a coloured place and its timeout outcome writes a coloured place, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role.
spans.label: s10

Minted names MUST be unique across all firings of a single execution and MUST be deterministic for a fixed scope ([NU-011]) and a fixed sequence of calling transitions (replay stability). So the names follow the order of the `freshName()` calls, not the order of the firings: with one minting action in flight at a time the two orders agree, and actions that run concurrently may call the minter in either order. The executor installs the minter, one counter shared by all its transitions ([NU-011]); absent an executor-installed minter, a fallback still guarantees uniqueness.

*When* an action calls `freshName()`, the executor *shall* return a name that differs from every name it returned earlier in the same execution, whether the earlier call came in the same firing or in an earlier one.
For a fixed scope and a fixed sequence of calling transitions, the executor *shall* return the same sequence of names to the `freshName()` calls, whichever firings the calls fall in.

What replays is the sequence **within a minting scope** ([NU-011]). Under the default scope the scope component of a name differs from run to run by design (that is what keeps a resumed execution from re-minting a live name), so a host that needs the *whole* name reproduced pins the scope, and a test compares names structurally or pins one rather than hard-coding a default-scope name.

- by naming it as a mint transition on the verifier (`mintTransitions` / `mint_transitions`);
- by its consuming a declared budget place ([NU-040]), whose token is what a fork consumes when it mints.

requirements.title: Resume-Safe Fresh-Name Minting
requirements.testDerivation: Run a ν-fork net under a **pinned** scope until a token carrying a minted name awaits its sibling at a join; snapshot and restore into a fresh execution under a different pinned scope — and again under the default one; fire the fork and assert the new name differs from the restored one and that the join does not merge the restored token with the new one. Repeat the restore twice concurrently and assert the two name sets are disjoint. No test may depend on how many executors the process constructed before it: compare names structurally (transition, scope, counter) or pin the scope, and include a case in which the resuming executor is the first one constructed.

paragraphs.text: [NU-010] scopes minted-name uniqueness to "a single execution". Restoring a marking ([CORE-073]) begins a **new** execution whose initial marking already holds names minted by the previous one. An implementation that satisfies [NU-010] by counting firings from zero therefore re-mints names that are already live — and because a [NU-020] join correlates on name equality alone, the collision does not surface as an error: it silently correlates tokens from different run segments, merging a restored token with an unrelated fresh one.

Names minted by an execution seeded from a restored marking MUST NOT collide with names minted by any other execution in the same restore lineage, other than a replay of the same segment (AC3), whether or not those names are still present in that marking. The mechanism is not prescribed. Two that satisfy it:

- a per-execution **scope** supplied by the host and incorporated into every minted name;
- carrying the minter's high-water mark in the snapshot and resuming strictly above it.

Under the scope mechanism, names minted under two different accepted scopes never collide, so the guarantee rests on the executions of a lineage running under different scopes: the default scope is drawn at random per executor (below), and a pinned scope is the host's promise. A replay that re-runs a segment under its pinned scope, from the marking the segment started from and with the same `freshName()` calls, mints the segment's names again, which is AC3, not a collision between segments. A name the host writes into a token itself, such as a copied correlation id, is not a minted name and is not covered.

**The restore lineage crosses processes.** [CORE-073] offers restore as a suspend boundary, a durable checkpoint, a crash-recovery point — so the execution that resumes a marking is, in the normal case, running in a *different process* from the one that minted the names in it. "Unique per executor" read as "unique within a process" is therefore not enough. Anything derived from a per-process counter restarts with the process, and the first executor of the new process re-mints the first name of the old one: exactly the silent merge above, in the default configuration.

**The default scope MUST be unique across processes — and is therefore not the run identifier.** Absent a host-supplied scope, an implementation using the scope mechanism MUST draw one per executor from the platform's random source: a 128-bit value rendered as exactly **32 lowercase hexadecimal characters**, of which at least 122 bits are random (a version-4 UUID with its dashes removed conforms). The rendering is fixed so that a default-scope name looks alike, and parses alike, in every language.

An earlier revision of this requirement said that an implementation which already publishes a run identifier SHOULD default the scope to it, "so one value means one thing". **That SHOULD is withdrawn**, because the two values are required to have opposite properties. A run identifier SHOULD be *reproducible* for a fixed construction order ([TIME-015] AC#14) — that is what lets a replay carry the same identifier, and it is what a per-process counter provides. A default scope MUST *differ* between two processes that did nothing differently — which is precisely what a reproducible value cannot do. One value cannot be both. The run identifier remains the reproducible one, the default scope is the unique one, and an implementation MUST NOT derive either from the other.

**The scope's uniqueness is required; its observability is not.** The default scope MAY be entirely internal — an implementation is not required to publish it, on an event or anywhere else, and MUST NOT be read as required to merely to satisfy this requirement. What a host can observe is the *name*, and the property that matters is that two executors never mint the same one. An implementation whose scope is internal therefore conforms exactly as one whose scope is visible, and the difference is not a divergence in behaviour.

**The name format, and what a scope may contain.** An implementation using the scope mechanism mints `<transition>#<scope>:<n>`, where `<n>` is a per-executor counter from zero. A host-supplied scope MUST be rejected when the executor is configured — not at the first mint — if it is **empty** or contains **`:`** or **`#`**; the separators are rejected rather than escaped. Two details are fixed because the implementations otherwise drift apart on them:

- *Empty* means length zero. A whitespace-only scope is legal, if unwise; an implementation MUST NOT trim the scope or test it for blankness, since "blank" is defined differently by every standard library and the same configuration would then be accepted in one language and refused in another.
- Rejecting `:` alone is **not** enough. Transition `a` under scope `b#c` and transition `a#b` under scope `c` both mint `a#b#c:0` — a collision between two segments of one lineage, which is what this requirement forbids. With `#` banned as well, a minted name parses uniquely whatever the transition name contains: the **last `:`** splits off the counter, and the **last `#` before it** splits off the scope; everything in front is the transition name.
A pinned scope is host text, so it SHOULD stay within the Basic Multilingual Plane for the reason given under [NU-020]'s tie-break; this is advice to the host, not a validation.

Deriving the floor by scanning the restored marking is **not** sufficient in general: name carrying values are opaque to the engine ([VER-004]), and a name minted into a token that has since been consumed leaves no trace in the marking while remaining live in host state and in any token the host holds across the restore.

Replay stability ([NU-010] AC3) is preserved **within** a run segment: for a fixed scope (or a fixed restored high-water mark) and a fixed order of `freshName()` calls, the minted sequence MUST be reproducible. The firing order fixes the order of the calls when at most one minting action is in flight at a time, or when every call is made inline by a synchronous action. Randomness is therefore admitted in exactly **one** place — the *default* scope, chosen once per executor — and nowhere else: the counter `<n>` MUST NOT be random, and a scope the host pinned MUST be used verbatim, with nothing random mixed into it or into the sequence minted under it. A host that needs a reproducible segment pins its scope (AC3). A host that pins nothing gets uniqueness instead of reproducibility, and that is the right default: an unreproducible name is visible and harmless, a cross-segment merge is neither.
*If* a host-supplied scope is empty or contains `:` or `#`, *then* the executor *shall* reject it when it is configured.
The executor *shall* accept a host-supplied scope that is not empty and contains neither `:` nor `#`, a whitespace-only scope included.

*Where* an executor uses the scope mechanism, the `i`-th `freshName()` call it answers, counting from zero across all its firings and transitions, *shall* return `<t>#<s>:<i>` with `i` written in decimal, where `t` is the name of the calling transition and `s` is the executor's scope, verbatim as the host pinned it or as it was drawn by default.
*Where* executors use the scope mechanism, no name minted by an execution under one accepted scope *shall* equal a name minted by an execution under a different accepted scope.

*Where* an executor is given no scope, the executor *shall* draw its scope from the platform's random source as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, which neither its construction order nor its run identifier determines.

A host *shall not* pin one scope for two executions of one restore lineage, except for a replay: an execution that re-runs an earlier segment, after it and not alongside it, from the marking that segment started from and with the same `freshName()` calls.

**The name format, and what a scope may contain.** An implementation using the scope mechanism
mints `<transition>#<scope>:<n>`, where `<n>` is a per-executor counter from zero. A host-supplied
scope MUST be rejected when the executor is configured — not at the first mint — if it is **empty**
or contains **`:`** or **`#`**; the separators are rejected rather than escaped. Two details are
fixed because the implementations otherwise drift apart on them:

- *Empty* means length zero. A whitespace-only scope is legal, if unwise; an implementation MUST
  NOT trim the scope or test it for blankness, since "blank" is defined differently by every
  standard library and the same configuration would then be accepted in one language and refused
  in another.
- Rejecting `:` alone is **not** enough. Transition `a` under scope `b#c` and transition `a#b`
  under scope `c` both mint `a#b#c:0` — a collision between two segments of one lineage, which is
  what this requirement forbids. With `#` banned as well, a minted name parses uniquely whatever
  the transition name contains: the **last `:`** splits off the counter, and the **last `#` before
  it** splits off the scope; everything in front is the transition name.

A pinned scope is host text, so it SHOULD stay within the Basic Multilingual Plane for the reason
given under [NU-020]'s tie-break; this is advice to the host, not a validation.

Deriving the floor by scanning the restored marking is **not** sufficient in general: name
carrying values are opaque to the engine ([VER-004]), and a name minted into a token that has
since been consumed leaves no trace in the marking while remaining live in host state and in
any token the host holds across the restore.

Replay stability ([NU-010] AC3) is preserved **within** a run segment: for a fixed scope (or
a fixed restored high-water mark) and a fixed order of `freshName()` calls, the minted
sequence MUST be reproducible. The firing order fixes the order of the calls when at most one
minting action is in flight at a time, or when every call is made inline by a synchronous
action. Randomness is therefore admitted in exactly **one** place — the *default* scope,
chosen once per executor — and nowhere else: the counter `<n>` MUST NOT be random, and a scope
the host pinned MUST be used verbatim, with nothing random mixed into it or into the sequence
minted under it. A host that needs a reproducible segment pins its scope (AC3). A host that pins
nothing gets uniqueness instead of reproducibility, and that is the right default: an
unreproducible name is visible and harmless, a cross-segment merge is neither.

*If* a host-supplied scope is empty or contains `:` or `#`, *then* the executor *shall* reject it when it is configured.

The executor *shall* accept a host-supplied scope that is not empty and contains neither `:` nor `#`, a whitespace-only scope included.

*Where* an executor uses the scope mechanism, the `i`-th `freshName()` call it answers, counting from zero across all its firings and transitions, *shall* return `<t>#<s>:<i>` with `i` written in decimal, where `t` is the name of the calling transition and `s` is the executor's scope, verbatim as the host pinned it or as it was drawn by default.

*Where* executors use the scope mechanism, no name minted by an execution under one accepted scope *shall* equal a name minted by an execution under a different accepted scope.

*Where* an executor is given no scope, the executor *shall* draw its scope from the platform's random source as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, which neither its construction order nor its run identifier determines.

A host *shall not* pin one scope for two executions of one restore lineage, except for a replay: an execution that re-runs an earlier segment, after it and not alongside it, from the marking that segment started from and with the same `freshName()` calls.

1. Restore a marking holding a name `n` minted by a prior execution; run the resumed
   execution, under the default scope or a pinned scope other than the prior execution's, so
   it mints at least as many names as the original minted; no minted name equals `n`.
2. A restored token awaiting its sibling at a [NU-020] join is not correlated with a
   freshly minted token of the resumed segment.
3. For a fixed scope and a fixed order of `freshName()` calls, two runs from the same restored
   marking mint the identical name sequence.
4. Two concurrent executions restored from the same snapshot, under the default scope or under
   two different pinned scopes, mint disjoint name sets.
5. **The default scope is not process-local.** An executor given no scope mints names whose scope
   component is 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, different for every executor and — where
   the implementation publishes a run identifier — not equal to it. AC1 and AC2 therefore hold
   when the resuming executor is the *first* one constructed in its process, which is the case a
   per-process counter fails.
6. **Scope validation and the parse rule.** An empty scope, a scope containing `:` and a scope
   containing `#` are each rejected at configuration; a whitespace-only scope is accepted. A name
   minted by a transition whose own name contains `#` and `:` splits back into transition, scope
   and counter by the rule above.

from the restored one and that the join does not merge the restored token with the new one.
Repeat the restore twice concurrently and assert the two name sets are disjoint. No test may
depend on how many executors the process constructed before it: compare names structurally
(transition, scope, counter) or pin the scope, and include a case in which the resuming executor
is the first one constructed.

requirements.body:
A transition MAY declare a **match specification**: a subset of its **input**
places, each with a key projection from a token's value to a `NameId` or to no name. Every
place named by the match MUST also be a declared input. The match adds a correlation
requirement on top of the existing input cardinalities ([IO-001]–[IO-004]):

- **Enablement** = the usual cardinality/bitmap/inhibitor checks ([CORE-022])
  **and** there exists a single name `n` present in *every* correlated input
  with at least that input's required count of key-projecting-to-`n` tokens.
- **Firing** consumes, for the chosen `n`, the matched tokens from each
  correlated input (FIFO within a name); non-correlated inputs consume FIFO as
  usual ([EXEC-010]).

A key projection may yield no name for a token (a value of another type, a projection that
returns no value): such a token has no name on that input, so that input never matches it and
never consumes it.

A match names each correlated input once: the input's cardinality, not a repeated key, sets how
many tokens of the name it takes. Building a match or a transition whose match keys one place
twice MUST fail. A match builder given fewer than two keys MUST fail; a construction path that is
not a match builder (Rust `MatchSpec::from_keys`, a TypeScript object literal) leaves that minimum
to the caller. Every correlated input requires at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]).

**Build.** The match checks run after every other build-time check of the transition: a place
keyed twice, then a key on a place that is not an input place, then the relay checks of
[NU-054]. The first check that fails names the error.

*If* a match builder is given fewer than two keys, *then* building the match *shall* fail.

*If* a match specification keys one place twice, *then* building the match *shall* fail.

Building a match from two or more keys on distinct places *shall* succeed.

*If* a transition fails to build without its match specification, *then* building it with the match specification *shall* fail.

*If* the match specification of a transition keys one place twice, *then* building the transition *shall* fail.

*If* the match specification of a transition keys a place that is not an input place of the transition, *then* building the transition *shall* fail.

Building a transition with a match specification *shall* succeed when the transition builds without the match, the match keys distinct input places of the transition, and the match declares each relay target once and as an output place of the transition ([NU-054]).

**Enablement and the chosen name.**

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, it *shall* be enabled on its token counts ([CORE-022]).

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, every correlated input *shall* hold at least one token of the chosen name and at least its required count of tokens of that name.

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, no other name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens *shall* have an earlier earliest `createdAt` among its tokens in the correlated inputs than the chosen name, or the same and precede it in the name order.

**Firing.**

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, its action *shall* receive from each correlated input the first tokens of the chosen name in queue order, as many as the consumption count of the input arc with `available` the number of tokens of the chosen name in the place ([IO-007]).

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, each correlated input that is not one of its reset places *shall* end the firing holding the tokens it did not deliver, in their order, followed by the tokens the firing deposited there.

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, its deposit *shall* be one its output spec offers for the tokens the firing takes ([IO-013], [IO-015]).

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, its read arcs *shall* deliver the head of each read place after the inputs are taken ([EXEC-012]).

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, each of its reset places *shall* end the firing holding only the tokens the firing deposited there ([CORE-034]).

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, each place that is not a correlated input *shall* deliver to its action, and keep, the tokens it would without the match specification: the tokens at the head of its queue, as many as the consumption count of its input arc and none without one, and, unless it is a reset place, the rest of its queue in order followed by the tokens the firing deposited there ([EXEC-010], [EXEC-020]).

**Determinism (tie-break).** When more than one name satisfies the join, the
implementation MUST choose by this exact rule, so all languages fire identically on names whose
values hold only Basic Multilingual Plane characters ([NU-001]):
1. the name whose earliest `createdAt` among all tokens carrying the name in the correlated
   inputs is **earliest**, whether the firing consumes those tokens or not;
2. ties broken by **name order** ([NU-001]).

> The name-order tie-break is byte-identical across implementations for **BMP**
> names. An executor-minted name is `"{transition}#{scope}:{n}"` ([NU-011]): its
> default scope and its counter are ASCII, so it is BMP exactly when the
> transition name — and the scope, where a host pinned one — is. Both of those
> are host text and fall under the same caveat as a user-supplied key: for
> supplementary-plane code points, Rust's code-point order can differ from the
> Java/TypeScript UTF-16 code-unit order; [NU-001] requires only
> per-implementation consistency, which holds.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. A join correlates by name, not arrival order: with branch A = [X@t0, Y@t1] and
   branch B = [Y@t0, X@t1], the join produces the X-X and Y-Y pairings, never X-Y.
2. With no name present in all correlated inputs, the join is not enabled; its
   input tokens remain.
3. A correlated `Exactly(k)` / `AtLeast(m)` input requires k / m tokens **of the
   matched name**; `All` consumes all tokens of the matched name.
4. The tie-break selects the name with the earliest `createdAt` among its tokens in the
   correlated inputs, then the least name in the name order; implementations agree on names of

5. A match that keys one place twice is rejected when the match is built, and when a
   transition is built with such a match from any other construction path (a bindings layer,
   a composition remap, an object literal).

**Test derivation:** `nu_join_matches_by_name_not_fifo` (reversed arrival),
`nu_join_blocks_without_matching_name`, mirrored across every executor in every

spans.text: *When* a transition fires, it *shall* also fire with the same chosen name from every marking that differs from its marking only by a pairing its keys and relay targets cannot tell apart, for every emission that differs from its emission by the same pairing, delivering tokens and leaving a marking that differ from its own by the same pairing.
spans.label: s1

spans.label: s2

spans.label: s3

paragraphs.text: Name correlation ([NU-020]) is the **only** per-token filter the enablement check applies. There is no unary value predicate on an input: guards were removed in [IO-006] and no implementation carries one, so token selection is determined by position ([EXEC-010], [IO-007]) and, on correlated inputs, by name equality, with the chosen name picked by the tie-break of [NU-020], which reads names and `createdAt` only. Nothing else about a token's value is read.

A pairing of values says, for each place, which pairs of values may stand in for each other there. A transition's keys and relay targets cannot tell a pairing apart when every key on a place, and every relay target at a place, projects the two values of each pair on that place to the same name or to no name. On a place that no key and no relay target reads, a pairing may pair any two values, and a transition without a match specification has no keys, so for it any pairing qualifies. Two markings differ by a pairing when every place holds as many tokens in both and the tokens at the same queue position of a place have the same `createdAt` and values the pairing pairs on that place. Two emissions, or two deliveries, differ by a pairing when they hold such tokens on the same places in the same order.

*When* a transition fires, it *shall* also fire with the same chosen name from every marking that differs from its marking only by a pairing its keys and relay targets cannot tell apart, for every emission that differs from its emission by the same pairing, delivering tokens and leaving a marking that differ from its own by the same pairing.
*When* a transition with a match specification fires, every token it delivers from a correlated input *shall* project to the chosen name under that input's key.

*When* a transition with a match specification fires, each correlated input that is not one of its reset places *shall* end the firing holding, of the tokens that do not project to the chosen name, exactly the ones it held before, in their order, followed by the ones the firing deposited there, in the order deposited.

*Note (non-normative).* Should a future revision reintroduce a unary input filter, the intended composition order is: the filter applies **first** and the name correlation runs over the survivors, so a token must pass the filter *and* project to the chosen name to be consumed. No implementation has such a filter today.

spans.label: s1

paragraphs.text: When more than one correlation name is simultaneously eligible at a matched transition, the implementation MUST select the name with the smallest `(oldest correlated-token timestamp, then NameId)` ordering: oldest first, ties broken by name. The selection is a pure function of the current marking and MUST be **identical across all conforming implementations** on names whose values hold only Basic Multilingual Plane characters ([NU-001]): the firing tie-break (`selectMatchName` / `select_match_name`) is byte-identical on such names, and any incremental acceleration of it MUST return byte-identical results to the reference function. A token a `ForwardInput` forwards on a timeout outcome keeps its original `created_at` in every implementation ([IO-014]), so a name whose oldest correlated token was forwarded orders the same everywhere.

A name is eligible at a matched transition when the match keys at least one input and every correlated input holds at least one token of the name and at least the input's required count of such tokens; a token whose key yields no name counts for no name ([NU-020]). The oldest correlated-token timestamp of a name is the earliest `createdAt` among all tokens of the name in the correlated inputs, whether the firing consumes them or not.
*If* some name is eligible at a matched transition, *then* the selection *shall* return a name.
*When* the selection returns a name, that name *shall* be eligible, and no eligible name *shall* precede it in the order by oldest correlated-token timestamp, then by name order.

When more than one correlation name is simultaneously eligible at a matched
transition, the implementation MUST select the name with the smallest
`(oldest correlated-token timestamp, then NameId)` ordering: oldest first, ties
broken by name. The selection is a pure function of the current marking and MUST
be **identical across all conforming implementations** on names whose values hold only Basic
Multilingual Plane characters ([NU-001]): the firing tie-break
(`selectMatchName` / `select_match_name`) is byte-identical on such names, and any incremental
acceleration of it MUST return byte-identical results to the reference function.
A token a `ForwardInput` forwards on a timeout outcome keeps its original `created_at` in
every implementation ([IO-014]), so a name whose oldest correlated token was forwarded
orders the same everywhere.

A name is eligible at a matched transition when the match keys at least one input and every
correlated input holds at least one token of the name and at least the input's required count of
such tokens; a token whose key yields no name counts for no name ([NU-020]). The oldest
correlated-token timestamp of a name is the earliest `createdAt` among all tokens of the name in
the correlated inputs, whether the firing consumes them or not.

*If* some name is eligible at a matched transition, *then* the selection *shall* return a name.

*When* the selection returns a name, that name *shall* be eligible, and no eligible name *shall* precede it in the order by oldest correlated-token timestamp, then by name order.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given the same eligible *(name → correlated-token timestamps)* state, every
   implementation selects the same `NameId`.
2. An incremental matcher returns the same `NameId` as the reference
   `selectMatchName` for any sequence of add/consume operations.
3. `NameId` ordering is byte-identical for ASCII/BMP names (an executor-minted
   name is one whenever its transition name and any host-pinned scope are — the
   default scope and the counter are ASCII; [NU-011]); supplementary-plane code
   points MAY order differently per
   [NU-001] (UTF-8 byte order vs UTF-16 code-unit order).

**Depends on:** [NU-020], [NU-001]
**Test derivation:** A randomised differential test (`MatchEngineIncrementalTest`,
`incremental_matches_select_byte_for_byte`, `incremental-matcher.test.ts`) asserts
the incremental `best()` equals `selectMatchName` over non-monotonic timestamps.
acceptance: Given the same eligible *(name → correlated-token timestamps)* state, every implementation selects the same `NameId`.
An incremental matcher returns the same `NameId` as the reference `selectMatchName` for any sequence of add/consume operations.

`NameId` ordering is byte-identical for ASCII/BMP names (an executor-minted name is one whenever its transition name and any host-pinned scope are — the default scope and the counter are ASCII; [NU-011]); supplementary-plane code points MAY order differently per [NU-001] (UTF-8 byte order vs UTF-16 code-unit order).

paragraphs.text: A correlated input behaves, under channel composition ([MOD-021]), as the input arc it layers on: its arc dedup/conflict rules are unchanged. A merge MUST NOT silently drop a match, and no implementation fuses two matches into one: when both merged sides carry a match, whatever places the two matches correlate, the merge MUST be rejected with an error naming the caller-side transition.

*When* at most one side of a channel merge carries a match, the channel merge *shall* reject with the same error when the same merge of the two transitions without their matches rejects, and otherwise *shall* give the merged transition of that merge with that side's match unchanged, or with no match when neither side carries one.
*If* both sides of a channel merge carry a match, *then* the channel merge *shall* be rejected with an error that names the caller-side transition.

A correlated input is therefore merged by the canonical input-arc merge table like any other input arc: a correlated `one()` and the other side's `one()` on the same place give one `exactly(2)` arc that the surviving match still correlates. The other side's token on that place is then a token of the chosen name, not the oldest token. Which error a merge reports when it also breaks a rule of [MOD-021] is not specified.

A correlated input behaves, under channel composition ([MOD-021]), as the input
arc it layers on: its arc dedup/conflict rules are unchanged. A merge MUST NOT
silently drop a match, and no implementation fuses two matches into one: when both
merged sides carry a match, whatever places the two matches correlate, the merge
MUST be rejected with an error naming the caller-side transition.

*When* at most one side of a channel merge carries a match, the channel merge *shall* reject with the same error when the same merge of the two transitions without their matches rejects, and otherwise *shall* give the merged transition of that merge with that side's match unchanged, or with no match when neither side carries one.

*If* both sides of a channel merge carry a match, *then* the channel merge *shall* be rejected with an error that names the caller-side transition.

A correlated input is therefore merged by the canonical input-arc merge table like any
other input arc: a correlated `one()` and the other side's `one()` on the same place give
one `exactly(2)` arc that the surviving match still correlates. The other side's token on
that place is then a token of the chosen name, not the oldest token. Which error a merge reports
when it also breaks a rule of [MOD-021] is not specified.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Composing a transition that carries a match with a side that carries none
   preserves the match on the flat net (it is not dropped).
2. A merge of two transitions that both carry a match is rejected with an error
   naming the caller-side transition, whatever places the two matches correlate.

**Depends on:** [MOD-021], [NU-020], [NU-054]
**Test derivation:** Channel-merge a matched transition with a passthrough side;
verify the composed transition still correlates. Channel-merge two matched transitions
whose matches key different places; verify the merge is rejected naming the caller-side
transition.
acceptance: Composing a transition that carries a match with a side that carries none preserves the match on the flat net (it is not dropped).
A merge of two transitions that both carry a match is rejected with an error naming the caller-side transition, whatever places the two matches correlate.

paragraphs.text: Be explicit about the cliff. **Safety / coverability** for the ν-fragment is **decidable** [RV-08]: the marking-with-names state space is a well-structured transition system. Full **reachability / liveness** with *unbounded* fresh names and *unbounded* recirculation is **undecidable** in general (ν-PN reachability is undecidable [RV-11]).

A **bounded budget** is the decidability lever, not merely operational hygiene. Model it structurally: a typed `Budget` place pre-seeded with `k` tokens whose single token a fork consumes when it mints a name and a join (or a dead-letter transition) returns. Then:

- "at most `k` live correlation groups" is the structural invariant `PlaceBound(Budget, k)` ([VER-002]); once the budget place is declared to the verifier, it is checkable with the existing untimed encoder, no name reasoning required;
- a `Pending` place (one token per live group, emptied only by join or dead-letter; a correlation group is live from the fork that mints its name until a join or dead-letter takes its `Pending` token) plus `PlaceBound(Pending, k)` and quiescence ([VER-002]) to `Pending = 0` expresses **"every forked name is joined or dead-lettered by the time the net comes to rest."**

With the budget bounded and branch places `PlaceBound`-checked, fresh names are drawn from a finite live pool, the WSTS stays finite, and these properties become provable. This is the [reask/retry-budget-as-typed-place] discipline applied to correlation.

Declaring a budget place to the verifier also declares the mint contract of [NU-010] for every transition that has an input arc on it: where such a transition writes a coloured place without consuming one, the ν routes read the write as a fresh name.
*Where* a place is declared to the verifier as a budget place, the ν routes *shall* read every transition that has an input arc on that place as a declared mint ([NU-010]).
The ν routes *shall* read a transition named as a mint transition on the verifier (`mintTransitions` / `mint_transitions`) as a declared mint, whatever budget places are declared.
The ν routes *shall* read a transition as a declared mint only when it is named as a mint transition on the verifier or has an input arc on a place declared to the verifier as a budget place.
A read, inhibitor or reset arc on a budget place declares nothing.

**JoinedOrDeadLettered.** The property `JoinedOrDeadLettered(pending)` says that no correlation group is left behind when the net comes to rest: no reachable quiescent marking holds a `pending` token. A run that never comes to rest does not violate it.

Every route that decides `JoinedOrDeadLettered(pending)` *shall* count a marking as violating it when the marking is quiescent ([VER-002]) and `pending` holds a token, whether or not a declared sink place is marked.
Every route that decides `JoinedOrDeadLettered(pending)` *shall* count a marking as violating it only when the marking is quiescent and `pending` holds a token.

In that quiescence a transition with a match specification *shall* count as enabled exactly when it is enabled as [NU-020] says: on its token counts, and with a name of which every correlated input holds at least one token and at least its required count; a match that correlates no input is never enabled.
A route that reads enablement on token counts alone does not decide `JoinedOrDeadLettered(pending)` on a net with a transition that has a match specification, and answers `Unknown` there ([NU-050]).

paragraphs.text: The untimed encoder is value-blind ([VER-004]). For ν-nets this is relaxed under a carve-out: a matched transition's **name equality** is encoded **exactly** rather than name-blind, so a counterexample that silently equates two *different* names (criterion **#1** below) is ruled out. The name dimension is the projection declared at the match ([NU-001]) — the analyzer treats it as name-symmetric.
The exactness goal MAY be realized by either of two routes:

- **Route A — bounded name-colouring** (the budget made literal). Names are modeled as a finite set of `k` **colours**, where `k` is the colour-slot bound of [NU-053], at least the number of live names: each coloured place becomes `k` per-colour counts, a mint introduces a *globally fresh* colour, and a join consumes the **same** colour from every correlated input, so no counterexample equates two different names. It stays in linear arithmetic, and its `Proven` is sound while the declared mints and the coloured consumers keep their contracts ([NU-010], [NU-051]). It applies to the **mint → matched-join fragment**: coloured places (the matched inputs) are produced only by minting forks and consumed only by matched joins, each mint is declared ([NU-010]), **a colour-slot bound exists** ([NU-053]), and coloured places carry no inhibitor/read/reset arc. A net outside this fragment, including one with no colour-slot bound, falls back to the sound over-approximation (criterion #1 then holds only where the exact route was taken).
- **Route B — SCG name-partition** (implemented). A **state-class-graph quotient partitioned by name relations**: each correlation token carries an abstract, interchangeable name-*symbol*, a matched join fires only on a name shared by every correlated input, and the graph is quotiented under name-permutation symmetry (the canonical key abstracts the symbol identities, which is what keeps it finite without a budget). This generalises the exactness **beyond the bounded fragment** — to budget-less but structurally name-bounded nets, to **name × time** (the DBM firing zone rides alongside the name partition), and to **quiescence** (deadlock / joined-or-dead-lettered, decided over the name-aware terminal classes). It is sound for every executor run, and complete for the free-choice name semantics the graph explores ([VER-012]) whenever the symbolic graph closes within the class bound; an unbounded live-name pool surfaces as graph truncation, which never yields `Proven`. The alternative realization — equality over an uninterpreted **name sort** (EUF) in the CHC encoder — is not taken (the SMT path is untimed, and Spacer over an uninterpreted sort is poorly supported).

When the live correlation-name pool is **not bounded** — no budget ([NU-040]) and no structural bound the name-partition quotient (Route B) can discover — the verifier MUST NOT return an unsound verdict (criterion **#2** below, mirroring the `Ignore`-mode discipline of [VER-006]); under Route B this appears as state-class-graph truncation, and the verdict is `Unknown` unless the prefix rule below finds a violating class.
**The verdict on a built graph.** Route B reads its verdict off the classes its build stored, in discovery order, by the prefix rule of [VER-012] AC3.
*If* the build of the Route B graph is stopped, because it runs out of total budget or is cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* Route B *shall* answer `Unknown`, whatever classes the build stored.

*If* the build is not stopped and a stored class violates a safety property, or an expanded class at which the net rests violates a quiescence property, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Violated`, also when the graph does not close.

*If* Route B answers `Violated`, *then* the class its counterexample ends at *shall* violate the property: a stored class for a safety property, an expanded class at which the net rests for a quiescence property.
*If* the build is not stopped and no class violates the property, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` when the graph closes and `Unknown` when it does not.
*If* the Route B graph does not close, *then* Route B *shall not* answer `Proven`.

Under modelled injection ([VER-006]) Route B treats an environment place as an inexhaustible input and so cannot observe its count or the names injected into it; it declines (`Unknown`) when a verdict would depend on them ([VER-006] AC8).

On a timed net Route B gives a matched join a clock only while one name-symbol is present in every correlated input, because the executor enables the join only then ([NU-020]). A join whose inputs hold tokens but share no name has no clock, so its latest bound constrains no other firing. The clock-restart rule of [TIME-012] reads the name layer too: a firing after which no name is present in every correlated input restarts the join's clock, even when the inputs still hold tokens, and a join whose inputs come to share a name starts a fresh clock then. This holds with and without the latest-bound relaxation for a late executor ([TIME-013]).

*While* a transition is not enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]), Route B *shall* hold no clock for it, even when its inputs hold the tokens its arcs require but no name is present in every correlated input.

*When* a transition fires and another transition `j` holds a clock and is not enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) in the intermediate marking ([TIME-012]), Route B *shall* take `j`'s clock away, even when `j`'s inputs still hold tokens, and *shall* give `j` a fresh clock if the firing leaves `j` enabled with an eligible name.

*When* a transition fires and another transition `j` holds a clock and is enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) before the firing, in the intermediate marking and after the firing, Route B *shall* keep `j`'s clock.
*When* a firing leaves a transition `j` enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) and `j` held no clock before it, Route B *shall* start `j`'s clock at that firing.
*When* a transition fires, Route B *shall* take its clock away and *shall* give it a fresh clock if the firing leaves it enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]).

*While* time passes, Route B *shall* keep the marking and the start of the clock of every transition enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]), and *shall* advance the clock reading by the time that passed.
Route B *shall* fire a transition only when it holds a clock that has run for at least the transition's earliest bound ([TIME-001]), and *shall* leave the clock reading unchanged at a firing.

Route B reads every coloured token through one name. It assumes that each key and relay projection reading a coloured place returns the name its writer put there: the name a mint stamped, or the name a relay or consumer carried over. The analysis cannot inspect a projection, so this is a contract on the net, like the mint contract of [NU-010]. Two projections that read one place differently, or a projection that returns no name for a written token, fall outside it.

Both routes read a coloured write as a fresh name only for a declared mint ([NU-010]), and as the consumed name only for a coloured consumer ([NU-051]). A write the executor makes on timeout is read by what it is: a forward carries the consumed token's name and a unit token has none. Where no role reads a coloured write faithfully, the net is outside both routes.
**Soundness.** Both routes are sound against the untimed executor, with no environment place, while the projections and the actions keep the contracts above.

*If* the coloured places start empty, every transition is in the fragment for its role, every key and relay projection reads the name its writer put there, and every declared mint and coloured consumer keeps its contract ([NU-010], [NU-051]), *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for a safety property only if no marking the untimed executor reaches violates it.

*If* in addition every correlated input takes at least one token, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for a quiescence property only if no marking the untimed executor reaches and rests at violates it.

*If* Route A builds its plan with the colour-slot bound of [NU-053], every key and relay projection reads the name its writer put there, and every declared mint and coloured consumer keeps its contract, *then* a `Proven` of the coloured encoding of a safety property *shall* hold of every marking the untimed executor reaches.
*If* in addition no transition of the net is reapable, *then* a `Proven` of the coloured encoding of a quiescence property *shall* hold of every marking the untimed executor reaches and rests at.

paragraphs.text: The [NU-050] Route B name-partition quotient decides the **mint → matched-join** fragment exactly. An opt-in **EXTENDED** fragment mode widens that exact path to two further shapes without weakening its soundness: a **coloured consumer** (drain/relay) that removes a correlation name without a match, and **carrier places** that thread a fork-minted name through intermediate places to a ν-join input. The mode is a two-value knob — **BASE** (default) reproduces the shipped mint → matched-join fragment exactly; **EXTENDED** is selected on the verifier builder (`fragmentMode` / `fragment_mode`). Both are decided by the solver-free Route B quotient, and by Route A where [NU-053] is offered; neither changes the canonical name-partition key format ([VER-012]), so cross-language byte compatibility is preserved.

- **Coloured consumer (drain/relay).** Under EXTENDED, a transition with **no** match spec MAY consume a coloured place. The analyzer admits it only as a drain/relay role and only when it consumes **exactly one** coloured input at count **exactly one** ([IO-001] `One` or [IO-002] `Exactly(1)`). *While* the fragment mode is BASE, the fragment classifier *shall* give no role to a transition without a match spec that consumes a coloured place. *While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, *if* a transition without a match spec consumes exactly one coloured input, at count one, has no reset, read or inhibitor arc on a coloured place, puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch, into each coloured place the branch writes, and on timeout writes a coloured place only by forwarding that input, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it the coloured-consumer role of that input's place, whether or not it is declared a mint. A coloured consumer **relays** the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch (threading the same name), or **drains** it (dead-letters the name) on a branch that produces no coloured output; a single `Xor` transition ([IO-012]) MAY relay on one branch and drain on another. *When* a coloured consumer fires on a branch with a name its coloured input holds, the name layer *shall* remove one token of that name from the input, add one token of that name to each coloured output of the branch and change no other count, so a branch with no coloured output drains the name. Because the consumed count is fixed at one, the role is identified by the input place name alone — no count, no input list. A consumer that consumes more than one coloured place, or consumes at any count other than one (`Exactly(n≥2)`, `AtLeast`, `All`), is **rejected** to the sound over-approximation: the base marking adds exactly one token per output place, so re-emitting a higher input cardinality into the name layer would over-count and could let a join fire by equating two distinct names (a false `Proven`). *While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, the fragment classifier *shall* give a transition without a match spec that consumes a coloured place no role other than the coloured-consumer role of its one coloured input, and that role only when it consumes exactly one coloured input, at count one, and puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch, into each coloured place the branch writes. The fragment classifier *shall* give the coloured-consumer role to no other transition: to none while the fragment mode is BASE, to no matched transition and to no transition that consumes no coloured place.

- **Relay/drain action precondition.** The coloured-consumer role is a modeling contract on the action, and MUST be documented as such. The action MUST thread the consumed correlation name into its coloured outputs (relay), or into **none** of them (drain); it MUST NOT mint a *fresh* name into a coloured output while consuming a coloured token. A consume-and-remint transition is **out of contract** for EXTENDED — the name layer would thread the consumed name where the runtime mints afresh, so this mode does not make such a net exact. Selecting EXTENDED is the declaration of this contract, and the report of a verdict names the consumers whose action writes it assumes. A write the executor makes on timeout is no action write: a timeout of a coloured consumer that writes a coloured place is a relay only when it forwards the consumed coloured input itself. A forward of another input copies a name the consumer did not consume, and an `Out.Place` writes a unit token with no name; either puts the net outside the fragment. *If* a transition without a match spec consumes a coloured place and its timeout writes a coloured place other than by forwarding that consumed input, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role.

- **Carrier places (fork-threaded co-mint).** Under EXTENDED, an author MAY declare intermediate **carrier** places (`carrierPlaces` / `carrier_place(s)`) that carry a fresh name from the minting fork ([NU-010]) onward to a ν-join input. The analyzer unions the declared carriers into the coloured set **before** role assignment, so the existing mint co-mints one fresh name into all of them. *While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, the fragment classifier *shall* give roles against the coloured set it uses with no carrier declared, with every declared carrier place added and no other place. In either fragment mode, a declaration whose carrier places are all places of the net is accepted. A declared carrier name absent from the net's places MUST NOT be silently ignored, in either fragment mode and whatever the query: the implementation MUST fail loudly (reject at the builder naming the offending place, or surface `Unknown` with a reason naming it), because a mistyped carrier would let two fork branches mint independent names and produce a confident, spurious deadlock verdict. A refusal that does not depend on the carrier declaration, such as a stop before the call starts ([VER-013]), an unresolved property place ([VER-003]) or a declared mint that is not a transition of the net ([NU-010]), may come first, and that refusal is then the answer. *If* a declared carrier place is not a place of the net, *then* the verifier *shall* either reject the declaration, naming such a place, or answer `Unknown` with a reason that names at least one such place and no other place, in both BASE and EXTENDED and whatever the query, unless the same request with no carrier place declared gets the same refusal. Under BASE, the fragment classifier ignores declared carriers (a documented no-op); the in-flight split of [VER-004] reads them in both modes. *While* the fragment mode is BASE, the fragment classifier *shall* give roles against the same coloured set whatever carrier places are declared.

- **Reset/read/inhibitor-on-coloured exclusion (BOTH modes).** In **both** BASE and EXTENDED, the analyzer rejects a net in which **any** coloured place carries a reset ([CORE-034]), read ([CORE-032]), or inhibitor ([CORE-031]) arc on any transition. Such an arc would be misclassified `Ordinary`, letting the base step zero or gate the coloured place while the name layer keeps the symbol, drifting the name layer from the base count marking. This is a deliberate soundness tightening applied to BASE too (rejection just falls back to the sound over-approximation); it never turns a `Proven`/`Violated` into an unsound verdict. *If* a coloured place carries a reset, read or inhibitor arc of a transition, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give that transition no role, in both BASE and EXTENDED.

- **Off-key coloured input exclusion (BOTH modes).** In **both** BASE and EXTENDED, the analyzer rejects a net in which a matched transition consumes a coloured place through an input that is **not** one of its match keys. *If* a matched transition consumes a coloured place through an input that is not one of its match keys, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role, in both BASE and EXTENDED. Such an input consumes FIFO ([NU-020]), whatever the token's name, so the name layer cannot know which name leaves the place: Route B would keep the symbol and Route A would force the join's shared colour on it. A non-coloured non-key input (a budget or permit) is unaffected. Rejection just falls back to the sound over-approximation.

- **Diagnosability.** When EXTENDED is requested but the net falls outside this fragment, the verifier MUST surface a short note (the "EXTENDED declined" note: a report line saying that the exact ν path was not taken and why, in words the implementation chooses) rather than silently falling back, so an author can tell the exact path was not taken.

builder (`fragmentMode` / `fragment_mode`). Both are decided by the solver-free

format ([VER-012]), so cross-language byte compatibility is preserved.

- **Coloured consumer (drain/relay).** Under EXTENDED, a transition with **no** match spec MAY
  consume a coloured place. The analyzer admits it only as a drain/relay role and only when it
  consumes **exactly one** coloured input at count **exactly one** ([IO-001] `One` or [IO-002]
  `Exactly(1)`). *While* the fragment mode is BASE, the fragment classifier *shall* give no role
  to a transition without a match spec that consumes a coloured place. *While* the fragment mode
  is EXTENDED, *if* a transition without a match spec consumes exactly one coloured input, at
  count one, has no reset, read or inhibitor arc on a coloured place, puts on each branch
  exactly one token, and never a drained batch, into each coloured place the branch writes, and
  on timeout writes a coloured place only by forwarding that input, *then* the fragment
  classifier *shall* give it the coloured-consumer role of that input's place, whether or not it
  is declared a mint. A coloured consumer **relays** the consumed name-symbol into each coloured
  output of the fired branch (threading the same name), or **drains** it (dead-letters the name)
  on a branch that produces no coloured output; a single `Xor` transition ([IO-012]) MAY relay
  on one branch and drain on another. *When* a coloured consumer fires on a branch with a name
  its coloured input holds, the name layer *shall* remove one token of that name from the input,
  add one token of that name to each coloured output of the branch and change no other count, so
  a branch with no coloured output drains the name. Because the consumed count is fixed at one,
  the role is identified by the input place name alone — no count, no input list. A consumer
  that consumes more than one coloured place, or consumes at any count other than one
  (`Exactly(n≥2)`, `AtLeast`, `All`), is **rejected** to the sound over-approximation: the base
  marking adds exactly one token per output place, so re-emitting a higher input cardinality
  into the name layer would over-count and could let a join fire by equating two distinct names
  (a false `Proven`). *While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, the fragment classifier *shall*
  give a transition without a match spec that consumes a coloured place no role other than the
  coloured-consumer role of its one coloured input, and that role only when it consumes exactly
  one coloured input, at count one, and puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a
  drained batch, into each coloured place the branch writes. The fragment classifier *shall*
  give the coloured-consumer role to no other transition: to none while the fragment mode is
  BASE, to no matched transition and to no transition that consumes no coloured place.

- **Relay/drain action precondition.** The coloured-consumer role is a modeling
  contract on the action, and MUST be documented as such. The action MUST thread
  the consumed correlation name into its coloured outputs (relay), or into **none**
  of them (drain); it MUST NOT mint a *fresh* name into a coloured output while
  consuming a coloured token. A consume-and-remint transition is **out of
  contract** for EXTENDED — the name layer would thread the consumed name where the
  runtime mints afresh, so this mode does not make such a net exact. Selecting
  EXTENDED is the declaration of this contract, and the report of a verdict names the
  consumers whose action writes it assumes. A write the executor makes on timeout is
  no action write: a timeout of a coloured consumer that writes a coloured place is a
  relay only when it forwards the consumed coloured input itself. A forward of another
  input copies a name the consumer did not consume, and an `Out.Place` writes a unit
  token with no name; either puts the net outside the fragment. *If* a transition without a
  match spec consumes a coloured place and its timeout writes a coloured place other than by
  forwarding that consumed input, *then* the fragment classifier *shall* give it no role.

- **Carrier places (fork-threaded co-mint).** Under EXTENDED, an author MAY declare
  intermediate **carrier** places (`carrierPlaces` / `carrier_place(s)`) that carry
  a fresh name from the minting fork ([NU-010]) onward to a ν-join input. The
  analyzer unions the declared carriers into the coloured set **before** role
  assignment, so the existing mint co-mints one fresh name into all of them.
  *While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, the fragment classifier *shall* give roles
  against the coloured set it uses with no carrier declared, with every declared
  carrier place added and no other place. In either fragment mode, a declaration
  whose carrier places are all places of the net is accepted. A
  declared carrier name absent from the net's places MUST NOT be silently ignored,
  in either fragment mode and whatever the query:
  the implementation MUST fail loudly (reject at the builder naming the offending
  place, or surface `Unknown` with a reason naming it), because a mistyped carrier would let
  two fork branches mint independent names and produce a confident, spurious
  deadlock verdict. A refusal that does not depend on the carrier declaration, such as a
  stop before the call starts ([VER-013]), an unresolved property place ([VER-003]) or a
  declared mint that is not a transition of the net ([NU-010]), may come first, and that
  refusal is then the answer. *If* a declared carrier place is not a place of the net, *then*
  the verifier *shall* either reject the declaration, naming such a place, or answer
  `Unknown` with a reason that names at least one such place and no other place, in
  both BASE and EXTENDED and whatever the query, unless the same request with no carrier
  place declared gets the same refusal. Under BASE, the fragment classifier
  ignores declared carriers (a documented no-op); the in-flight split of [VER-004]
  reads them in both modes.
  *While* the fragment mode is BASE, the fragment classifier *shall* give roles
  against the same coloured set whatever carrier places are declared.

- **Reset/read/inhibitor-on-coloured exclusion (BOTH modes).** In **both** BASE and
  EXTENDED, the analyzer rejects a net in which **any** coloured place carries a
  reset ([CORE-034]), read ([CORE-032]), or inhibitor ([CORE-031]) arc on any
  transition. Such an arc would be misclassified `Ordinary`, letting the base step
  zero or gate the coloured place while the name layer keeps the symbol, drifting
  the name layer from the base count marking. This is a deliberate soundness
  tightening applied to BASE too (rejection just falls back to the sound
  over-approximation); it never turns a `Proven`/`Violated` into an unsound verdict. *If* a
  coloured place carries a reset, read or inhibitor arc of a transition, *then* the fragment
  classifier *shall* give that transition no role, in both BASE and EXTENDED.

- **Off-key coloured input exclusion (BOTH modes).** In **both** BASE and EXTENDED,
  the analyzer rejects a net in which a matched transition consumes a coloured place
  through an input that is **not** one of its match keys. *If* a matched transition
  consumes a coloured place through an input that is not one of its match keys, *then* the
  fragment classifier *shall* give it no role, in both BASE and EXTENDED. Such an input consumes
  FIFO ([NU-020]), whatever the token's name, so the name layer cannot know which
  name leaves the place: Route B would keep the symbol and Route A would force the
  join's shared colour on it. A non-coloured non-key input (a budget or permit) is
  unaffected. Rejection just falls back to the sound over-approximation.

- **Diagnosability.** When EXTENDED is requested but the net falls outside this
  fragment, the verifier MUST surface a short note (the "EXTENDED declined" note: a
  report line saying that the exact ν path was not taken and why, in words the
  implementation chooses) rather than silently falling back, so an author can tell the exact path was not
  taken.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. (MUST) Under EXTENDED, a drain/relay fixture (a non-match transition consuming
   one coloured place at count one) classifies into the coloured-consumer role;
   under BASE the same net is rejected to the over-approximation.
2. (MUST) A coloured consumer that consumes at count `Exactly(n≥2)` (or `AtLeast` /
   `All`), or consumes more than one coloured input, is rejected under EXTENDED — no
   false `Proven` from an over-counted name layer, no dropped base-enabled firing.
3. (MUST) In both BASE and EXTENDED, a net with a reset, read, or inhibitor arc on a
   coloured place is rejected (returns no fragment).
4. (MUST) In both BASE and EXTENDED and whatever the query, a declared carrier place
   not present in the net fails loudly (builder rejection naming the place, or `Unknown`
   with a reason naming the place), unless a refusal that does not depend on the declaration
   is the answer; it is never silently ignored.
5. (SHOULD) With carriers declared, an end-to-end quiescence property (deadlock-free
   / joined-or-dead-lettered) is decided exactly via Route B — it PROVES on a
   fork-threaded co-mint plus drain fixture and reports VIOLATED when the drain is
   removed, and the verdict is attributable to Route B (the report names the
   name-partition quotient), not the name-blind SMT path.
6. (MAY) A single `Xor` coloured consumer relays the name on one branch and drains
   it on another through the same transition.
7. (MUST) In both BASE and EXTENDED, a matched transition that consumes a coloured
   place through a non-key input is rejected (returns no fragment, no coloured plan),
   and a stranding such a net can reach is not reported `Proven`.
8. (MUST) Under EXTENDED, a coloured consumer whose timeout forwards another input, or
   writes a unit token, into a coloured place is rejected on both routes. With
   `m1: budget → A1`, `m2: budget → A2` minting, `r1: A1, reqA → xor(okA, timeout(20,
   forwardInput(reqA, KA)))`, its twin `r2` into `KB` and a join on `KA`, `KB`, the
   executor reaches `done` when both requests carry one id, and `placeBound(done, 0)` is
   not `Proven`. A consumer whose timeout forwards its coloured input is still a relay.

rejects it under BASE; an `Exactly(2)` coloured consumer is rejected (blocker-1 /
blocker-2 regression); a reset-on-coloured net is rejected in both modes; an unknown

query on a fork-threaded co-mint plus drain fixture PROVES via Route B and turns
VIOLATED when the drain is removed.
