paragraphs.text: The ν properties of [NU-040] and [VER-002] count tokens. Some contracts are about which name the tokens carry. A search box that shows the results of the latest query should hold one name in the place that records the query and in the place that shows its results; a stale reply that lands after the user has typed again breaks that while every count stays in range. An implementation MAY offer two properties that read the name layer of Route B ([NU-050], [VER-012]):

- **NameAligned(S)**, for a non-empty list `S` of places: in every reachable marking, the places of `S` together hold at most one distinct name. For places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, and the name-symbols `s` and `t`: `s` resident in `p` and `t` resident in `q` imply `s = t`. An empty place imposes nothing, but a place holding two names violates it whatever the others hold, so the singleton `NameAligned(p)` says that `p` never holds two names.
- **QuiescentNameAligned(S)**: the same predicate, read only in the reachable quiescent markings. Quiescence is the reap-aware quiescence of [VER-002]: on the graph, an expanded class every firing out of which is of a reapable transition. Like `JoinedOrDeadLettered` ([NU-040]) it carries no sink clause: declared sink places ([VER-002], [VER-014]) do not weaken it.

*Where* name alignment is offered, `NameAligned(S)` for a non-empty `S` *shall* hold on a class of the graph exactly when, for places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, every name-symbol resident in `p` equals every name-symbol resident in `q`.

`NameAligned` is a reachability-safety property and `QuiescentNameAligned` a quiescence property, for every rule of [VER-012] that distinguishes the two (the early stop of AC5, the prefix rule of AC3). The predicate compares names only for equality, so it is invariant under any permutation of the name-symbols. It is therefore a function of the canonical key of a class ([VER-012] AC2), and deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph.

*When* the graph closes, Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` exactly when every class of the graph is name-aligned on `S`, and for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` exactly when every class of the graph at which the net rests is.

`S` keeps the order the caller gives. Its places compare by name, and a place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence, so `NameAligned(box, list, box)` is `NameAligned(box, list)`. An empty `S` MUST be rejected where it is constructed, as the language reports a caller's error, rather than yield a verdict. The order of `S` changes no verdict; it fixes the description and which place a reason names.

**Coloured places only.** Every place of `S` MUST be a coloured place of the fragment Route B classified for the call: match keys ([NU-020]), declared carriers ([NU-051]) and relay targets ([NU-054]). An uncoloured place carries no name in the name layer, so the predicate on it holds vacuously and a `Proven` would say nothing about the net. A place that is uncoloured, or absent from the net (the net does not declare it and the initial marking does not mark it), MUST fail loudly: the verdict is `Unknown`, never `Proven`, and where no earlier refusal of the refusal order below applies, its reason names a place of `S`: the first absent place of `S`, otherwise the first uncoloured one. A place that a mint or a coloured consumer writes is coloured only when it is one of these, which is why the worked example declares `inflightA`, `inflightB` and `list` as carriers. The coloured set is the one the classifier computes for the call (Rust `coloured_order`, the `co` of the Lean theorems), not a set the caller names.

The name a carrier or relay target holds is the name the analysis threads into it. No projection reads a carrier, so that this name is the name the token's value is about rests on the documented, unchecked contract of the coloured consumers that write it ([NU-051]): a `fetchA` whose action answered a different query than the name it relays would still prove aligned. The property is exactly as faithful to what a token carries as those contracts are.

The coloured places MUST start empty (the `hempty` premise of the Lean theorems). A call whose initial marking holds a token in a coloured place (a restored marking, [CORE-073], [NU-011]) is `Unknown`, and where no earlier refusal of the refusal order below applies, its reason names the place, the first in code-point order of place names when several are marked; since nothing else decides the property, there is no fallback.

**EXTENDED.** Under **BASE** the coloured set is the match keys alone ([NU-051], [NU-054]), so a property place that is a carrier or a relay target is uncoloured there. Such a call is refused at step 2 or at step 6 of the refusal order below unless an earlier step refuses it, and the reason of either step MUST name EXTENDED. A net outside the EXTENDED fragment gets the "EXTENDED declined" note of [NU-051] and the verdict `Unknown`. For a name-alignment property the note MUST NOT say that the property was verified by another route; it says the verdict is `Unknown`.

**Route B only.** Route A ([NU-050], [NU-053]), the name-blind SMT pipeline ([VER-001]), the linear bound ([VER-015]), the state-equation and firing-bound phases ([VER-018], [VER-019]), the bounded witness phase ([VER-025]), the bounded enumeration ([VER-017]) and the structural checks ([VER-020]) do not see names. None of them decides a name-alignment property: called directly, each returns no verdict, or `Unknown` with a reason saying that it is decided only by the name-partition graph, and the dispatcher MUST NOT defer a Route B `Unknown` to any of them (no [NU-053] fallback). The script encoders (`encodeScripts`, `encode_scripts`, `encode_smt_scripts`) return no script for these properties.

A name-alignment query goes to Route B whatever the shape of the net: it needs no matched transition, only a coloured fragment. For every other property the classifier returns no fragment for a net without a matched transition and the dispatcher sends such a net to the flat phases; an implementation MUST lift both gates for the name-alignment properties, and only for them. The dispatcher sends a name-alignment property to Route B before its other routing tests: a declared budget place, which keeps a reachability-safety property on Route A ([NU-050]), does not apply.

**Modelled injection.** Under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)` ([VER-006]) the decline rule of [NU-050] and [VER-006] AC8 applies to both properties. In addition, under these modes `QuiescentNameAligned` with a registered environment place that the net declares is `Unknown`, and where no earlier refusal of the refusal order below applies, nor an earlier rule of its step 5, the reason names the first such place in code-point order and points to `Arrivals` ([VER-006]); the vacuity reading of [VER-006] AC6 does not apply to it. Route B keeps an environment place inexhaustible and never consumes it. A net that reads input from one (say, a keystroke stream into `first` and `retire`) therefore has no resting class in the graph, and the vacuity reading would turn any graph of it that closes into `Proven`, even on a misaligned net, while the executor rests misaligned between keystrokes. On the worked example the graph does not close at all (each keystroke mints a name that can wait in `inflightB`), so the verdict would be a truncation `Unknown`; the rule makes the reason name the environment place instead. Under `Arrivals` the net has no environment places left ([VER-006]); the decline of [VER-006] AC10 for an arrival into a coloured place still applies.
**Refusal order.** A call can meet several of these refusals at once. Its verdict is `Unknown` with the reason of the first that applies, in this order, so every implementation names the same place:

1. The refusals that precede every route for every property, in this order: a call cancelled or out of total budget before it starts ([VER-013]); a place of `S` that the net does not declare and the initial marking does not mark ([VER-003] AC5), naming the first such place of `S`; a `Bounded(k)` environment outside its premises ([VER-006] AC3); the in-flight refusal of [VER-004].
2. The net is outside the fragment of the mode even when every transition counts as a mint: the fragment decline of the mode, under EXTENDED the note of **EXTENDED** above, under BASE a decline that names EXTENDED.
3. Under `Arrivals(k)` or `Arrivals(min, max)`, an arrival into a coloured place ([VER-006] AC10), naming the first such place in the order the environment places were registered.
4. The net is outside the fragment only because a transition writes a coloured place without consuming one and is not a declared mint: the decline names those transitions in declaration order ([NU-010]).
5. Under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, an environment place Route B cannot model ([VER-006] AC8). The rules run in this order, each over the environment places the net declares in code-point order of names: one that is coloured; one that an inhibitor arc tests (naming the first such transition in code-point order); where conflict priority is in effect ([NU-052]), one that two or more transitions consume; then, for `QuiescentNameAligned`, the first of them (**Modelled injection** above), and for `NameAligned`, the first that is in `S`.
6. The first place of `S`, in the order of `S`, that is not coloured. Under BASE the reason also names EXTENDED.
7. A coloured place the initial marking marks: the first in code-point order of place names.

Steps 3 and 5 apply whether or not the coloured places start empty. A declared mint or carrier that is not in the net is the caller's error and is reported as [NU-010] and [NU-051] say, outside this order. The `Ignore` downgrade of a `Proven` ([VER-006]) and a truncation `Unknown` are not refusals: they follow a graph that was built.

*If* a name-alignment call meets a refusal of step 1 of the refusal order, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` with the reason of the first refusal of step 1 that applies, in the order step 1 lists them, naming for an absent place the first place of `S` that the net does not declare and the initial marking does not mark.

*If* no refusal of step 1 applies and the net is outside the fragment of the mode even when every transition counts as a mint, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` with the fragment decline of the mode, whose reason names EXTENDED under BASE.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 and 2 applies and, under `Arrivals(k)` or `Arrivals(min, max)`, an arrival feeds a coloured place, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first such place in the order the environment places were registered.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 3 applies and transitions write a coloured place without consuming one and are not declared mints, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming those transitions in declaration order.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 4 applies and, under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, a rule of step 5 applies, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first environment place, in code-point order, that the first applicable rule finds, and for an inhibitor arc also the first transition in code-point order that tests it.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 5 applies and a place of `S` is not coloured, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first such place in the order of `S`, and under BASE the reason *shall* also name EXTENDED.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 6 applies and the initial marking marks a coloured place, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first marked coloured place in code-point order of place names.

*If* no step of the refusal order applies, *then* the verifier *shall not* refuse the call with a refusal of that order: unless the call is the caller's error of a declared mint or carrier that is not in the net, or a later poll sees a stop ([VER-013]), Route B builds the graph, and the verdict is the one it reads off that graph.

**Truncation.** A graph that does not close within the class bound never yields `Proven` (Lean `Decide.truncated_never_proven`). The prefix rule of [VER-012] AC3 applies: a `NameAligned` violated by a stored class, or a `QuiescentNameAligned` violated by an expanded class at which the net rests (every firing out of it is of a reapable transition; with nothing reapable, an expanded class with no successor, Lean `Decide.quiescentAt`), is `Violated` with the shortest witness in the explored graph and a report line naming the truncation; otherwise the verdict is `Unknown`.
*If* the graph does not close, because the build reaches the class bound, runs out of total budget or is cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* Route B *shall not* answer `Proven` for either property.
*If* the graph does not close and the prefix rule finds no violation, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Unknown`.

**Violated.** A counterexample is reported as every Route B counterexample is ([VER-003], [VER-012]): the shortest path in the name-partition graph from the initial class to a violating class, attributed to Route B, with `counterexampleConfirmed` absent (the trace is a path of the graph, not of the flat abstract semantics) and `counterexampleTiming` set by [VER-003]. The graph expands every base-enabled firing and lets a coloured consumer take any resident name, where the executor takes the oldest token ([EXEC-010]); a run of the net follows the trace when the executor's order meets the graph's choice.
*If* Route B answers `Violated` for either property, *then* the class its counterexample ends at *shall* violate the property.

**Soundness.** Lean `Novel/RouteB/Aligned.lean` (`routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound`, `routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound`) proves: for the **untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings**, a `Proven` of either property holds in every marking that executor reaches (for the quiescent form, every marking at which it rests): the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name. The premises are:

*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches.

*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking that the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches and rests at, resting being read with the reapable set of the call ([VER-002]).

The proof reads the predicate on the executor's name view (`alignedAll_view_iff`) and shows that an uncoloured place of `S` adds nothing to it (`alignedAll_uncoloured`), which is why that case is not allowed to prove. Order and repeats in `S` do not change it (`alignedAll_congr_mem`). Conflict-only priority ([NU-052]) applies as it does to every Route B property.

The proof does not cover what the shipped Route B computes on every net. Route B builds the timed name × time graph (with the latest bounds dropped as [VER-002] requires), and its agreement with a timed executor is not proved (gap R6 of `Novel/RouteB/Sound.lean`). This includes the all-immediate worked example below. The Lean model also has no in-flight state. Informally, and not proved: the predicate stays true when tokens are removed, and on a net without inhibitor, reset or drain arcs a marking with actions in flight holds a subset of the tokens of a marking that an atomic run of the graph's semantics reaches, where a coloured consumer may take any resident name. A FIFO atomic run does not always reach one: on the buggy variant below, with `fetchA` and `fetchB` both in flight, `staged` can hold the second name while `listEmpty` is still marked. So the in-flight markings are covered by the graph for `NameAligned`, not by the atomic executor.

**Worked example (search as you type).** Uncoloured places `typed` (2 tokens, two keystrokes), `idle` (1), `armedA`, `armedB`, `clr`, `ready`, `listEmpty` (1), `slot` (1); coloured places `box`, `inflightA`, `inflightB`, `reply`, `staged`, `list`, all empty at the start. Under EXTENDED, with `sendA` and `sendB` declared mints and `inflightA`, `inflightB`, `list` declared carriers:

| Transition | Firing | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `first` | `idle, typed → armedA` | ordinary |
| `retire` | `box(n), typed → armedB` | coloured consumer, drain |
| `sendA` | `armedA → box(n'), inflightA(n')` | declared mint (first query) |
| `sendB` | `armedB → box(n'), inflightB(n')` | declared mint (follow-up query) |
| `fetchA` | `inflightA(n) → reply(n)` | coloured consumer, relay (the action calls the API) |
| `fetchB` | `inflightB(n) → reply(n)` | coloured consumer, relay (the action calls the API) |
| `apply` | `match(reply, box), slot → box, staged, clr` | ν-join relaying to `box` (its own key) and `staged` |
| `clearNone` | `listEmpty, clr → ready` | ordinary, before the first result |
| `clear` | `list(m), clr → ready` | coloured consumer, drain |
| `show` | `staged(n), ready → list(n), slot` | coloured consumer, relay |

Each query has its own fetch transition, so with an API call that answers asynchronously the two requests are in flight at once on every executor, whether or not it starts a transition again while an earlier firing of it is in flight ([CONC-002]), and replies land in `reply` in the order the actions answer. A stale reply stays in `reply`: `apply` is name-disabled for it once `retire` has taken its name out of `box`. `box`, `staged`, `list`, `inflightA` and `inflightB` never hold more than one token (`slot` bounds `staged` and `list`; `idle` and the two keystrokes bound the rest), so the graph's free choice of a resident name coincides with the executor's FIFO order on them; only `reply` can hold a stale reply beside the current one. The net is closed: `typed` holds exactly two keystrokes, and the verdicts below are about that net, not about an unbounded keystroke stream (for one, see "Modelled injection" above). The net rests only after both keystrokes are consumed (`retire` stays enabled while `typed` and `box` are non-empty), so the quiescent verdicts speak about markings where all input has been typed and processed. The results:

- `QuiescentNameAligned(box, list)` is `Proven`: at rest, the list shows the results of the query in the box.
- `NameAligned(box, list)` is `Violated` with a shortest witness of 8 firings: after the second keystroke the box holds the new name while the list still shows the old results. Only the quiescent form holds.
- `QuiescentCount({list}, 1, 1)` ([VER-002]) is `Proven`: at rest, exactly one result is shown.

The buggy variant replaces `apply` with `apply_bug: reply(n), slot → staged, clr`, a coloured consumer relay with no match on `box` (`box`, `inflightA`, `inflightB`, `reply`, `staged`, `list` declared carriers, `sendA` and `sendB` declared mints). `QuiescentNameAligned(box, list)` is `Violated` with a shortest witness of 12 firings in which the reply to the first keystroke is applied last and the list ends on the old results while `box` holds the new name. Every executor takes that run when both fetch actions are in flight and `fetchA`'s action answers after `fetchB`'s: `apply_bug` takes the oldest reply, which is then the reply to the second keystroke. The reported trace is one linearisation of that run; where it lists both replies resident in `reply`, the executor realises the same firings with `fetchB` answering first. With actions that complete synchronously the replies arrive in mint order and the bug does not occur, which is why the verdict is about the net and not about one schedule.

notes.text:
the properties sit beside `JoinedOrDeadLettered` and `QuiescentCount`.

- Java: `SmtProperty.nameAligned(first, rest...)` and `SmtProperty.nameAligned(places)` for a collection, likewise `quiescentNameAligned`; records `NameAligned(List<Place<?>> places)` and `QuiescentNameAligned(List<Place<?>> places)`, whose constructors copy, deduplicate and reject an empty list. A new permitted record of the sealed `SmtProperty` breaks exhaustive switches, so it ships in a major release.
- TypeScript: `nameAligned(...places)` and `quiescentNameAligned(...places)`, typed to take at least one place, members of the `SmtProperty` union with `type: 'name-aligned'` and `type: 'quiescent-name-aligned'` and the field `places`.
- Rust: `SmtProperty::NameAligned { places: Vec<String> }` and `SmtProperty::QuiescentNameAligned { places }`, with constructors `SmtProperty::name_aligned(places)` and `SmtProperty::quiescent_name_aligned(places)` over any iterable of names, which panic on an empty one. A new variant of the exhaustive enum is a major change.
- Python: `name_aligned(places)` and `quiescent_name_aligned(places)` in `libpetri.verification`, over an iterable of places, raising `ValueError` on an empty one, through the Rust verifier, also re-exported from `libpetri`, as `joined_or_dead_lettered` and `quiescent_count` are.
- Every language describes them byte for byte on the report's `Property:` line as `Name alignment of ` and `Quiescent name alignment of ` followed by the names of the places of `S` after deduplication, in order, separated by `, ` except that ` and ` separates the last two: `Name alignment of box`, `Name alignment of box and list`, `Name alignment of a, b and c`, and `Quiescent name alignment of a, b and c` likewise.

why the worked example declares `inflightA`, `inflightB` and `list` as carriers. The coloured set is
the one the classifier computes for the call (Rust `coloured_order`, the `co` of the Lean
theorems), not a set the caller names.

The name a carrier or relay target holds is the name the analysis threads into it. No projection
reads a carrier, so that this name is the name the token's value is about rests on the documented,
unchecked contract of the coloured consumers that write it ([NU-051]): a `fetchA` whose action
answered a different query than the name it relays would still prove aligned. The property is
exactly as faithful to what a token carries as those contracts are.

The coloured places MUST start empty (the `hempty` premise of the Lean theorems). A call whose
initial marking holds a token in a coloured place (a restored marking, [CORE-073], [NU-011]) is
`Unknown`, and where no earlier refusal of the refusal order below applies, its reason names the
place, the first in code-point order of place names when several are marked; since nothing else
decides the property, there is no fallback.

**EXTENDED.** Under **BASE** the coloured set is the match keys alone ([NU-051], [NU-054]), so a
property place that is a carrier or a relay target is uncoloured there. Such a call is refused at
step 2 or at step 6 of the refusal order below unless an earlier step refuses it, and the reason of
either step MUST name EXTENDED. A net outside the EXTENDED fragment gets the "EXTENDED declined" note of [NU-051] and the
verdict `Unknown`. For a name-alignment property the note MUST NOT say that the property was
verified by another route; it says the verdict is `Unknown`.

**Route B only.** Route A ([NU-050], [NU-053]), the name-blind SMT pipeline ([VER-001]), the linear
bound ([VER-015]), the state-equation and firing-bound phases ([VER-018], [VER-019]), the bounded
witness phase ([VER-025]), the bounded enumeration ([VER-017]) and the structural checks ([VER-020]) do not see names. None of them decides a
name-alignment property: called directly, each returns no verdict, or `Unknown` with a reason
saying that it is decided only by the name-partition graph, and the dispatcher MUST NOT defer a
Route B `Unknown` to any of them (no [NU-053] fallback). The script encoders (`encodeScripts`,
`encode_scripts`, `encode_smt_scripts`) return no script for these properties.

A name-alignment query goes to Route B whatever the shape of the net: it needs no matched
transition, only a coloured fragment. For every other property the classifier returns no fragment
for a net without a matched transition and the dispatcher sends such a net to the flat phases; an
implementation MUST lift both gates for the name-alignment properties, and only for them. The
dispatcher sends a name-alignment property to Route B before its other routing tests: a declared
budget place, which keeps a reachability-safety property on Route A ([NU-050]), does not apply.

**Modelled injection.** Under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)` ([VER-006]) the decline rule of
[NU-050] and [VER-006] AC8 applies to both properties. In addition, under these modes
`QuiescentNameAligned` with a registered environment place that the net declares is `Unknown`, and
where no earlier refusal of the refusal order below applies, nor an earlier rule of its step 5, the
reason names the first such place in code-point order and points to `Arrivals` ([VER-006]); the
vacuity reading of [VER-006] AC6 does not apply to it. Route B keeps
an environment place inexhaustible and never consumes it. A net that reads input from one (say, a
keystroke stream into `first` and `retire`) therefore has no resting class in the graph, and the
vacuity reading would turn any graph of it that closes into `Proven`, even on a misaligned net,
while the executor rests misaligned between keystrokes. On the worked example the graph does not
close at all (each keystroke mints a name that can wait in `inflightB`), so the verdict would be a
truncation `Unknown`; the rule makes the reason name the environment place instead. Under `Arrivals` the
net has no environment places left ([VER-006]); the decline of [VER-006] AC10 for an arrival into
a coloured place still applies.

**Refusal order.** A call can meet several of these refusals at once. Its verdict is `Unknown` with
the reason of the first that applies, in this order, so every implementation names the same place:

1. The refusals that precede every route for every property, in this order: a call cancelled or
   out of total budget before it starts ([VER-013]); a place of `S` that the net does not declare
   and the initial marking does not mark ([VER-003] AC5), naming the first such place of `S`; a
   `Bounded(k)` environment outside its premises ([VER-006] AC3); the in-flight refusal of
   [VER-004].
2. The net is outside the fragment of the mode even when every transition counts as a mint: the
   fragment decline of the mode, under EXTENDED the note of **EXTENDED** above, under BASE a decline
   that names EXTENDED.
3. Under `Arrivals(k)` or `Arrivals(min, max)`, an arrival into a coloured place ([VER-006] AC10),
   naming the first such place in the order the environment places were registered.
4. The net is outside the fragment only because a transition writes a coloured place without
   consuming one and is not a declared mint: the decline names those transitions in declaration
   order ([NU-010]).
5. Under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, an environment place Route B cannot model ([VER-006]
   AC8). The rules run in this order, each over the environment places the net declares in
   code-point order of names: one that is coloured; one that an inhibitor arc tests (naming the
   first such transition in code-point order); where conflict priority is in effect ([NU-052]), one
   that two or more transitions consume; then, for `QuiescentNameAligned`, the first of them (**Modelled
   injection** above), and for `NameAligned`, the first that is in `S`.
6. The first place of `S`, in the order of `S`, that is not coloured. Under BASE the reason also
   names EXTENDED.
7. A coloured place the initial marking marks: the first in code-point order of place names.

Steps 3 and 5 apply whether or not the coloured places start empty. A declared mint or carrier that is not in the net is the caller's
error and is reported as [NU-010] and [NU-051] say, outside this order. The `Ignore` downgrade of a
`Proven` ([VER-006]) and a truncation `Unknown` are not refusals: they follow a graph that was
built.

*If* a name-alignment call meets a refusal of step 1 of the refusal order, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` with the reason of the first refusal of step 1 that applies, in the order step 1 lists them, naming for an absent place the first place of `S` that the net does not declare and the initial marking does not mark.

*If* no refusal of step 1 applies and the net is outside the fragment of the mode even when every transition counts as a mint, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` with the fragment decline of the mode, whose reason names EXTENDED under BASE.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 and 2 applies and, under `Arrivals(k)` or `Arrivals(min, max)`, an arrival feeds a coloured place, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first such place in the order the environment places were registered.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 3 applies and transitions write a coloured place without consuming one and are not declared mints, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming those transitions in declaration order.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 4 applies and, under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, a rule of step 5 applies, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first environment place, in code-point order, that the first applicable rule finds, and for an inhibitor arc also the first transition in code-point order that tests it.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 5 applies and a place of `S` is not coloured, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first such place in the order of `S`, and under BASE the reason *shall* also name EXTENDED.

*If* no refusal of steps 1 to 6 applies and the initial marking marks a coloured place, *then* the verifier *shall* answer `Unknown` naming the first marked coloured place in code-point order of place names.

*If* no step of the refusal order applies, *then* the verifier *shall not* refuse the call with a refusal of that order: unless the call is the caller's error of a declared mint or carrier that is not in the net, or a later poll sees a stop ([VER-013]), Route B builds the graph, and the verdict is the one it reads off that graph.

**Truncation.** A graph that does not close within the class bound never yields `Proven` (Lean
`Decide.truncated_never_proven`). The prefix rule of [VER-012] AC3 applies: a `NameAligned`
violated by a stored class, or a `QuiescentNameAligned` violated by an expanded class at which the
net rests (every firing out of it is of a reapable transition; with nothing reapable, an expanded
class with no successor, Lean `Decide.quiescentAt`), is `Violated` with the shortest witness in
the explored graph and a report line naming the truncation; otherwise the verdict is `Unknown`.

*If* the graph does not close, because the build reaches the class bound, runs out of total budget or is cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* Route B *shall not* answer `Proven` for either property.

*If* the graph does not close and the prefix rule finds no violation, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Unknown`.

**Violated.** A counterexample is reported as every Route B counterexample is ([VER-003],
[VER-012]): the shortest path in the name-partition graph from the initial class to a violating
class, attributed to Route B, with `counterexampleConfirmed` absent (the trace is a path of the
graph, not of the flat abstract semantics) and `counterexampleTiming` set by [VER-003]. The graph
expands every base-enabled firing and lets a coloured consumer take any resident name, where the
executor takes the oldest token ([EXEC-010]); a run of the net follows the trace when the executor's
order meets the graph's choice.

*If* Route B answers `Violated` for either property, *then* the class its counterexample ends at *shall* violate the property.

**Soundness.** Lean `Novel/RouteB/Aligned.lean` (`routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound`,
`routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound`) proves: for the **untimed, environment-free executor
with atomic firings**, a `Proven` of either property holds in every marking that executor reaches
(for the quiescent form, every marking at which it rests): the tokens in the places of `S` all
carry the same name. The premises are:

- the coloured places start empty;
- the mints and coloured consumers keep their contracts ([NU-010], [NU-051], [NU-054]);
- the projection contract of [NU-050]: every match-key and relay projection reads one name per
  token, the name its writer gave it, agreeing across keys and relays and never returning no name
  (Lean `Exec.ProjCoherent`, built into the model, checked by no implementation);
- every firing writes one token to each output place its branch names ([IO-016] AC4). A mint or
  relay that writes two tokens carrying different names into `box` is exactly the kind of firing
  that would falsify a `Proven` alignment;
- every place of `S` coloured, which the refusal above enforces;
- the conditions the classifier establishes (`InFragment`), unguarded inputs, and, for the
  quiescent form, join keys that consume at least one token (`PosKeys`).

*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches.

*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking that the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches and rests at, resting being read with the reapable set of the call ([VER-002]).

The proof reads the predicate on the executor's name view (`alignedAll_view_iff`) and shows that an
uncoloured place of `S` adds nothing to it (`alignedAll_uncoloured`), which is why that case is not
allowed to prove. Order and repeats in `S` do not change it (`alignedAll_congr_mem`).
Conflict-only priority ([NU-052]) applies as it does to every Route B property.

The proof does not cover what the shipped Route B computes on every net. Route B builds the timed
name × time graph (with the latest bounds dropped as [VER-002] requires), and its agreement with a
timed executor is not proved (gap R6 of `Novel/RouteB/Sound.lean`). This includes the all-immediate
worked example below. The Lean model also has no in-flight state. Informally, and not proved: the
predicate stays true when tokens are removed, and on a net without inhibitor, reset or drain arcs
a marking with actions in flight holds a subset of the tokens of a marking that an atomic run of
the graph's semantics reaches, where a coloured consumer may take any resident name. A FIFO atomic
run does not always reach one: on the buggy variant below, with `fetchA` and `fetchB` both in
flight, `staged` can hold the second name while `listEmpty` is still marked. So the in-flight
markings are covered by the graph for `NameAligned`, not by the atomic executor.

**Worked example (search as you type).** Uncoloured places `typed` (2 tokens, two keystrokes),
`idle` (1), `armedA`, `armedB`, `clr`, `ready`, `listEmpty` (1), `slot` (1); coloured places `box`,
`inflightA`, `inflightB`, `reply`, `staged`, `list`, all empty at the start. Under EXTENDED, with
`sendA` and `sendB` declared mints and `inflightA`, `inflightB`, `list` declared carriers:

| Transition | Firing | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `first` | `idle, typed → armedA` | ordinary |
| `retire` | `box(n), typed → armedB` | coloured consumer, drain |
| `sendA` | `armedA → box(n'), inflightA(n')` | declared mint (first query) |
| `sendB` | `armedB → box(n'), inflightB(n')` | declared mint (follow-up query) |
| `fetchA` | `inflightA(n) → reply(n)` | coloured consumer, relay (the action calls the API) |
| `fetchB` | `inflightB(n) → reply(n)` | coloured consumer, relay (the action calls the API) |
| `apply` | `match(reply, box), slot → box, staged, clr` | ν-join relaying to `box` (its own key) and `staged` |
| `clearNone` | `listEmpty, clr → ready` | ordinary, before the first result |
| `clear` | `list(m), clr → ready` | coloured consumer, drain |
| `show` | `staged(n), ready → list(n), slot` | coloured consumer, relay |

Each query has its own fetch transition, so with an API call that answers asynchronously the two
requests are in flight at once on every executor, whether or not it starts a transition again while
an earlier firing of it is in flight ([CONC-002]), and replies land in `reply` in the order the
actions answer. A stale reply stays in `reply`: `apply` is name-disabled for it once `retire` has
taken its name out of `box`. `box`, `staged`, `list`, `inflightA` and `inflightB` never hold more
than one token (`slot` bounds `staged` and `list`; `idle` and the two keystrokes bound the rest),
so the graph's free choice of a resident name coincides with the executor's FIFO order on them;
only `reply` can hold a stale reply beside the current one. The net is closed: `typed` holds exactly two keystrokes, and the verdicts below are about that net, not
about an unbounded keystroke stream (for one, see "Modelled injection" above). The net rests only
after both keystrokes are consumed (`retire` stays enabled while `typed` and `box` are non-empty),
so the quiescent verdicts speak about markings where all input has been typed and processed. The
results:

- `QuiescentNameAligned(box, list)` is `Proven`: at rest, the list shows the results of the query in
  the box.
- `NameAligned(box, list)` is `Violated` with a shortest witness of 8 firings: after the second
  keystroke the box holds the new name while the list still shows the old results. Only the
  quiescent form holds.
- `QuiescentCount({list}, 1, 1)` ([VER-002]) is `Proven`: at rest, exactly one result is shown.

The buggy variant replaces `apply` with `apply_bug: reply(n), slot → staged, clr`, a coloured
consumer relay with no match on `box` (`box`, `inflightA`, `inflightB`, `reply`, `staged`,
`list` declared carriers, `sendA` and `sendB` declared mints). `QuiescentNameAligned(box, list)`
is `Violated` with a shortest witness of 12 firings in which the reply to the first keystroke is
applied last and the list ends on the old results while `box` holds the new name. Every executor
takes that run when both fetch actions are in flight and `fetchA`'s action answers after
`fetchB`'s: `apply_bug` takes the oldest reply, which is then the reply to the second keystroke. The reported trace is one linearisation of that
run; where it lists both replies resident in `reply`, the executor realises the same firings with
`fetchB` answering first. With actions that complete synchronously the replies arrive in mint order
and the bug does not occur, which is why the verdict is about the net and not about one schedule.

glossary.text: A named container that holds tokens [CORE-001]. Two places are the same place exactly when they have the same identity [CORE-002].

The number of tokens a place holds in a marking, written `m(p)`. Enablement and firing read token counts only: no input arc tests a token's value [IO-006]. The exception is a correlated input of a ν-net match specification, where they count the tokens of one name [NU-020].
The distribution of tokens across all places at one instant [CORE-070]. A place no arc touches keeps its tokens and is inert [CORE-072].
A place is marked when its token count is not zero.

An arc from a place to a transition that the transition consumes from when it fires, according to the arc's cardinality `One`, `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` [CORE-030], [IO-001]–[IO-004]. A transition declares at most one input arc per place [CORE-030].
`requiredCount()`: the fewest tokens an input place must hold for the transition to be enabled. It is 1 for `One` and `All`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `m` for `AtLeast(m)` [IO-007].

`consumptionCount(available)`: the tokens a firing removes from an input place that holds `available` tokens. It is 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `available` for `All` and `AtLeast(m)` [IO-007]. On a correlated input of a ν-net match specification, `available` is the number of tokens of the chosen name [NU-020].
An arc from a transition to a place: a place that the transition's output spec names [CORE-035], [IO-017].
An arc from a place to a transition that disables the transition while the place is marked [CORE-031]. It never consumes.

An arc from a place to a transition that requires the place to be marked for the transition to be enabled [CORE-032]. It never consumes. A transition has no read arc on a place it has an input arc on [EXEC-012].
An arc from a place to a transition that removes every token from the place when the transition fires [CORE-034]. It never affects enablement.

A transition is enabled in a marking when every input place holds at least its required count, every read place is marked and no inhibitor place is marked [CORE-022], [IO-005]. Reset arcs and output arcs play no part. For a transition with a ν-net match specification this is the count-level part of enablement only: its enablement check also needs a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens [NU-020].

To fire is to perform one firing. One firing of an enabled transition consumes from its input places, empties its reset places and deposits the tokens of one outcome [CORE-030], [CORE-034], [CORE-035]. Read as one step from a marking `m` to a marking `m'`, a firing ignores timing and priority.

To remove tokens from an input place when the transition fires: as many as the consumption count, oldest first [CORE-030], [IO-007]. On a correlated input of a ν-net match specification the count and the order apply to the tokens of the chosen name only [EXEC-010], [NU-020]. Read arcs and inhibitor arcs never consume [CORE-031], [CORE-032].

The tokens a firing adds to the marking, counted per place: how many tokens each place receives. It may be written as a list of places with repetition, a place receiving one token per occurrence, but only the count per place is normative: two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit, whatever their order [CORE-036]. A reset place ends a firing holding exactly what the firing deposited there [CORE-034].
The tree of `Place`, `And`, `Xor`, `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` nodes that says where a transition's action may write [IO-010]–[IO-014]. A transition with no output spec deposits nothing.

One way the action can satisfy the output spec: a set of places, taking one child at every `Xor` and the union at every `And` [IO-015], [IO-016]. With output validation enabled [CONC-026], a firing that ends with its action deposits one or more tokens in each place of one output branch and none in any other place: the branch fixes which places receive tokens, not how many [IO-015], [CORE-036]. The output branches of a spec that builds are pairwise distinct sets [IO-012]. The analyses that enumerate them model one token per place [IO-016].
The places that received at least one token from a firing [IO-015].

The way a firing ends when the executor's own budget timer on the `Timeout` node fires before the action completes [IO-013]. An output spec holds at most one `Timeout` node, so a transition has at most one timeout outcome [IO-013]. The `Timeout` child holds no `Xor` node, so that outcome deposits in one fixed set of places [IO-013]. The marking then receives the `Timeout` child's tokens and nothing else: one minted token in each place the child names through `Place`, and for each `ForwardInput(from, to)` the tokens the firing consumed from `from`, each keeping its value and `created_at` [IO-014]. It is compared with other deposits per place [CORE-036], [IO-012]. An exception the action raises is not a timeout outcome.

`ForwardInput(from, to)`, allowed only inside the child of a `Timeout` node: on the timeout outcome, one token in `to` for each token the firing consumed from `from`, in consumption order, each keeping the consumed token's value and `created_at` [IO-014]. In an output branch it claims `to` [IO-015].

Two lists of places name the same set of places when every place of each is a place of the other, whatever the order or repetition. Places are the same under the implementation's own `Place` equality [CORE-002], [MOD-024]. Output branches are compared this way [IO-012], [IO-015].

The checks building a transition runs: the input-arc check of [CORE-030], the input-count checks of [IO-002] and [IO-004], the input-and-read check of [EXEC-012], the timing check of [TIME-001], then, on its output spec and in this order, a place named twice in one output branch [IO-011], more than one `Timeout` node [IO-013], an `Xor` node inside the child of the `Timeout` node [IO-013], a `ForwardInput` outside the child of a `Timeout` node [IO-014], a `ForwardInput` whose `from` is not an input place [IO-014], and two output branches that claim the same set of places [IO-012], then, for a transition with a match specification, a place the match keys twice and a key on a place that is not an input place [NU-020], and per relay target one declared twice and one that is not an output place [NU-054]. The first check that fails names the error. No executor option skips them [CONC-026].
A transition builds when it passes every build-time check. A definition that fails one is not a transition of any net: no executor holds it, so it is never enabled and never fires [CORE-022].

The interval `[earliest, latest]` a transition's timing specification gives: `Immediate`, `Deadline(by)`, `Delayed(after)`, `Window(earliest, latest)` or `Exact(at)` [TIME-001]–[TIME-006]. `Immediate` and `Delayed` have no finite latest bound; their `latest()` is the maximum duration.

The finite stand-in for "no latest bound", about 100 years: `MAX_DURATION_MS` = 3153600000000 ms, or `MAX_DURATION` in Java [TIME-001]. No valid timing has an earliest bound above it, no valid `Deadline` has a `by` above it, and no valid `Window` has a latest bound above it [TIME-001].
The monotonic time source from which the executor stamps armed transitions and computes elapsed time [TIME-010], [TIME-015]. Its readings never decrease and may repeat [TIME-015].
A place on which a transition has an input, read, inhibitor or reset arc [CORE-030]–[CORE-034]. A place the transition only deposits into is not one of its arc places.

A firing writes a place when it consumes from it, deposits into it or drains it through a reset arc. Draining a reset place that is already empty counts as a write. An injected token writes the place it lands in [ENV-003]. Reading through a read arc and testing through an inhibitor arc never write [TIME-013].

A transition is armed when it is enabled and holds a clock: a stamp, the firing-clock reading taken by the enablement update that most recently newly armed it [TIME-010]. A transition is newly armed when it is enabled in the initial marking, when it is enabled after a firing or an injected token that wrote one of its arc places while it was not armed, and when its clock restarts [TIME-012]. A transition that is not enabled is not armed. Armed is not Enabled: a reaped transition is enabled but not armed [TIME-013].
The current reading of the firing clock minus an armed transition's stamp [TIME-010]. Only an armed transition has one.
A transition is ready when it is armed, its elapsed time is at least its earliest bound and it is not expired [TIME-010], [EXEC-002].
The per-executor grace band added to a latest bound before a transition is reaped: 5 ms by default, and `0` for strict enforcement [TIME-013].

A transition is reapable when its timing is `Deadline` or `Window` [TIME-013]. `Exact`, `Immediate` and `Delayed` are not reapable, though `Exact` has a deadline in the sense of `hasDeadline()` [TIME-001], [TIME-006].
A reapable transition is expired when it is armed and its elapsed time is strictly greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance [TIME-013].

To reap an expired transition is to disarm it in the deadline step of a cycle without firing it, emitting `TransitionTimedOut` [TIME-013], [EXEC-001], [EVT-009]. A reaped transition keeps its tokens and stays enabled but not armed, and does not fire, until a firing or an injected token writes one of its arc places; it is then newly armed if it is enabled [TIME-013].

The tokens of a place are kept in the order they were added. The oldest token is the head of the place; a firing consumes from the head, except on a correlated input of a ν-net match [EXEC-010], [NU-020], and reads the head [EXEC-012], and a deposit adds at the tail [EXEC-020].
A place the net does not declare: no transition of the net has an arc on it or names it in its output spec. Its tokens are retained in the marking, inert, since no arc can reference them [CORE-072].

What a transition runs when it fires: it receives a transition context holding the tokens the firing consumed and the tokens its read arcs read, and it either completes with output tokens, written through the context or returned, or fails [CORE-050], [EXEC-030]. A firing that ends with the completion of its action deposits exactly those tokens [CORE-050], [EXEC-020]; a firing that ends with its timeout outcome deposits none of them [IO-013], except tokens the action already published with ctx.flush() (Rust, Python; [IO-015]). The built-in passthrough action completes with no token and is recognised by identity [CORE-051].

A completion is an action that returned normally [EXEC-020]. The executor admits it when it processes it, in step 1 of a cycle or, for a synchronous action, inside the firing pass [EXEC-001]. It never admits the completion of a firing that ended with its timeout outcome [EXEC-022], that a stop on a terminal place abandoned [EXEC-042] or that an immediate termination abandoned [ENV-015]. Only an admitted completion deposits, and only when output validation, if enabled [CONC-026], does not reject its produced set [EXEC-020], [EXEC-021].

A place a host injects tokens into from outside the executor: a marker wrapper around a regular place, whose name and token type stay accessible [ENV-001]. The environment places of a run are registered with the executor when it is built, and no step of the run adds or removes one [ENV-002]. An executor whose inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript) answers an injection into any other place with an error; one whose inject takes a place name (Rust, Python) deposits into the place the name resolves to, and its host injects only into environment places [ENV-002]. A run with environment places waits at quiescence for injections instead of finishing [ENV-010]. A place may be an environment place and a port at once; its registration then applies to the place after composition [ENV-001].

A step of the verifier's flat step relation that adds one token to an injected environment place that resolves in the flat net: the injection rule of the HORN encoding [VER-006], the `inject(<place>)` step of the counterexample replay [VER-003] and of the bounded witness phase [VER-025]. Under `Bounded(k)` it is enabled only while the place holds fewer than `k` tokens, under `AlwaysAvailable` always. Under `Ignore` and `Arrivals` the flat net has none [VER-006].

A run to a violating marking from which no single step can be dropped so that the rest still replays to a violating marking [VER-025]. An irredundant run need not be a shortest one. The bounded witness phase reports one that also ends at the first violating marking it reaches.
The bitmap of a marking with one bit per place, set exactly when the place is marked [CONC-004].
A machine word of a bitmap: it holds the bits of a run of consecutive place indices. A bitmap is a sequence of words, and a word past the end of a bitmap reads as zero [CONC-004], [PERF-042].
The bitmap of a transition with a bit set for each of its input places and read places: all of them must be marked [CONC-004].
The bitmap of a transition with a bit set for each of its inhibitor places: none of them may be marked [CONC-004].

Phase 1 of the enablement check. It passes on a bitmap when every bit of the transition's needs-mask is set and no bit of its inhibitor-mask is set: `(marking & needs-mask) == needs-mask AND (marking & inhibitor-mask) == 0` [CONC-004], [CONC-008]. Reset arcs and output arcs play no part.
Phase 2 of the enablement check. It passes when every input place holds at least its required count [CONC-008], [IO-007].

The check an executor runs to decide whether a transition is enabled: the presence check on the presence bitmap of the marking, then the cardinality check, then, for a transition with a match specification, the ν-match check [CONC-008], [NU-020].
An opaque correlation identity, constructed from a string value [NU-001]. A token carries no name field: a key projection reads a name off the token's value [NU-020].

What a transition may declare to join by name: a list of its input places, each with a key projection, and optionally relay targets, each an output place with a key projection [NU-020], [NU-054]. A transition with one is a matched transition.
An input place that the match specification of its transition names. Its required count and consumption count apply to the tokens of the chosen name [NU-020].

The function a match specification gives a correlated input: from a token's value to a name, or to no name. A token whose key yields no name has no name on that input: it is never matched and never consumed by that input [NU-020].

The name a firing of a matched transition joins on: among the names of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens, the one whose earliest `createdAt` among all tokens of the name in the correlated inputs is earliest, ties broken by the name order [NU-020], [NU-022].

The tokens a firing takes from a correlated input: the first tokens of the chosen name in queue order, as many as the consumption count of the input arc with `available` the number of tokens of the chosen name [IO-007], [NU-020]. Tokens of other names stay in the place, in their order.
An output place a match specification declares for its transition, with a key projection: every token the firing deposits there must project to the chosen name [NU-054].

A place whose tokens carry a correlation name in the name layer of Route B: a match key of a matched transition [NU-020] and, under EXTENDED, also a declared carrier place [NU-051] and a relay target [NU-054]. Under BASE the coloured set is the match keys alone [NU-055]. The classifier computes the coloured set for each call.

The function a ν verifier applies to each transition of a net, in the fragment mode BASE or EXTENDED, to give it a role in the fragment Route B decides exactly (a mint, a matched join, a coloured consumer or an ordinary transition), or no role, in which case the net falls back to the sound over-approximation [NU-050], [NU-051].

Under conflict-only priority, a transition H pre-empts a transition L in a class when H is enabled, is not L, has strictly higher priority, is ready no later than L, has no firing in flight, fires in the class and competes with L for a consumed input. L is then not expanded from the class [NU-052].
A list S of places is name-aligned in a marking when the places of S together hold at most one distinct name: any two names resident in places of S, in the same place or in two, are equal [NU-055].
The answer a verifier gives for a property: `Proven`, `Violated` or `Unknown` [VER-003].

A net fragment that is never run on its own: a body net (its places and transitions) and an interface of ports, each exposing one body place with a direction, and channels, each exposing one body transition [MOD-001], [MOD-003], [MOD-005]. Instantiating it under a prefix gives a module instance [MOD-010].

The string a subnet definition is instantiated under. A prefix is non-empty and contains no `/`, the reserved separator [MOD-010]. Under prefix `p` a place or transition named `x` is renamed `p/x` [MOD-010]; nesting gives names of the form `outer/inner/x` [MOD-013].

What instantiating a subnet definition under a prefix gives: the prefix, a renamed copy of the body, in which every place and transition is renamed under the prefix, every arc names the renamed places and every timing, priority and action is kept, and handles that resolve the definition's port and channel names to the renamed places and transitions [MOD-010], [MOD-011]. Two instances of one definition under different prefixes share no place and no transition name [MOD-010].

divergences.java: actions invoked inline; concurrency comes from the returned stage
structural on name and token type; restore takes the net's places

divergences.rust: deposited into the named place; registration is the host's
`ExecutorClock`; Python offers only the Rust-side `ManualClock` and `SteppedClock`
`ctx.flush()`; flushed tokens survive a later validation failure

defects.title: The timeout outcome is validated against the output spec
defects.text: both validate the timeout outcome against the whole output spec, so a spec such as `And(A, Timeout(d, B))` fails the firing on every timeout instead of depositing `B`. Rust skips validation on the timeout path and still runs the join-relay check. `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java` (`processCompletedTransitions`), `typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts` (`validateOutSpec` in `processCompletedTransitions`, on the completion path that also settles a timed-out firing). The production executors have the same check: `PrecompiledNetExecutor.processCompletedTransitions` in Java and the general branch of `typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts`.
defects.fix: both executors of each runtime skip the output-spec validation and the IO-016 multiplicity warning for a firing that ended with the timeout outcome and run only the join-relay check (NU-054), so `And(A, Timeout(d, B))` deposits `B`. Java `AbstractNetExecutorEngineTest.OutputTimeoutTests.outTimeout_andSibling_depositsTheTimeoutChildUnvalidated_EXEC021` and `outTimeout_andSibling_forwardsEveryTokenWithoutMultiplicityWarning_EXEC021`; TypeScript `executor-shared-semantics.test.ts`, "the timeout outcome is not validated (EXEC-021, EXEC-022, IO-013)", on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: `clashExec_timeoutValidated_conflict` (ClashesExec.lean), `EXEC_021_forbids_validateTimeout` (EXEC_021.lean), `IO_013_forbids_validateTimeout` (IO_013.lean).

defects.title: The TypeScript builder hands its live sets to the built net
defects.text: `build()` passes the builder's own place and transition sets to the net, so a later builder call changes a net that was already built. `PetriNetBuilder.build` (`typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts`). A channel `compose` after `build()` even deletes the caller transition from the built net. Only the build without fusion shares the sets.
defects.fix: `build()` hands the net copies of the builder's place and transition sets. TypeScript `petri-net.test.ts`, "a built net keeps its places and transitions when the builder is used again (CORE-041)" and "a channel compose after build leaves the built net intact (CORE-041)".
defects.evidenceText: `CORE_041_forbids_alias` (CORE_041.lean), `aliasBuilder_unstable` (Reference/Build.lean).

defects.title: TypeScript identifies places by object reference
defects.text: `place(name)` returns a new object on each call and the built net keeps places by reference, while the compiled net keys them by name, so one place can be held twice. `place` (`typescript/src/core/place.ts`), the `_places` field of `PetriNetBuilder` and its `transition` method (`typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts`). The output spec's place sets do the same: `allPlaces` and `enumerateBranches` (`typescript/src/core/out.ts`) collect into a JS `Set` of place objects, so `Xor(And(A, B), And(A', C))` with `A` and `A'` two `place('A')` objects (it builds: the IO-011 and IO-012 checks compare names) has an `allPlaces` set of four members for three places, and the unbuildable `And(A, A')` enumerates one branch of two members for one place. The fusion build and the `Transition` input, read and output place sets compare places by object as well, so `fork` or `transform` on `Xor(And(A, B), And(A', C))` writes `A` twice.
defects.fix: places are kept by name, and the first object seen for a name wins, in the builder, the fusion build, the transition place sets, `allPlaces` and `enumerateBranches`. TypeScript `petri-net.test.ts`, "holds one place for two place objects with one name (CORE-002, CORE-040)" and its fusion variant; `transition.test.ts`, "collects input, read and output places by name (CORE-002)"; `out.test.ts`, "collects one place per name (CORE-002, IO-017)" and "a branch holds one place per name (CORE-002, IO-016)".
defects.evidenceText: none beyond the CORE_040, CORE_002, IO_016 and IO_017 assumes; under name identity the TypeScript net breaks CORE_040 line 3, and the TypeScript `allPlaces` breaks the union of IO_017's `Xor` line.

defects.title: A TypeScript event shares the executor's consumed array
defects.text: the `TransitionStarted` event carries the executor's own `consumed` array, which the executor also hands on, so the event is not a copy. `typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts` (`fireTransition`), `TransitionStarted` (`typescript/src/event/net-event.ts`). The precompiled executor (`typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts`) does the same.
defects.fix: both executors put a copy of the consumed tokens into the `TransitionStarted` event, made only when an event store is enabled. TypeScript `executor-shared-semantics.test.ts`, "carries a copy of the consumed tokens (EVT-001 AC2)", on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: none. EVT-001 has no block: a Lean event is a value, so a shared array cannot be stated (`netEvent_value`, GlossaryEvents.lean, cites EVT-001).

defects.title: A TypeScript resolver that returns `undefined` binds `undefined`
defects.text: `bindActionsWithResolver` treats only `null` as no action, so a plain JavaScript resolver such as `name => obj[name]` rebinds an unknown transition to `undefined`. `PetriNet.bindActionsWithResolver` (`typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts`). `SubnetDef.bindActionsWithResolver` (`typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts`) makes the same test.
defects.fix: both resolver forms treat `undefined` as `null`, and their return type is widened to `TransitionAction | null | undefined`. TypeScript `petri-net.test.ts`, "bindActionsWithResolver defers a transition when the resolver returns undefined (CORE-042)"; `subnet-verify-options.test.ts`, "the resolver form defers a transition on undefined, as on null (CORE-042)".
defects.evidenceText: none; the CORE_042 assumes cite it (the block reads a resolver's `null`/`None` as `none`, line 3, and the model has no `undefined`).

defects.title: Java and TypeScript accept `action(null)`
defects.text: the builder setter stores `null` (or `undefined`) as the action. The identity check of CORE-043 passes such a transition, and every firing of it then fails. Python raises `TypeError`; Rust cannot express it. `Transition.Builder.action` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java`), `TransitionBuilder.action` (`typescript/src/core/transition.ts`).
defects.fix: the builder setter rejects a missing action: Java throws `NullPointerException` on `action(null)` and TypeScript a `TypeError` on `null` or `undefined`; leaving the call out still gives the passthrough default. Java `TransitionTest.core051_builder_rejectsNullAction`; TypeScript `transition.test.ts`, "rejects a null or undefined action (CORE-051)".
defects.evidenceText: none; the CORE_051 assumes record it.

defects.title: A Python transition is not equal to itself when read back
defects.text: the `Transition` wrapper defines no `__eq__` or `__hash__`, and `PetriNet.transitions` returns a fresh wrapper on every access, so `net.transitions[0] == net.transitions[0]` is `False`. The fix is `__eq__` and `__hash__` on the wrapped `TransitionId`. `PyTransition` and the `transitions` getter of `PyPetriNet` (`rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs`).
defects.fix: the wrapper defines `__eq__` and `__hash__` over the wrapped transition's `TransitionId`. Python `test_smoke.py::test_core_021_ac2_transition_read_back_equals_itself`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the CORE_021 assumes record it.

defects.title: The CORE-043 check runs on the derived split net under CONFLICT
defects.text: under `PrioritySemantics` CONFLICT the verifier splits a sink into a start half, which keeps the sink's name and action and gains an output place, and then runs the CORE-043 check on that derived net. A net that compiles is refused, and the Rust error says the sink declares an output spec when it declares none. Rust: `with_in_flight` (`rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs`), `halves` (`in_flight.rs`), `verify_name_scg` (`nu_scg_verifier.rs`), `StateClassGraph::build_core` (`state_class_graph.rs`). Java: the state-space lookup in `SmtVerifier.pipeline` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java`), `StateClassGraph.initialStateClass` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/StateClassGraph.java`). TypeScript: `SmtVerifier.verify` (`typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`, after `prepare()`). Rust's SMT entry already checks the submitted net; its refusals come from the graph builders it calls on the split net, which are CORE-043 entry points with checks of their own, so a check run once before any rewrite does not end the defect on its own. Java also checks a field that a previous call left rewritten, so a reused verifier can fail its second call (RD-47).
defects.fix: the start half of a split passthrough sink gets a placeholder action instead of the passthrough in all three runtimes, so the split net passes CORE-043 exactly when the submitted net does; Java and TypeScript also run the entry check on the caller's net before `prepare()`. The public graph builders keep their own checks. Rust `smt_verifier.rs` `core043_conflict_split_of_a_passthrough_sink_is_not_refused`; Java `SplitDemandTest.CORE043_aConflictSplitOfAPassthroughSinkIsNotRefused`; TypeScript `smt-verifier-core043.test.ts`, "a conflict split of a passthrough sink is not refused (CORE-043)"; Python `test_smoke.py::test_core_043_conflict_split_of_a_passthrough_sink_is_not_refused`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the CORE_043 assumes record it.

defects.title: Java's `input` with several tokens contradicts its own javadoc
defects.text: with more than one token delivered from a place, `input` returns the oldest token's value, while its javadoc says it fails. Rust, TypeScript and Python report an error. `TransitionContext.input` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java`) against its own javadoc. Java's `fork()` and `transform(Place, fn)` rely on `input` returning the oldest token (the documented CORE-052 divergence), so the javadoc is what is wrong.
defects.fix: the javadoc says that `input` returns the oldest value and points to `inputs(Place)` for the whole batch; the behaviour is unchanged. Java `TransitionContextTest.core060_input_withSeveralTokens_returnsOldestValue` pins it.
defects.evidenceText: `CORE_060_batch_undecided` shows the block leaves the case open; the defect is Java against its own documentation.

defects.title: A caller transition bound to two channels is not rejected
defects.text: no runtime rejects one caller transition bound to two channels of one instance. Rust stages the merges in a map keyed by the caller's name, so only the merge its hash order visits last survives; Java and TypeScript add both merges under one name (`apply_composition` in `rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs`, `applyComposition` in `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java` and `typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts`).
defects.fix: each runtime's channel binding rejects a caller transition, compared by identity, that is already bound to another channel of the call, with `Transition '<t>' is already bound to channel '<c1>'; it cannot also be bound to channel '<c2>' (MOD-020)`; Python raises it as `ValueError`. Rust `compose.rs` `bind_channel_rejects_one_caller_transition_on_two_channels_mod020` and `compose_one_caller_transition_on_two_channels_names_both_mod020`; Java `ChannelCompositionTest.compose_oneCallerTransitionOnTwoChannels_isRejected_MOD020_AC6`; TypeScript `channel-composition.test.ts`, "compose_oneCallerTransitionOnTwoChannels_isRejected (MOD-020 AC6)"; Python `test_channel_composition.py::test_one_caller_transition_bound_to_two_channels_is_rejected`.
defects.evidenceText: none; MOD-020 makes distinct caller-side names a caller obligation (`mod020_fresh`, MOD_020.lean) and states nothing about such a call.

defects.title: An empty `/` segment in a cluster key fails the export
defects.text: on a key such as `a//x` or `http://host/x`, `register_prefix_chain` skips the empty segment and never registers the key itself; the builder then fails at the node's key. `rust/libpetri-export/src/cluster_builder.rs` (`register_prefix_chain`). Python's `dot_export` and archive writer reach that exporter and raise `PanicException`. Java fails on fewer keys: `String.split` keeps inner empty segments, so the keys `a//x` and `http://host` draw, and only a key with a leading or trailing `/`, such as `/a` (the key of `/a/x`) or `a/` (the key of `a//x`), throws a `NullPointerException` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/export/ClusterBuilder.java`, `registerPrefixChain`). TypeScript throws a `TypeError` on a key with a leading `/` and on the empty key (`typescript/src/export/cluster-builder.ts`).
defects.fix: the three exporters register the glossary key chain (every non-empty prefix that ends before a `/`, then the key itself, the empty key included) and take the deepest common prefix as the longest element of one chain that is in the other; keys without an empty segment draw as before. Rust `cluster_builder.rs` `exp_016_key_with_empty_segment_registers_its_key_chain` and `dot_exporter.rs` `exp_016_empty_segment_names_export_without_panic`; Java `ClusterBuilderTest.partitionRegistersTheKeyChainOfAKeyWithAnEmptySegment_EXP016` and `SubnetDotExportTest.dotExport_emptySegmentNames_doNotThrow_EXP016`; TypeScript `cluster-builder.test.ts`, "EXP-016: a key with an empty /-segment (a/, a//x, /a) draws its key chain and does not throw"; Python `test_dot_export.py::test_exp_016_empty_segment_cluster_key_exports_without_panic` and `::test_exp_016_empty_segment_cluster_key_archives_without_panic`.
defects.evidenceText: `registerChain` (Reference/ExportCluster.lean); EXP-016's name assumption (`ExportNet.ClusterKeysWellFormed`) keeps such nets out of the block.

defects.title: A flush can publish after the action completed
defects.text: the flush closure has no completed or abandoned check and can outlive the action: a Rust action that moved `ctx.flush_fn()` into a spawned task, or a Python context held past the action, can still send a batch after the action completed, by a normal return, an error return or the expiry of its budget (on a timeout the executor drops the action future). Phase 1b then deposits that batch, although the action had completed before it flushed it. The fix is an abandoned flag on the closure, set in the timeout arm and at completion. `rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs` (the `set_flush_fn` closure in `fire_transition_async`), `rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs` (`flush_fn`), `rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs` (`PyActionContext::from_transition_context`).
defects.fix: the flush closure and its spawned task share a gate under one lock: the task marks the firing ended once the action completes, fails or times out, before it sends the completion, and a later flush returns an error naming EXEC-022 and deposits nothing (Python raises `RuntimeError`). Rust `backend_suite_tests.rs` `late_flush::exec_022_a_flush_after_the_firing_ended_is_refused` and `late_flush::exec_022_a_flush_before_the_timeout_is_deposited`; Python `test_ctx_flush.py::test_a_flush_after_the_timeout_is_refused_exec_022` and `::test_a_flush_after_the_action_returned_is_refused_exec_022`.
defects.evidenceText: `EXEC_022_forbids_lateFlush` (EXEC_022.lean); `CONC_003_forbids_flushAfterError` (CONC_003.lean), the case after an error return.

defects.title: Java's firing pass and decision to wait judge at readings of their own
defects.text: a Java cycle takes four readings of the firing clock: the enablement update, the deadline step, the firing pass and the decision to wait each read the clock (`clockNanos()`). The pass judges readiness at its own reading instead of the deadline step's, and the decision to wait judges the next timing boundary at a fourth reading (`nanosUntilNextTimedTransition`, called from `awaitCompletionOrEvent`, its poll loop and `awaitExternalEvent`). Rust takes one reading per cycle and conforms. TypeScript's deadline step and pass share one reading, which conforms, but its decision to wait takes another (RD-32). The pass checks only the earliest bound at its reading and never checks expiry again, so a `Deadline` or `Window` transition whose elapsed time passes its latest bound plus the tolerance between the deadline step's reading and the pass's is neither reaped nor refused: it fires. Example: `Deadline(100)`, tolerance 5, armed at 0; the deadline step reads 105.9 ms (elapsed 105, not past 105, so no reap), the pass reads 106.0 ms (elapsed 106) and fires it. The reading at the decision to wait is later than the deadline step's, so it only shortens the wait, which CONC-010 accepts; it is still a new reading that TIME-010 rules out. `updateDirtyTransitions`, `enforceDeadlines`, `fireReadyGeneral` and `nanosUntilNextTimedTransition` (used in `awaitCompletionOrEvent`, its poll loop `awaitCompletionPolling` and `awaitExternalEvent`), in `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java` and `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`.
defects.fix: Java takes one firing-clock reading per cycle, before the enablement update, and hands it to the deadline step, the firing pass and the decision to wait in both executors; the poll loop only counts the timer down. TypeScript's decision to wait takes the cycle reading through the RD-32 change. Java `AbstractInjectableClockTest`: `firingPassJudgesReadinessAtTheDeadlineStepsReading_TIME014_TIME010`, `firingPassNeverStartsAReapableTransitionPastItsLatestBound_TIME013_TIME010` and `decisionToWaitJudgesTheNextBoundaryAtTheCycleReading_TIME010_CONC010`; TypeScript `injectable-clock.test.ts`, "CONC-010 AC3 / TIME-010: a boundary that falls due during the wait setup still gets a timer".
defects.evidenceText: `TIME_014_forbids_passReread` (TIME_014.lean), `TIME_010_cycle_forbids_rereadAtBegin` and `TIME_010_cycle_forbids_rereadAtPark` (TIME_cycle.lean).

defects.title: Java's archive header order changes from one JVM to the next
defects.text: the V2 and V3 header build the tags and the metadata histogram with `Map.copyOf`, whose iteration order is randomised per JVM, and the writer serialises maps in iteration order. The compact constructors of `SessionArchive.V2` and `SessionArchive.V3` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/archive/SessionArchive.java`) and of `SessionMetadata` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/archive/SessionMetadata.java`). The writer makes its own `Map.copyOf` of the tags before the header does (`writeV2` and `writeV3` in `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/archive/SessionArchiveWriter.java`), so every V2 and V3 header the writer writes is affected.
defects.fix: the header tags and the metadata histogram are unmodifiable maps in ascending code-point order of their keys (`CodePointOrder.sortedCopy`), and the writer hands the session's tags to the header without a copy of its own. Java `SessionArchiveV3Test.headerRendersTagsAndHistogramInAscendingKeyOrder_EVT025` and `readBackTagsAndHistogramIterateInAscendingKeyOrder_EVT025`.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_025_mutant_seededTags` (EVT_025.lean).

defects.title: Python archives at most 10,000 events
defects.text: `write_from_store` copies the store into a debug store of the default capacity of 10,000 events before writing, so a larger store is archived without its oldest events. `rust/libpetri-py/src/archive.rs` (`DebugEventStore::new` in `write_from_store`).
defects.fix: the copy is a debug store sized to the snapshot, so no event is evicted before the write. Python `test_archive.py::test_evt_025_archive_keeps_every_event_of_a_store_over_10000`.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_025_forbids_copyThroughBounded` (EVT_025.lean).

defects.title: Python writes archive version 3 only
defects.text: the binding offers `write_from_store`, which always writes version 3, and no `writeV1` or `writeV2`. `rust/libpetri-py/src/archive.rs`.
defects.fix: `SessionArchiveWriter` offers `write_v1` and `write_v2` beside `write_from_store`, which writes version 3; `write_v1` takes no tags, since the version 1 header has none. Python `test_archive.py::test_evt_025_ac1_writes_header_versions_1_2_and_3`.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_025_forbids_v3Only` (EVT_025.lean).

defects.title: Python stamps an empty archive with the wall clock
defects.text: for an empty store `write_from_store` takes the start and end times from `SystemTime::now`, so two archives of the same empty session differ. `rust/libpetri-py/src/archive.rs`.
defects.fix: the start time is the first event's timestamp, or 0 for an empty store, and the end time the last event's, or none for an empty store; the wall clock is not read. Python `test_archive.py::test_evt_025_two_archives_of_one_empty_session_are_identical`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the EVT_025 assumes record it.

defects.title: Java's `transitionEvents` throws on an event with no transition name
defects.text: `transitionEvents` calls `equals` on the transition name of every log message and throws on an engine diagnostic whose name is `null`, which both Java executors emit on an interrupted run. `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/event/EventStore.java`.
defects.fix: `transitionEvents` compares names with `Objects.equals`, so an event with no transition name is skipped and the helper does not throw. Java `EventStoreTest.transitionEventsSkipsAnEventWithNoTransitionName_EVT030_AC2` and `AbstractTerminationReasonTest.interruptedRunEmitsAnEngineWarning_EVT013`, on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_030_mutant_throwsOnNameless` (EVT_030.lean).

defects.title: Java's `computeAt` does not clamp the index
defects.text: `MarkingCache.computeAt` passes the index to `subList` and throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` past the stream length. `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/MarkingCache.java`. The debug protocol handler has the same unclamped `subList` on its fallback path (RD-46).
defects.fix: `computeAt` clamps the index to the stream length after its check for an index of 0 or less. Java `MarkingCacheTest.computeAtBeyondStreamLengthClampsToEnd_EVT032_AC2`.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_032_mutant_noClamp` (EVT_032.lean).

defects.title: A channel merge drops the caller's declared places from the correspondence
defects.text: when a caller transition that carries no correspondence is merged with an instance transition that carries one, the merged transition keeps the instance side's correspondence whole, and a transition that carries a correspondence is never re-read from its arcs.
