The caller's declared places are then no keys, so a later pass that renames one of them (fusion at build, or instantiating the retrofitted net under MOD-014) leaves it unresolved, and the caller's action fails its declared-place check after its inputs were consumed (EXEC-031). `merge_local_name_maps` and `build_local_name_map` (`rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs`), `mergePlaceAlias` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java` and `typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts`). The opposite case, a caller that carries a correspondence merged with an instance transition that carries none, drops the instance side's declared places in the same functions.
defects.fix: a channel merge gives a side that carries no correspondence an identity entry for every place its arcs and output specification name, merges the two sides with identity yielding to non-identity, and drops the result when it is all identity, as the Lean reference `corrMergeVia corrSideFull` does. Rust `mod031_place_resolution.rs` `channel_merge_then_fusion_keeps_caller_declared_place_mod031` and `mod031_identity_roundtrip.rs` `channel_merge_then_fusion_caller_action_fires_mod031`; Java `ChannelCompositionTest.channelMerge_callerWithoutAlias_keepsItsDeclaredPlacesAsKeys_MOD031`, `channelMerge_instanceWithoutAlias_keepsItsDeclaredPlacesAsKeys_MOD031` and `NestedPlaceAliasTest.channelMergeThenFusion_callerResolvesItsDeclaredPlace_MOD031`; TypeScript `compose-action-place-alias.test.ts`, "channel merge then fusion: caller action resolves its declared place (MOD-031 key-set completeness)", and `channel-composition.test.ts`, "channelMerge_callerWithoutAlias_keepsItsDeclaredPlacesAsKeys (MOD-031 key-set completeness)"; Python `test_channel_composition.py::test_caller_declared_place_survives_a_later_renaming_pass`.
defects.evidenceText: `MOD_031_mergeThenPass_undecided` (MOD_031.lean): after the runtimes' merge and one pass the declared place `h` resolves to `h`, which no arc names; after the reference's merge it resolves to `f`.

defects.title: Java's compose token-type check reads one host place per name
defects.text: `compose(SubnetDef)` compares each body place with one host place per name, the one put last into a name-keyed map. When the builder already holds two places of one name with different token types (Java's `Place` equality is structural on name and type) and the last one has the body place's type, Java accepts the call where MOD-025 rejects it. `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java` (`Builder.compose(SubnetDef)`).
defects.fix: the check indexes the host places by name to a list and rejects a body place when any host place of that name has another token type. Java `ComposeDirectTest.composeDirect_placeTokenTypeConflict_withTwoSameNamedHostPlaces_throws_MOD025`.
defects.evidenceText: none; line 4 of MOD-025 (MOD_025.lean) states the rejection, and no theorem models Java's name-keyed map.

defects.title: A fusion set that lists its first member again drops that member
defects.text: the non-canonical members are every member after the first position, so a set with members `[a, b, a]` counts `a` among them. Fusion then drops the declared place `a` (it comes back only through an arc of a rewritten transition), runs the input merge on a transition whose only input arcs are on `a`, and drops `a`'s cluster entry. `build_with_fusion` (`rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs`), `buildWithFusion` and `filterFusedMembership` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java` and `typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts`). The input merge has no visible effect, since CORE-030 already rejects two input arcs on one place; what shows is the dropped standalone `a` and its dropped membership entry. Python was listed at first, but the binding declares no fusion sets (MOD-060), so it has no such call.
defects.fix: the fusion build skips a non-canonical member equal to the canonical member, so `[a, b, a]` keeps the declared place `a` and its entry; `nonCanonical()` itself is unchanged. Rust `fusion.rs` `fuse_repeated_canonical_member_keeps_it_mod061` and `petri_net.rs` `direct_compose_then_fuse_repeated_canonical_keeps_its_entry_mod026`; Java `FusionTest.fuse_repeatedCanonicalMember_keepsIt_MOD061` and `ComposeDirectMembershipTest.directCompose_thenFuseWithRepeatedCanonical_keepsCanonicalEntry_MOD026`; TypeScript `fusion.test.ts`, "fuse_repeatedCanonicalMember_keepsIt (MOD-061 step 3)", and `compose-direct-membership.test.ts`, "directCompose_thenFuseWithRepeatedCanonical_keepsCanonicalEntry (MOD-026 AC5)".
defects.evidenceText: `mod061_dupCanonical_kept` (MOD_061.lean) and `mod026_dupCanonical_kept` (MOD_026.lean): the reference keeps `a` and its entry.

defects.title: Java reports `counterexampleConfirmed` `false` on the name-coloured encoding
defects.text: the check that the initial marking violates the property is gated on a flat answer (`colouredPlan == null`), but the replay that follows has no such gate. On a name-coloured `Violated` the flat decoder finds no `Reachable` fact of the flat arity (the coloured `Reachable` has another shape), the empty decode makes `assessCounterexample` return `Unconfirmed`, and the result is `Violated` with `counterexampleConfirmed` `false`, also when the initial marking violates the property. Rust and TypeScript leave the field absent on this path. The IC3/PDR `Violated` case of `SmtVerifier.pipeline` and `SmtVerifier.assessCounterexample` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java`); `CounterexampleDecoder.decodeStateSet` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/z3/CounterexampleDecoder.java`); Rust `rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs` (`replay_phase` returns `None` when coloured). Confirmed by a run: `JoinRelayTest.fig12c(true)` with `R = 2`, budget `R`, the `FIG12C_CARRIERS` and `PlaceBound(R, 1)` (violated at the initial marking) returns `Violated` on route `SMT` with the name-coloured encoding, an empty trace and `counterexampleConfirmed` `false`. A coloured `Reachable` with the flat arity, which would need one colour slot per coloured place, does not occur on a net the encoding accepts: every ν-join consumes from two coloured places at once, so the encoding has at least two slots.
defects.fix: on the name-coloured encoding the `Violated` answer takes the no-replay branch, reports `Counterexample replay: not applicable (name-coloured encoding, NU-053)` and leaves `counterexampleConfirmed` absent, as Rust and TypeScript do. Java `InitialViolationTraceTest.VER003_AC8_aNameColouredInitialViolationLeavesCounterexampleConfirmedAbsent` and `VER003_AC8_aNameColouredViolationLeavesCounterexampleConfirmedAbsent`.
defects.evidenceText: line 6 of VER-003 (VER_003.lean) asks for `counterexampleConfirmed` not `false` at an initial violation; a decider that answers `some false` there, the reference otherwise, fails the block (checked in the wave W10 mutant run, not kept as a theorem). ν-nets are outside `Reference.TimedNet`, so VER_003.lean has no theorem about the coloured path.

defects.title: Rust ignores a carrier declaration it cannot resolve, outside Route B
defects.text: Rust checks the declared carriers only under EXTENDED and only inside Route B (`rust/libpetri-verification/src/nu_scg_verifier.rs`, `verify_name_scg`, which answers `Unknown` naming the place). An absent carrier is therefore silently ignored in three cases: under BASE; under EXTENDED on a call that does not reach Route B; and under EXTENDED on a bounded quiescence query that does reach it, because the pipeline drops the Route B `Unknown` there and defers to Route A (`defer_to_route_a` in `SmtVerifier::verify_net`, `rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs`), whose `build_plan` skips a carrier it cannot resolve (`rust/libpetri-verification/src/name_coloured_encoder.rs`). The open-net route (`verify_open_net` with a `configure_smt` hook) refuses an unknown mint but ignores an unknown carrier as well, and the doc comments promised more than Rust checked. Java and TypeScript reject the declaration in both modes (`SmtVerifier.carrierPlaces`).
defects.fix: `SmtVerifier::verify` judges the carrier declaration on the caller's net before any rewrite or route and answers `Unknown` with `declared carrier place 'x' not in the net (NU-051)` in both modes; `encode_scripts` panics with the same reason, and `verify_open_net` refuses before either route. Python's `encode_smt_scripts` raises `ValueError` with it. Rust `mint_declarations.rs` `nu_051_an_unknown_carrier_is_refused_in_both_modes_on_every_route`, `nu_051_encode_scripts_panics_for_a_carrier_not_in_the_net` and `nu_051_verify_open_net_answers_unknown_for_a_carrier_not_in_the_net`; Python `test_nu_mint_contract.py::test_nu_051_an_unknown_carrier_is_refused_in_both_modes` and `::test_nu_051_encode_smt_scripts_rejects_a_carrier_not_in_the_net`.
defects.evidenceText: `NU_051_carrier_forbids_routeBOnly` (BASE) and `NU_051_carrier_forbids_routeADeferral` (EXTENDED) in `NU_051_carrier.lean`: the shape Rust ships answers `Proven` on the co-mint net with the mistyped carrier `7`.

defects.title: TypeScript's state-space cache grows on every `Arrivals` query and never hits
defects.text: the enumeration looks the graph up under the caller's net and the closed initial marking (`typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`, `enumerate`), and the marking half of the key names `Place` objects by identity (`typescript/src/verification/state-space-cache.ts`, `resolveStateSpace` and `markingKey`). The `Arrivals` closure makes new arrival-source `Place` objects on every call (`typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`, `applyArrivals`), so every query under `Arrivals` misses, builds, and adds one more entry, and the report does not say that the cache was not used. No verdict is wrong, since the cache never hits there. `Arrivals(0)`, and `Arrivals` with no environment place, do not close the net and hit the cache. Java bypasses the cache under `Arrivals` with a report line; Rust and Python key the fingerprint of the closed net.
defects.fix: the enumeration does not use the cache when the `Arrivals` closure added arrival sources, and writes Java's report line for it; `Arrivals(0)` still uses the cache. TypeScript `state-space-cache.test.ts`, the two tests of "VER-017 AC7" (two `arrivals(k)` queries through one cache each build and carry the line; `arrivals(0)` uses the cache).
defects.evidenceText: none; `VER_017_cache` takes the key as an abstract value (its assumes records the `Arrivals` clause as the key's job).

defects.title: TypeScript hands the selected environment mode to `verify` only when there is an input port
defects.text: `SubnetDef.verify` registers the environment places and the selected mode only when the harness has an environment place (`typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts`). For a subnet with no input or in-out port the configure hook receives a verifier on the verifier default `AlwaysAvailable` (the `_environmentMode` field of `SmtVerifier`, `typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`), not on the selected mode, so a hook that registers an environment place itself runs under the wrong mode. Rust (`run_per_property`, `rust/libpetri-verification/src/harness.rs`) and Java (`SubnetDef.verify`, `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java`) set the mode on every call, and Python rides on Rust.
defects.fix: `SubnetDef.verify` sets the harness environment places and the selected mode on every per-property verifier, whether or not the harness has an environment place. TypeScript `subnet-verify-options.test.ts`, "a hook on a subnet with no input port runs under the selected mode (MOD-051)".
defects.evidenceText: `MOD_051_forbids_modeOnlyWithEnvs` in `MOD_051.lean`: the forwarder without its input port, verified under `Ignore` with a hook that registers `sut/IN`; the TypeScript shape (`mod051ModeOnlyWithEnvs`) proves `TerminatesAtSink` where line 4 requires `Violated`.

defects.title: The Python binding adapter resolves the given name before the correspondence
defects.text: `require_output` and `resolve_lookup_key` first look the given name up in the allowed outputs or in the delivered input or read map, and fall back through `local_name_map` only when that fails (`rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs`). When the given name is itself a place of the call's kind that the correspondence resolves to another place (a port `a` bound to the caller place `b`, and a port `b` bound to `c`), the call answers for the given place, not for the place the correspondence names. Java and TypeScript resolve first; the Rust native context hands the correspondence to native actions.
defects.fix: the adapter resolves the given name through the correspondence first and looks up only the resolved name; its error messages still name the given name. Python `test_subnet_local_names.py::test_correspondence_resolves_before_the_given_name_mod031` (`[input]` and `[read]`) and `::test_output_resolves_before_the_given_name_mod031`.
defects.evidenceText: `MOD_031_ctx_mutant_literalFirst_killed` and `mod031ctx_collision` in `MOD_031.lean`: on the collision example the name-first lookup answers for the wrong place.

defects.title: Java and TypeScript resolve the timeout branch's places a second time
defects.text: the executor deposits the timeout branch through `outputToHarvest` and `forwardToHarvest` with the places the rewritten output specification names, which are already the actual places (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/ExecutorSupport.java`, `produceTimeoutOutputRecursive`; `typescript/src/runtime/executor-support.ts`, `produceTimeoutOutput`). Both methods resolve the place through the correspondence again (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java`; `typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts`). On a collision (port `a` bound to the caller place `b`, port `b` bound to `c`) the timeout token meant for `b` lands on `c`. The `from` side of a `ForwardInput` is resolved twice as well (Java reads it through `TransitionContext.inputTokens`, TypeScript in `forwardToHarvest`), so a timeout can forward a token taken from the wrong input, or fail the firing when the twice-resolved place fails the declared-place check before `action-timed-out` is emitted. Rust deposits the timeout branch on the places as given.
defects.fix: `outputToHarvest` and `forwardToHarvest` take the actual places of the rewritten output spec as given, and Java reads the `from` tokens from the raw input. Java `AbstractNetExecutorEngineTest.OutputTimeoutTests.outTimeout_portCollision_depositsOnTheBoundPlace_MOD031_IO013` and `outTimeout_forwardInput_portCollision_forwardsFromTheBoundPlace_MOD031_IO014`; TypeScript `compose-action-place-alias.test.ts`, "the timeout branch deposits on the bound place under a port-name collision" and "a timeout ForwardInput reads and deposits on the actual places under a collision", on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: `mod031ctx_timeout_resolveTwice` in `MOD_031.lean`.

defects.title: TypeScript blocks without a timer when a boundary falls due during the wait's setup
defects.text: `awaitWork` computes its timer from a fresh clock reading taken inside `millisUntilNextTimedTransition` (`typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts`, `precompiled-net-executor.ts`), later than the cycle reading `cycleNowMs` (taken in `executeLoop`) and after the `await Promise.resolve()` yield. When a boundary has passed by that later reading, the method returns 0. The wait returns early only when no action is in flight (`if (timerMs === 0 && promises.length === 0) return;`); with an action in flight it skips the timer (`if (timerMs > 0)`) and blocks in `Promise.race` over the in-flight completions and the wake-up only. Example: a `Delayed(10)` transition `t` armed at reading 0, an action `u` in flight for an hour, a cycle reading of 9.9 (so `t` is not Ready and nothing fires) and a wait reading of 10.05: the loop blocks with no timer and `t` waits for `u` to return. Rust takes its timer from `cycle_now` (`run_async`, `rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs`), and Java leaves its poll as soon as `nanosUntilNextTimedTransition() <= 0` (`BitmapNetExecutor.java`, `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`); Python rides on Rust. This is the TypeScript half of RD-16's decision to wait.
defects.fix: `awaitWork(cycleNowMs)` hands the cycle reading to `millisUntilNextTimedTransition`, which takes no reading of its own, in both executors; the same change fixes the TypeScript half of RD-16. TypeScript `injectable-clock.test.ts`, "CONC-010 AC3 / TIME-010: a boundary that falls due during the wait setup still gets a timer", on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: `CONC_010_forbids_untimedPark` in `CONC_010.lean`: a park with no timer while `nextBoundary` at the cycle reading is set breaks line 4. At the later reading `t` is Ready, so line 2 would forbid the block as well. `TIME_010_cycle_forbids_rereadAtPark` in `TIME_cycle.lean`: a decision to wait that takes a new reading breaks the TIME-010 companion's line 5.

defects.title: Java and TypeScript read the output collector at admission, not at completion
defects.text: neither runtime detaches the output collector when an action completes normally; only the timeout path detaches it (`detachForTimeout`, `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java`, `typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts`). The output is read when the orchestrator later admits the completion, in `processCompletedTransitions` of `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java` (`flight.context().rawOutput()`; the completion is queued in `fireTransition`), `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`, `typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts` (the `.then` in `fireTransition` detaches nothing) and `precompiled-net-executor.ts`. So a token an action writes after its future or promise completed, from a thread or a timer it started, and before the completion is admitted, is deposited at the commit. Rust moves the outputs into the completion message when the action returns. Java's synchronous paths (`processSyncOutput`) read the output without detaching it too, and `PrecompiledNetExecutor` reused a pooled context per transition, so a write that arrived after admission landed in the next firing of the same transition. The fix is to detach the collector at completion, as the timeout path already does.
defects.fix: both runtimes detach the write target when the action completes (`detachAtCompletion`) and keep what was written as the harvest, so a later write is dropped. Java detaches in the completion callback and on the synchronous path, and its precompiled executor gives every firing a fresh context; TypeScript detaches in the first reaction to the action's promise, also with an action timeout armed. Java `AbstractNetExecutorEngineTest.OutputAtCompletionTests.aWriteAfterCompletionIsNotDeposited_CONC003` and `aLateWriteDoesNotReachTheNextFiring_CONC003`; TypeScript `executor-shared-semantics.test.ts`, "a token written after the action's promise settled is not deposited (CONC-003)", with and without an action timeout, on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: `CONC_003_forbids_lateWrite` (CONC_003.lean).

defects.title: Java's awaitTermination waits out its timeout on a loop that never ran or that died at boot
defects.text: two paths leave `started` true and `terminatedFuture` never completed, so `awaitTermination` gets past `if (!started) return true`, waits out its whole timeout and answers false, on every later call too. (a) A rejected submit. `run(Duration, RunTimeoutPolicy)` sets `started = true` before `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(this::executeLoop, executor)` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java`, `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`). When the executor rejects the task, the call throws `RejectedExecutionException` and the loop never runs. A `close()` before the run does this on an executor that owns its pool, since `close()` shuts the pool down (`BitmapNetExecutor.close`); a caller-supplied executor that rejects the task does it without a close. (b) A store that throws at boot. `executeLoop` emits `ExecutionStarted` and the first marking snapshot before its `try`/`finally` (`BitmapNetExecutor.java`, `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`), and `emitEvent` does not catch (`BitmapNetExecutor.java`, `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`). A store that throws on these appends makes `run()` throw before the `finally` that completes `terminatedFuture`; the loop is gone and `running` stays true. The termination bookkeeping of the `finally` already survives a throwing store; the boot does not. Reproduced against `java/target/classes`: after a rejected `run(Duration)`, and after a `run()` that threw `IllegalStateException` from a store that throws on every append, both executors answer `awaitTermination(300 ms)` with false after 300 ms. TypeScript, Rust and Python provide no `awaitTermination`.
defects.fix: `run(Duration, policy)` restores `started` and rethrows when the submit throws, and `executeLoop` emits its boot events inside the `try`, so a store that throws at boot still reaches the `finally` that completes `terminatedFuture`, with the termination reason `STOPPED`. Java `AbstractNetExecutorEnvironmentTest.LifecycleTests.awaitTermination_trueAtOnceAfterARejectedRun_ENV016` and `awaitTermination_trueAfterABootThatThrew_ENV016_AC1`, on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: none of its own. Case (a) is an answer false on a loop that never started, which line 1 of `ENV_016_await` forbids (`ENV_016_await_mutant_blocksUnstarted` is that answer). Case (b) has no image in the model, which has no step for a loop that dies before its run: read as a loop that stays running, it meets every line, so the defect shows only against AC1 and the quoted throwing-store sentence. The fix is to set `started` only once the submit is accepted, or to complete `terminatedFuture` when the submit fails, and to move the boot emissions inside the `try`.

defects.title: Java's executor builders keep the caller's environment-place set
defects.text: `Builder.environmentPlaces(Set<EnvironmentPlace<?>>)` stores the caller's set (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java`, `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java`), `build()` passes it on and the constructor keeps it without a copy (`this.environmentPlaces = environmentPlaces;` in both constructors). `inject` tests that live set on every call (`environmentPlaces.contains(place)` in both), so a host that changes its own set after `build()` adds or removes a registration in the middle of the run. `hasEnvironmentPlaces` is read once in the constructor, so the quiescence decision of ENV-010 keeps the registration of the build while `inject` and the dead-arc report follow the changed set. The varargs overload copies (`Set.of(places)`) and is not affected. TypeScript copies the names into a set of its own; Rust and Python take the registrations by value. Reproduced against `java/target/classes`: an executor built with the caller's set `{A}` answers an injection into `B` with an error; after the caller removes `A` and adds `B`, an injection into `A` fails and one into `B` is accepted.
defects.fix: both executor constructors keep `Set.copyOf(environmentPlaces)` and compute `hasEnvironmentPlaces` from that copy, so `inject`, the dead-arc report and the quiescence decision read one fixed set. Java `AbstractNetExecutorEnvironmentTest.LifecycleTests.environmentPlacesAreFixedAtBuild_ENV002`, on both executors.
defects.evidenceText: `ENV_002_forbids_shrinks` (ENV_002.lean): an executor whose registrations are removed during the run breaks line 3. A registration added during the run breaks line 1. The fix is `Set.copyOf(places)` in the builder or the constructor.

defects.title: Java's debug protocol renders maps and sets in a per-JVM order
defects.text: `NetEventConverter.toEventInfo` builds the `details` of `NetEventInfo` with `Map.of(...)` of two or more entries (`ExecutionStarted`, `ExecutionCompleted`, `TransitionCompleted`, `TransitionFailed`, `TransitionTimedOut`), and `withInstancePrefix` returns `Map.copyOf(copy)`, so every event of a composed net whose details then hold two or more entries is affected too. `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/NetEventConverter.java`: those five cases of `toEventInfo` and the `Map.copyOf` in `withInstancePrefix`, and through `withInstancePrefix` also the `TransitionStarted`, `ActionTimedOut`, `TokenAdded` and `TokenRemoved` cases. `DebugSessionRegistry.tagsFor` hands `Map.copyOf(session.tags())` to `SessionSummary.tags` (`DebugSessionRegistry.java`), and the `SubnetInstanceInfo` constructor copies its name sets with `Set.copyOf` (`DebugResponse.java`), which drops the `LinkedHashSet` order `buildSubnetInstances` builds for a stable `Subscribed` response (recorded on its own as RD-45). The iteration order of these immutable collections is salted per JVM, `DebugResponse` is a Jackson type, and Jackson writes a map and a set in iteration order (no `ORDER_MAP_ENTRIES_BY_KEYS` is set, and a set is written as an array either way), so one event, session list or subscription renders differently from one JVM to the next. Rust builds the event details as a `BTreeMap` (`rust/libpetri-debug/src/net_event_converter.rs`), and TypeScript as object literals and insertion-ordered sets. Reproduced with JDK 25.0.2: `Map.of` of the three `ExecutionCompleted` keys and `Set.copyOf(List.of("a", "b", "c", "d"))` print in different orders in successive JVMs.
defects.fix: the debug-protocol records normalise their collections where they are built: `NetEventInfo.details` and `SessionSummary.tags` are sorted by code point, as Rust's `BTreeMap` is, `DebugSessionRegistry.tagsFor` returns a sorted copy, and `SubnetInstanceInfo` keeps its build order (RD-45). Java `NetEventConverterTest.detailsRenderInKeyOrder_EVT014_AC5`, `DebugSessionRegistryTest.tagsForIsSortedByKey_EVT025` and `DebugProtocolSubnetTest.subnetInstanceNamesKeepBuildOrder_EVT014_AC5`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the debug protocol has no model. The EVT_025 assumes record it.

defects.title: Java and TypeScript dedup ghost edges by a NUL-joined string
defects.text: `synthesizeGhostEdges` keys the dedup map by the string `x + "\0" + y`, not by the ordered pair. A cluster key may hold the NUL character (it is ASCII, inside EXP-016's name assumption, and no builder checks place names), so the distinct pairs (`a\0b`, `c`) and (`a`, `b\0c`) share the key `a\0b\0c` and the second pair gets no ghost edge. `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/export/ClusterBuilder.java`, `typescript/src/export/cluster-builder.ts`. Rust keys the dedup map by the `(String, String)` pair (`rust/libpetri-export/src/cluster_builder.rs`, ghost synthesis). The fix is a key that cannot collide, such as a nested map or a length-prefixed key.
defects.fix: Java dedups by the ordered pair `List.of(x, y)` and TypeScript by the length-prefixed key `${x.length}:${x}${y}`; neither can collide. Java `ClusterBuilderTest.ghostEdgesDedupByOrderedPair_nulInKeyDoesNotMerge_EXP017`; TypeScript `cluster-builder.test.ts`, "EXP-017: ghost edges dedup by ordered pair".
defects.evidenceText: `EXP_017_forbids_nulDedup` and `exp017_nulNet_counts` (EXP_017.lean): on `exp017NulNet` the reference draws two ghost edges and the NUL-joined dedup draws one.

defects.title: Rust verification checks the mint declaration against its own rewritten net
defects.text:
`SmtVerifier::verify` checks the declared mints (`name_fragment::unknown_mint_reason(self.net, ...)`, `rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs`) inside `verify_net`, after the verifier's own rewrites: the `Arrivals(k)` closure (`with_arrivals`, called from `verify`), the inert places, the in-flight split and the terminal rewrite (`verify_terminals_split`). Those rewrites add transitions such as `complete:` (`completion_transition`, `rust/libpetri-verification/src/in_flight.rs`) and `env:arrive[i]:

` (`close_open_net`, `rust/libpetri-verification/src/open_net/closure.rs`), so a declaration naming one of them is accepted and verification answers a verdict. Every other entry point checks the caller's net and refuses the same request with `declared mint transition 'complete:t' not in the net (NU-010)`: Rust `encode_scripts` (`smt_verifier.rs`, before `with_arrivals`), Python `encode_smt_scripts` (`py_encode_smt_scripts`, `rust/libpetri-py/src/verification.rs`), Java at declaration (`SmtVerifier.mintTransitions`, `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java`) and TypeScript at declaration and in `encodeScripts` (`mintTransitions` and `encodeScripts`, `typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`, both on `callerNet`). Rust's own docs promise the same answer (`encode_scripts` panics "with the reason verify answers Unknown with"; the doc comment of `unknown_mint_reason` in `name_fragment.rs`). The fix is to run the check on the caller's net before `with_arrivals`, as `encode_scripts` does. Open-net verification is not affected: all three runtimes check its declaration on the closed net.
defects.fix: `verify` judges the mint declaration on the caller's net before the `Arrivals` closure and the other rewrites, as `encode_scripts` does, so `complete:t` and `env:arrive[0]:p0` are refused with the NU-010 reason. Rust `mint_declarations.rs` `nu_010_ac6_mint_naming_a_rewrite_added_transition_is_refused`; Python `test_nu_mint_contract.py::test_nu_010_ac6_mint_naming_a_rewrite_added_transition_is_refused`.
defects.evidenceText: `NU_010_unknownMint_forbids_rewrittenNet` (`NU_010_ac6.lean`): an entry point that checks the names against the caller's transitions plus `complete:t` answers `Violated` on `p0 -> t -> p1` with `complete:t` declared, where the reference script encoding fails with the NU-010 reason (`nu010_rewritten_vs_encode`).

defects.title: The Route B environment decline reads the selected mode, not whether conflict priority applies
defects.text: the verifier switches the mode it hands on to `NONE` only when the in-flight split refuses a pruner (Rust `with_in_flight`, Java `applyInFlight` through `conflictOff`, TypeScript `applyInFlight` through `_effectivePriority`). When conflict priority does not apply because a transition of the net is read as reapable, the selected `CONFLICT` reaches the Route B environment check, which declines whenever an environment place under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)` has two or more consumers ("is a consumed input shared under conflict priority"), although Route B itself turns the pruning off on that net (`verify_via_name_scg_reaping`, `NuScgVerifier.verifyReaping`, `verifyViaNameScgReaping`). So on a net with a ν-join, no declared budget, one `Deadline` or `Window` transition (`assumeNoReaping` not set) and an uncoloured environment place two transitions consume, `Unreachable` or `PlaceBound` on a non-environment place answers `Unknown` ("Declined under environment injection") under `CONFLICT` and the Route B verdict under `NONE`. The same check refuses a name-alignment call: under `CONFLICT`, on a net with a reapable transition, a `NameAligned(S)` or `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` call under `AlwaysAvailable` whose uncoloured environment place outside `S` two transitions consume, and that steps 1 to 4 and the first two rules of step 5 let through, answers `Unknown` ("is a consumed input shared under conflict priority") where the refusal order of NU-055 reaches its later rules or builds the graph. Rust: `SmtVerifier::verify_net` (passes `self.priority_semantics` to `route_b_env_observation`) and `route_b_env_observation` (the decline), in `rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs`. Java: `SmtVerifier.pipeline` (passes `effectivePriority()`, still `CONFLICT` unless `conflictOff`) and `routeBEnvObservation` (the decline), in `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java`. TypeScript: `SmtVerifier.runPipeline` (passes `_effectivePriority`) and `routeBEnvObservation` (the decline), in `typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`. The fix is to hand the environment check `CONFLICT` only when conflict priority applies (`conflict_pruning_applies` and the pruning not turned off by the split), `NONE` otherwise.
defects.fix: the Route B environment check gets `CONFLICT` only where conflict pruning applies and `NONE` otherwise, in all three runtimes; where pruning applies the decline still stands. Rust `smt_verifier.rs` `nu_052_env_decline_only_where_conflict_priority_applies`; Java `SmtVerifierTest.envDeclineReadsWhetherConflictPriorityApplies_NU052_VER006_AC8`; TypeScript `smt-verifier.test.ts`, "NU-052 / VER-006 AC8: the env decline applies only where conflict priority is in effect"; Python `test_nu_verification.py::test_nu_052_env_decline_only_where_conflict_priority_applies`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the setup model `NuSetupFn` of `NU_052_split` does not model the environment decline. The `NU_052_split` assumes record it, and the `NU_055_refusal` assumes in `NU_055_steps.lean` (the paragraph on step 5 of the refusal order) record that the gate's conflict fact is "conflict priority is in effect" as NU-052 states it, not the runtimes' reading.

defects.title: Rust and TypeScript dedup state classes by a marking string that does not escape place names
defects.text: both runtimes dedup state classes by a rendered string in which place names are not escaped. Rust renders the marking as `name:count` entries joined by `,` (`MarkingState::canonical_key`, `rust/libpetri-verification/src/marking_state.rs`), the class key appends `|` and `Dbm::zone_key` (`StateClass::canonical_key` in `state_class.rs`; `dbm.rs`, clock names joined by `,`), and `StateClassGraph::build` dedups by that string (in `build_core`, `state_class_graph.rs`). TypeScript renders the marking as `{name:count, ...}` (`MarkingState.toString`, `typescript/src/verification/marking-state.ts`) and dedups by `classKey` = marking string, `|`, zone key (`analysis/state-class-graph.ts`, used in `StateClassGraph.build`). Route B interns the base class by the same strings: Rust `intern_base` (`name_state_class_graph.rs`, `canonical_key` then `#` and the `ready_earliest` bits), TypeScript `internBase` over `baseKeyOf` (`analysis/name-state-class.ts`, `analysis/name-state-class-graph.ts`). Place names are arbitrary strings (`Place::new` checks nothing), so the markings {`a`:1, `b`:1} and {`a:1,b`:1} (TypeScript: {`a:1, b`:1}) get one key. On the net `t1: x -> a, b`, `t2: x -> 'a:1,b'` from {`x`:1}, both successors of the initial class have no clocks, so their class keys are equal: the Rust build reports `complete=true` with 2 classes where the correct graph has 3, the edge (`t2`, 0) points to the class with marking {`a`:1, `b`:1}, and `is_reachable` of {`a:1,b`:1} answers `false`. The TypeScript build also stores 2 classes. A marking that a timed run reaches is then missing from a graph reported closed, which can give an unsound `Proven`; in Route B the first arrival's base class is kept and the second marking is lost the same way. Java keys by structure (`StateClass.equals` over `MarkingState` and the DBM, and the record `BaseKey` in `NameStateClassGraph.java`), so it does not collide. Rust's `reachable_markings` dedups by the same string, and `zone_key` leaves clock names unescaped; TypeScript's counterexample decoder dedups markings by `toString()` too. The fix is a key that cannot collide: key the maps by the structured marking and zone, as Java does, or escape or length-prefix every name in the rendering.
defects.fix: Rust escapes `\`, `,`, `:`, `|` and `#` in place and clock names in `canonical_key` and `zone_key`, so the class key, `reachable_markings` and `intern_base` are injective. TypeScript keys classes, Route B base classes, `StateClass.equals`, `isReachable` and the counterexample decoder by `MarkingState.key()`, the JSON of the sorted entries; the public `StateClassGraph.reachableMarkings()` still returns display strings. Rust `state_class_graph.rs` `ver_010_class_key_does_not_merge_markings_through_place_names`, `marking_state.rs` `ver_010_canonical_key_escapes_separators` and `dbm.rs` `ver_010_zone_key_escapes_clock_names`; TypeScript `state-class-graph.test.ts`, "VER-010: a place named "a:1, b" does not share a class key with {a:1, b:1}" and "VER-012: Route B keeps the marking that renders like the first arrival's". Python runs the Rust verifier and has no test of its own.
defects.evidenceText: `VER_010_key_forbids_markingBlind` (`VER_010.lean`): an identity that gives two classes with different markings and one zone one key breaks `VER_010_key` line 2. The model indexes places by number and has no place names, so the string rendering itself is not modelled.

defects.title: TypeScript gives an unnamed transition of an instance the action of the first transition of its name
defects.text: `Instance.bindActions` binds the renamed body through a resolver that, for a name the mapping does not give, returns the action of the first transition of the renamed body with that name (`typescript/src/core/instance.ts`), and `PetriNet.bindActionsWithResolver` rebuilds a transition whenever the resolver's action differs from its own (`typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts`). No builder and no instantiation checks transition names (ruling D23 assumes them distinct; `renameNet` adds every body transition, `typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts`), so an instance can hold two transitions of one name. Instantiate a body with `x` (action A1), `x` (action A2) and `y` as `p` and call `bindActions({y: B})`: the second `p/x` ends up with A1 instead of A2. With distinct names the first transition of a name is the transition itself and nothing changes. Rust and Python (the resolver returns `None`, so the transition is cloned, `bind_actions_with_resolver` in `rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs`) and Java (the resolver returns `null`, so the action is kept, `Instance.bindActions` in `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java`) keep the transition's own action. The fix is a resolver that returns `null` for a name the mapping does not give, as Java does.
defects.fix: the resolver returns `null` for a name the mapping does not give, so every such transition keeps its own action. TypeScript `instantiate.test.ts`, "MOD-030: a transition the mapping does not name keeps its own action, even with a same-named sibling".
defects.evidenceText: `MOD_030_forbids_firstOfName` (`MOD_030.lean`): the binding that gives an unnamed transition the action of the first transition of its name breaks `MOD_030` line 4 on an instance with two transitions named `p/x`.

defects.title: Java and TypeScript treat the last millisecond of the total budget differently from the clamp
defects.text: both runtimes poll the deadline on a finer clock than the clamp reads it, so when less than one millisecond of the total budget is left the two disagree. Java: `Z3Solver.run` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/z3/Z3Solver.java`) calls `deadline.check()`, which throws only once the nanosecond deadline has passed (`VerificationDeadline.expired`, `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/VerificationDeadline.java`), and then sets `left = Math.max(1, deadline.remainingMs())` with `remainingMs` the remaining nanoseconds divided down to whole milliseconds. With 0 < remaining < 1 ms the whole milliseconds left are 0, yet Java starts a `z3` process with `-t:1`, `-T:2` and a 2001 ms watchdog. TypeScript: `runZ3Text` (`typescript/src/verification/z3/z3-process.ts`) refuses when `Math.floor(deadline.remainingMs()) <= 0` but records no stop, while every poll (`Deadline.check` through `passed()`, `remainingMs() <= 0`, `typescript/src/verification/total-budget.ts`; `enter`, and the `unknown` case of the IC3/PDR query and the certificate check in `runPipeline`, `smt-verifier.ts`) still sees time left. In that window the IC3/PDR query is refused, `runZ3Spacer` turns the rejection into `unknown` with the reason `total verification budget of <N> ms exhausted; z3 not started` (`z3/spacer-runner.ts`), the `check()` of the `unknown` case does not throw, and `verify()` returns that reason without `during IC3/PDR query`. A step that steps aside after a refused call (the state-equation phase, for example) is followed by `enter()` of the next step, which passes, so a step is entered after the refusal. Rust and Python use one whole-millisecond `remaining()` for the entry poll, the polls inside a step and the clamp (`total_budget.rs` `expired_now`, `step`, `cut`, `clamp`), so the clamp refuses exactly when a poll records `Stop::Budget`. The fix is one clock for both: Java should start no process when `remainingMs()` is 0 and record the budget stop there (or poll and clamp on whole milliseconds, as Rust does); TypeScript should record the stop when the clamp refuses, or poll on `Math.floor(remainingMs()) <= 0`.
defects.fix: both runtimes poll on the whole-millisecond clock the clamp reads: Java's `expired()` is `remainingMs() <= 0` and `Z3Solver.run` starts no process with no whole millisecond left, and TypeScript's `passed()` tests `Math.floor(remainingMs()) <= 0`. Java `TotalBudgetTest.subMillisecondRemainderStopsAsTheClampDoes_VER013_AC9` and `StubZ3Test.totalBudget_noProcessStartsWithoutAWholeMillisecondLeft_VER013_AC9`; TypeScript `total-budget.test.ts`, "VER-013 AC9: with less than one whole millisecond left the poll stops as the clamp refuses".
defects.evidenceText: `VER_013_args_forbids_javaSubMs` (`VER_013.lean`): the clamp that raises a remainder of 0 whole milliseconds to 1 ms breaks `VER_013_args` line 6 while lines 4 and 5 hold for it. `VER_013_stop_forbids_refuseUnrecorded` (`VER_013.lean`): a runner whose refused call records no stop breaks `VER_013_stop` line 4, and its `Unknown` keeps the refusal's own reason. The two clocks themselves are not modelled; the model has one stop per poll.

defects.title: Java does not poll the total budget after an unclamped z3 call
defects.text: after the process, `Z3Solver.run` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/z3/Z3Solver.java`) checks only `VerificationDeadline.cancelled()` and `clamped && deadline.expired() && !answered(reply)`. A total budget that runs out during a call whose own timeout was not clamped is therefore not recorded. Concrete run: total budget 10 000 ms, per-call timeout 5 000 ms, and the IC3/PDR query starts with exactly 5 000 ms left, so `left < timeoutMs` is false and the call is not clamped; `z3` overruns `-t` and is stopped by the `-T` backstop at about 6 s. `SpacerRunner.run` returns `Unknown` with the hard-timeout reason, the HORN `Unknown` case of `SmtVerifier.pipeline` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java`) does not poll, and no later `enter()` follows, so `verify()` returns the solver's reason where Rust and TypeScript give `total verification budget of 10000 ms exhausted during IC3/PDR query`. Rust and Python poll after every call (`Z3Solver::run` calls `total_budget::note_if_expired`, which is `cut`), and TypeScript's `unknown` case of the IC3/PDR query polls with `run.deadline?.check()` (in `runPipeline`, `typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts`). The fix is a deadline poll after every call, clamped or not (`deadline.check()` once the reply is in, before it is returned unanswered), as Rust's `note_if_expired` does.
defects.fix: `Z3Solver.run` polls after every reply, clamped or not, and charges a stop to the running step when the reply is not an answer; an answer that arrives after the deadline is returned and the next `enter()` stops the call, as Rust's `note_if_expired` does. Java `StubZ3Test.totalBudget_spentDuringAnUnclampedCallIsChargedToThatStep_VER013`.
defects.evidenceText: `VER_013_stop_forbids_noPostPoll` (`VER_013.lean`): the runner whose solver calls make no poll after the reply breaks `VER_013_stop` line 4 on the IC3/PDR query under a 100 ms budget spent from poll 2 and a solver that answers `unknown`; its finished `Unknown` keeps `the solver answered unknown` where the reference gives the budget reason.

defects.title: Python archive headers carry an empty structure
defects.text: `write_from_store` built the archived debug session with `places: None` (`rust/libpetri-py/src/archive.rs`), so `build_net_structure` returned no places and no transitions (`rust/libpetri-debug/src/debug_session_registry.rs`) and the header's `structure` listed neither, although the writer has the net. The Rust registry fills it (`places: Some(PlaceAnalysis::from_net(net))`, `register_with_tags` in `debug_session_registry.rs`).
defects.fix: the archived session carries `places: Some(PlaceAnalysis::from_net(net))`, so the header's `structure` lists the net's places and transitions. Python `test_archive.py::test_evt_025_archive_header_structure_lists_the_nets_places_and_transitions`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the EVT_025 model keeps the session's header fields, the net structure among them, opaque.

defects.title: Java's `SubnetInstanceInfo` loses the build order of its name sets
defects.text: the `SubnetInstanceInfo` constructor copied its place and transition name sets with `Set.copyOf` (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/DebugResponse.java`), which drops the `LinkedHashSet` order `buildSubnetInstances` builds, so a `Subscribed` response listed the names of a subnet instance in an order salted per JVM. It was found with RD-36, whose text names the same constructor.
defects.fix: the constructor copies each set into an unmodifiable `LinkedHashSet`, which keeps the build order and still rejects `null`. Java `DebugProtocolSubnetTest.subnetInstanceNamesKeepBuildOrder_EVT014_AC5`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the debug protocol has no model.

defects.title: Java's debug protocol handler does not clamp a replay index
defects.text: `DebugProtocolHandler.ClientState.computeStateAt` passes the index to `subList` on its fallback without a subscription (`java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/DebugProtocolHandler.java`), the same unclamped call as RD-22. It was latent: the protocol commands reach that fallback only with an index within the stream.
defects.fix: the call clamps the index with `Math.clamp(targetIndex, 0, events.size())`. It has no test of its own: `ClientState` is private and no protocol command reaches the fallback with an index past the end; `MarkingCacheTest.computeAtBeyondStreamLengthClampsToEnd_EVT032_AC2` covers the clamp of RD-22.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_032_mutant_noClamp` (EVT_032.lean).

defects.title: A reused Java `SmtVerifier` checks the net its previous call rewrote
defects.text: the CORE-043 check before `prepare()` read the mutable `net` field (`pipeline` and `encodeScripts` in `java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java`), which the previous call left rewritten. A second call therefore threw when the first call's rewrite had made a CORE-043 violation, the case of RD-08 (a passthrough sink split under `CONFLICT`), for example on `encodeScripts()` called twice. The read outside the synchronized `prepare()` was also a data race when threads share a verifier.
defects.fix: `pipeline()` and `encodeScripts()` run the check on the caller's net (`callerNet`), with the RD-08 change. Java `SplitDemandTest.CORE043_aReusedVerifierChecksTheCallersNet`.
defects.evidenceText: none; the CORE_043 assumes record it, as for RD-08.

defects.title: No debug protocol handler invalidates its replay cache after an eviction
defects.text: the debug protocol handler kept one marking replay cache per session and reused it after the session's debug event store evicted events. A seek or a step backward after an eviction replayed from a snapshot of events the store no longer held, so it returned a state that is not the replay of the retained events.
defects.fix: the handler invalidates the cache before it computes a state whenever the store's evicted count changed since the cache was last used (Java also compares the first retained event). Java `DebugProtocolHandler.SubscriptionState.computeStateAt`, TypeScript `SubscriptionState.computeStateAt` in `debug-protocol-handler.ts`, Rust `compute_state_at` in `debug_protocol_handler.rs`; Python uses the Rust handler. Tests: Java `DebugProtocolHandlerTest.SeekAndStepFlow.seekAfterEvictionReplaysTheRetainedEvents_EVT032_AC3` and the step-backward twin, the TypeScript and Rust handler tests citing EVT-032.
defects.evidenceText: none; EVT_032 and EVT_032_B state the cache contract and assume a coherent caller.

defects.title: Rust never emits the MarkingSnapshot event
defects.text: Rust declared `NetEvent::MarkingSnapshot` and its consumers read it (debug converter, marking cache, archive metadata), but no executor emitted it.
defects.fix: the shared executor core emits `MarkingSnapshot` right after `ExecutionStarted` and right before `ExecutionCompleted`, on both backends and in `run_sync` and `run_async`, so Python gets it too. The session archive reader now reads an archived snapshot back instead of turning it into a `TransitionEnabled` for an unknown transition. A store that records several runs now holds each run's start snapshot, so a replay resets to that run's marking.
defects.evidenceText: the Rust and Python emission `polRust` (`lean/Libpetri/Reference/Events.lean`) emits both snapshots; the Rust stream then meets EVT-032's run companion (`EVT_032_B_rust`), which reads only the counts.

defects.title: The Rust MarkingSnapshot event carries token counts, not tokens
defects.text: `NetEvent::MarkingSnapshot` holds `BTreeMap<Arc<str>, usize>`, a count per place, so the event cannot carry the tokens.
defects.fix: none yet. Carrying tokens changes the shape of a public enum variant, a breaking change that needs a coordinated major release of the Rust crate and the Python binding.
defects.evidenceText: `EVT_014_forbids_countsOnly`: a snapshot that keeps each place's count and loses its tokens breaks EVT-014, and keeps its order and place-set lines (`evt014_countsOnly_lines34`). No theorem states EVT-014 of the Rust emission `polRust`.

defects.title: The event stores lack the EVT-030 query helpers
defects.text: only the Python binding offered a place filter, offset and limit, and `counters()`; the Rust store also had no filter by event type.
defects.fix: each store gains the helpers with the Python binding's semantics, without an API break. Java: default methods `EventStore.placeEvents`, `filter(predicate, offset, limit)` and `counters()`. TypeScript: free functions `queryEvents` (with `EventQuery`), `placeEvents`, `countEvents`, `counters` and `eventPlaceName`. Rust: `InMemoryEventStore::events_of_type`, `place_events`, `query(&EventQuery)`, `count_of_types` and `counters`, and `NetEvent::event_type`. Tests cite EVT-030 in each language.
defects.evidenceText: none.
